concepts.shortDefinition: A protocol used by card schemes to authenticate online card payments, often by a code or approval in the cardholder's banking app.
concepts.bodyHtml: A protocol used by card schemes to authenticate online card payments, often by a code or approval in the cardholder's banking app. It is the main way card issuers apply strong customer authentication online.

concepts.shortDefinition: The core UCITS diversification limit: a UCITS may invest no more than 10% of its assets in transferable securities or money market instruments of one issuer, and holdings above 5% in single issuers must not together exceed 40% of the fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The core UCITS diversification limit: a UCITS may invest no more than 10% of its assets in transferable securities or money market instruments of one issuer, and holdings above 5% in single issuers must not together exceed 40% of the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: An attack in which a party controlling a majority of a network's mining power (proof of work) or stake (proof of stake) rewrites recent history, for example to double-spend coins or censor transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: An attack in which a party controlling a majority of a network's mining power (proof of work) or stake (proof of stake) rewrites recent history, for example to double-spend coins or censor transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A rouble-backed stablecoin associated with the evasion of sanctions against Russia.
concepts.bodyHtml: A rouble-backed stablecoin associated with the evasion of sanctions against Russia. The EU prohibited all transactions involving it in its 19th sanctions package against Russia, adopted in October 2025.

concepts.shortDefinition: Two ways UCITS using value at risk measure global exposure.
concepts.bodyHtml: Two ways UCITS using value at risk measure global exposure. Absolute VaR limits the fund's VaR to 20% of its net asset value; relative VaR limits it to twice the VaR of an unleveraged reference portfolio.

concepts.shortDefinition: Designs that let user accounts be controlled by smart contract logic rather than a single private key, enabling features such as social recovery, spending limits, batched transactions and paying fees in tokens other than the network's native coin.
concepts.bodyHtml: Designs that let user accounts be controlled by smart contract logic rather than a single private key, enabling features such as social recovery, spending limits, batched transactions and paying fees in tokens other than the network's native coin.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that, with the customer's consent, collects and consolidates information from the customer's payment accounts at one or more banks or other providers, for example to show all balances in one app or to assess creditworthiness.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that, with the customer's consent, collects and consolidates information from the customer's payment accounts at one or more banks or other providers, for example to show all balances in one app or to assess creditworthiness.

concepts.shortDefinition: The bank or other provider that holds a customer's payment account.
concepts.bodyHtml: The bank or other provider that holds a customer's payment account. Under open banking rules it must give authorised third parties secure access to that account through a dedicated interface.

concepts.shortDefinition: Fraud in which a criminal gains control of a customer's account, for example by stealing credentials through phishing or a SIM swap, and uses it to make payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fraud in which a criminal gains control of a customer's account, for example by stealing credentials through phishing or a SIM swap, and uses it to make payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment that moves money directly from the payer's bank account to the payee's, without using a card network, often initiated through open banking payment initiation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment that moves money directly from the payer's bank account to the payee's, without using a card network, often initiated through open banking payment initiation.

concepts.shortDefinition: Categories of investor allowed to invest in products not available to the general public, based on income, assets or experience.
concepts.bodyHtml: Categories of investor allowed to invest in products not available to the general public, based on income, assets or experience. Definitions differ: in the US accredited investors meet income or wealth tests; in the UK certified high net worth and sophisticated investors are exempt from some financial promotion restrictions.

concepts.shortDefinition: Recording income or expenses in the period they relate to, rather than when cash is received or paid.
concepts.bodyHtml: Recording income or expenses in the period they relate to, rather than when cash is received or paid. Funds accrue interest, fees and other costs daily so that the NAV reflects them fairly for investors dealing on each day.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share class that reinvests the income it receives in the fund instead of paying it out, so that the income is reflected in a rising NAV per share.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share class that reinvests the income it receives in the fund instead of paying it out, so that the income is reflected in a rising NAV per share. A distributing share class pays income out to investors as dividends.

concepts.shortDefinition: The bank or payment institution that provides a merchant with the ability to accept card payments and receives the funds on the merchant's behalf.
concepts.bodyHtml: The bank or payment institution that provides a merchant with the ability to accept card payments and receives the funds on the merchant's behalf. Card acquiring is a regulated payment service.

concepts.shortDefinition: An exchange traded fund (ETF) whose manager selects investments rather than tracking an index.
concepts.bodyHtml: An exchange traded fund (ETF) whose manager selects investments rather than tracking an index. In Ireland an ETF may disclose its holdings quarterly rather than daily, which supports active, “semi-transparent” ETFs.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment approach in which the manager selects assets with the aim of outperforming a benchmark or achieving a target outcome, rather than tracking an index.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment approach in which the manager selects assets with the aim of outperforming a benchmark or achieving a target outcome, rather than tracking an index.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service, such as an oracle network or a bridge, that is secured by restaked assets from a restaking protocol.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service, such as an oracle network or a bridge, that is secured by restaked assets from a restaking protocol. Stakers earn extra rewards but can be penalised (slashed) if the service's rules are broken.

concepts.shortDefinition: A public identifier, derived from a public key or a smart contract, to which virtual assets can be sent.
concepts.bodyHtml: A public identifier, derived from a public key or a smart contract, to which virtual assets can be sent. Anyone can see an address's balance and history on a public blockchain, but not who controls it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A scam in which an attacker sends tiny or zero-value transactions from an address that looks like one the victim uses, hoping the victim later copies the fake address from their transaction history and sends funds to it.
concepts.bodyHtml: A scam in which an attacker sends tiny or zero-value transactions from an address that looks like one the victim uses, hoping the victim later copies the fake address from their transaction history and sends funds to it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Checking crypto addresses involved in a transaction against sanctions lists and blockchain analytics data to identify links to sanctioned parties, scams, mixers or other illicit activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Checking crypto addresses involved in a transaction against sanctions lists and blockchain analytics data to identify links to sanctioned parties, scams, mixers or other illicit activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A key, or set of keys, with special powers over a smart contract or protocol, such as to upgrade, pause, mint or change parameters.
concepts.bodyHtml: A key, or set of keys, with special powers over a smart contract or protocol, such as to upgrade, pause, mint or change parameters. Where several keys must sign (for example three of five), the arrangement is a multisig. Whoever holds the admin key effectively controls the protocol, whatever the marketing says.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm that administers a fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm that administers a fund. It keeps or controls the register, admits investors after due diligence, reconciles holdings and corrects errors, and remains responsible even where a distributed ledger or a third party supports record-keeping.

concepts.shortDefinition: A widely used symmetric encryption algorithm, adopted as a US federal standard in 2001.
concepts.bodyHtml: A widely used symmetric encryption algorithm, adopted as a US federal standard in 2001. It protects data at rest and in transit, including stored key material and backups.

concepts.shortDefinition: A breach of an investment restriction or other rule caused by the manager’s own action, such as buying an asset above a limit.
concepts.bodyHtml: A breach of an investment restriction or other rule caused by the manager’s own action, such as buying an asset above a limit. It must be corrected immediately, investigated for its impact and may require compensation to the fund or investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) service of giving personalised recommendations to a client about crypto-asset transactions or services.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) service of giving personalised recommendations to a client about crypto-asset transactions or services. Advisers must assess suitability and staff must have the necessary knowledge and competence.

concepts.shortDefinition: An agent acts on a client's instructions for a fee; a principal trades against the client from its own inventory and earns the spread.
concepts.bodyHtml: An agent acts on a client's instructions for a fee; a principal trades against the client from its own inventory and earns the spread. Crypto firms often act in both capacities, so the capacity on each trade matters for conflicts and client protection.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), the EU's law on artificial intelligence.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), the EU's law on artificial intelligence. It bans certain AI practices, sets requirements for high-risk AI systems, such as those used for creditworthiness assessments, and sets transparency duties for general-purpose AI. Its obligations apply in phases.

concepts.shortDefinition: Software that acts on its own within set limits, for example holding a wallet and paying for services.
concepts.bodyHtml: Software that acts on its own within set limits, for example holding a wallet and paying for services. Good practice treats it like an employee with a signing mandate, with spending caps, oversight and a named owner.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the EU AI Act, the skills, knowledge and understanding that allow providers, deployers and affected persons to use artificial intelligence (AI) systems in an informed way.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the EU AI Act, the skills, knowledge and understanding that allow providers, deployers and affected persons to use artificial intelligence (AI) systems in an informed way. Firms must take measures to ensure sufficient AI literacy of their staff.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) rulebook that sets the conditions for Irish AIFs (retail investor AIFs (RIAIFs) and qualifying investor AIFs (QIAIFs)) and their alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs), supplementing the AIFM Regulations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) rulebook that sets the conditions for Irish AIFs (retail investor AIFs (RIAIFs) and qualifying investor AIFs (QIAIFs)) and their alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs), supplementing the AIFM Regulations. The revised Rulebook, effective 5 May 2026, removed the separate loan-originating QIAIF (L-QIAIF) category, lifted the prohibition on lending and giving guarantees and requires disclosure of at least two liquidity management tools (LMTs).

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2024/927), which amended the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) and the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) from 16 April 2026.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2024/927), which amended the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) and the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) from 16 April 2026. It introduced EU rules on loan origination, harmonised liquidity management tools (LMTs), more reporting on delegation, minimum substance for management companies (ManCos) and wider permitted services; its UCITS amendments are known as UCITS VI.

concepts.shortDefinition: Keeping signing keys on devices that are never connected to a network.
concepts.bodyHtml: Keeping signing keys on devices that are never connected to a network. An air gap is a process rather than a place, and it is broken wherever a transaction, file or image crosses in or out.

concepts.shortDefinition: A free distribution of tokens to wallet addresses, often to reward early users or attract attention.
concepts.bodyHtml: A free distribution of tokens to wallet addresses, often to reward early users or attract attention.

concepts.shortDefinition: Systematic unfairness in a model's outputs, for example against particular groups, often arising from biased training data or design choices.
concepts.bodyHtml: Systematic unfairness in a model's outputs, for example against particular groups, often arising from biased training data or design choices.

concepts.shortDefinition: A coin that tries to hold a peg through code and incentives, usually involving a second token, rather than reserves of real-world assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A coin that tries to hold a peg through code and incentives, usually involving a second token, rather than reserves of real-world assets. TerraUSD is the leading example of failure.

concepts.shortDefinition: A collective investment undertaking that raises capital from several investors to invest it under a defined investment policy for their benefit, and which is not a UCITS.
concepts.bodyHtml: A collective investment undertaking that raises capital from several investors to invest it under a defined investment policy for their benefit, and which is not a UCITS. Its manager is regulated under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD).

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal person whose regular business is managing one or more AIFs, which means at least performing portfolio management or risk management for them.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal person whose regular business is managing one or more AIFs, which means at least performing portfolio management or risk management for them. AIFMs above the size thresholds must be authorised under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD).

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive 2011/61/EU), applying since 22 July 2013, which regulates the managers of AIFs rather than the funds themselves.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive 2011/61/EU), applying since 22 July 2013, which regulates the managers of AIFs rather than the funds themselves. It covers authorisation, capital, organisation, delegation, depositaries, valuation, leverage, disclosure and reporting, and gives authorised alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) a passport to manage EEA AIFs and market them to professional investors across the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: The global trade association for the alternative investment management industry, representing hedge fund, private credit and alternative asset managers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The global trade association for the alternative investment management industry, representing hedge fund, private credit and alternative asset managers. It publishes sound-practice guides and due diligence questionnaires widely used by investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US trading venue for securities run by a registered broker-dealer; some tokenisation platforms operate one alongside their transfer-agency business.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US trading venue for securities run by a registered broker-dealer; some tokenisation platforms operate one alongside their transfer-agency business.

concepts.shortDefinition: The two main models for regulating crypto firms.
concepts.bodyHtml: The two main models for regulating crypto firms. Anti-money laundering (AML) registration (the FATF Recommendation 15 baseline, as in the EU's fifth AML Directive and the UK Money Laundering Regulations) checks owners and anti-money-laundering controls. Activity authorisation (for example the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) in the EU) adds governance, capital, custody and conduct rules for each permitted activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A valuation method under which an instrument is carried at its purchase price adjusted for the steady accrual of any discount or premium up to maturity, rather than at its market price.
concepts.bodyHtml: A valuation method under which an instrument is carried at its purchase price adjusted for the steady accrual of any discount or premium up to maturity, rather than at its market price. Public debt constant net asset value (CNAV) money market funds (MMFs), and low volatility net asset value (LVNAV) MMFs for assets maturing within 75 days, may use it to deal at a constant NAV.

concepts.shortDefinition: Cash and bank deposits that a UCITS may hold on an ancillary basis, for example to meet redemptions, rather than as part of its investment policy.
concepts.bodyHtml: Cash and bank deposits that a UCITS may hold on an ancillary basis, for example to meet redemptions, rather than as part of its investment policy. A feeder UCITS may hold up to 15% of its assets in ancillary liquid assets and financial derivative instruments used only for hedging.

concepts.shortDefinition: The regular reporting that AIFMs must make to their regulator under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), named after the annex of the Level 2 rules that sets out the templates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The regular reporting that AIFMs must make to their regulator under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), named after the annex of the Level 2 rules that sets out the templates. It covers each AIF's main instruments, exposures, concentrations, liquidity, leverage and risk profile.

concepts.shortDefinition: The yearly meeting of a company’s shareholders, at which the accounts are presented, directors are elected and resolutions are voted on.
concepts.bodyHtml: The yearly meeting of a company’s shareholders, at which the accounts are presented, directors are elected and resolutions are voted on. A corporate fund is generally required to hold one, but the directors of an Irish collective asset-management vehicle (ICAV) may dispense with it; a unit trust has no such requirement.

concepts.shortDefinition: The audited report a fund must publish each year, with financial statements, a portfolio statement and a manager's report.
concepts.bodyHtml: The audited report a fund must publish each year, with financial statements, a portfolio statement and a manager's report. UCITS and alternative investment funds (AIFs) must also publish or provide half-yearly or other periodic reports.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto-asset designed to hide the sender, receiver or amount (e.g.
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto-asset designed to hide the sender, receiver or amount (e.g. Monero). Under the EU anti-money laundering (AML) Regulation, regulated firms may not handle them from July 2027.

concepts.shortDefinition: Policies and controls to prevent bribery.
concepts.bodyHtml: Policies and controls to prevent bribery. Under the UK Bribery Act 2010, firms commit an offence if an associated person bribes on their behalf, unless they have adequate procedures.

concepts.shortDefinition: A charge on a subscribing or redeeming investor, paid into the fund to cover the dealing costs caused by the transaction, so that other investors are not diluted.
concepts.bodyHtml: A charge on a subscribing or redeeming investor, paid into the fund to cover the dealing costs caused by the transaction, so that other investors are not diluted. It is an anti-dilution liquidity management tool (LMT).

concepts.shortDefinition: A liquidity management tool (LMT) that passes the dealing costs of subscriptions and redemptions to the investors who trade, to protect remaining investors from dilution: a redemption fee, swing pricing, dual pricing or an anti-dilution levy.
concepts.bodyHtml: A liquidity management tool (LMT) that passes the dealing costs of subscriptions and redemptions to the investors who trade, to protect remaining investors from dilution: a redemption fee, swing pricing, dual pricing or an anti-dilution levy. The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) guidelines recommend that managers select at least one.

concepts.shortDefinition: The laws, systems and controls that prevent the financial system being used to launder the proceeds of crime or to finance terrorism.
concepts.bodyHtml: The laws, systems and controls that prevent the financial system being used to launder the proceeds of crime or to finance terrorism. For funds, AML checks on investors are mainly carried out by the transfer agent (TA) and distributors.

concepts.term: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism
concepts.shortDefinition: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: the laws, systems and controls that stop the financial system being used to launder criminal proceeds or fund terrorism.
concepts.bodyHtml: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: the laws, systems and controls that stop the financial system being used to launder criminal proceeds or fund terrorism.
concepts.sortKey: anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism

concepts.shortDefinition: The new EU authority created to coordinate national anti-money laundering (AML) supervisors and to strengthen the consistency of AML supervision across the EU.
concepts.bodyHtml: The new EU authority created to coordinate national anti-money laundering (AML) supervisors and to strengthen the consistency of AML supervision across the EU.

concepts.shortDefinition: The series of EU directives setting anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) requirements.
concepts.bodyHtml: The series of EU directives setting anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) requirements. The fourth (2015/849, as amended by the fifth) applies until the AML Regulation takes over in July 2027. The sixth (Directive (EU) 2024/1640) covers national supervisors, financial intelligence units and beneficial ownership registers. A separate directive, sometimes also called AMLD6 (2018/1673), harmonises money laundering offences.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1624), which will apply from 10 July 2027 and will replace much of the national anti-money laundering (AML) rulebook, including the rules on beneficial ownership, with a single EU rulebook.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1624), which will apply from 10 July 2027 and will replace much of the national anti-money laundering (AML) rulebook, including the rules on beneficial ownership, with a single EU rulebook.

concepts.term: Anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and countering proliferation financing
concepts.shortDefinition: Anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and countering proliferation financing: anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) extended to cover the financing of weapons of mass destruction.
concepts.bodyHtml: Anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and countering proliferation financing: anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) extended to cover the financing of weapons of mass destruction.
concepts.sortKey: anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and countering proliferation financing

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK rule since 7 October 2024 requiring sending and receiving payment firms to share the cost of reimbursing victims of authorised push payment fraud over Faster Payments and CHAPS, up to £85,000 per claim, with limited exceptions such as gross negligence.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK rule since 7 October 2024 requiring sending and receiving payment firms to share the cost of reimbursing victims of authorised push payment fraud over Faster Payments and CHAPS, up to £85,000 per claim, with limited exceptions such as gross negligence.

concepts.shortDefinition: Application programming interface: a defined way for one piece of software to request data or services from another.
concepts.bodyHtml: Application programming interface: a defined way for one piece of software to request data or services from another. Exchanges, banks and wallets offer APIs so that clients and apps can connect directly; open banking is built on them.

concepts.shortDefinition: A chip designed for one task.
concepts.bodyHtml: A chip designed for one task. In crypto, ASICs are specialised machines for proof-of-work mining, far more efficient than general-purpose computers.

concepts.shortDefinition: In the UK, a firm or person that carries on regulated activities under the responsibility of an authorised principal firm, without its own authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: In the UK, a firm or person that carries on regulated activities under the responsibility of an authorised principal firm, without its own authorisation. The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has tightened principals' oversight duties.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) assessment of a client’s knowledge and experience that a firm must carry out when selling a complex product without advice.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) assessment of a client’s knowledge and experience that a firm must carry out when selling a complex product without advice. The client is warned if the product is not appropriate.

concepts.shortDefinition: A check that a client has the knowledge and experience to understand the risks of a product or service, required for non-advised sales of complex products and for some crypto services under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
concepts.bodyHtml: A check that a client has the knowledge and experience to understand the risks of a product or service, required for non-advised sales of complex products and for some crypto services under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

concepts.shortDefinition: Buying and selling the same or equivalent assets to profit from a price difference between them.
concepts.bodyHtml: Buying and selling the same or equivalent assets to profit from a price difference between them. Authorised participants (APs)’ arbitrage between an exchange traded fund (ETF)’s market price and the value of its assets keeps the two close; some hedge fund strategies seek arbitrage opportunities.

concepts.shortDefinition: Eligible firms buy a stablecoin below par and redeem it with the issuer at par, or mint at par and sell above it.
concepts.bodyHtml: Eligible firms buy a stablecoin below par and redeem it with the issuer at par, or mint at par and sell above it. This arbitrage is what holds the peg for the many holders who cannot redeem directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: The governance token of Arbitrum, a layer 2 network that settles to Ethereum.
concepts.bodyHtml: The governance token of Arbitrum, a layer 2 network that settles to Ethereum. ARB holders vote on changes to the Arbitrum protocol and its treasury.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), a fund that does not promote environmental or social characteristics or have a sustainable investment objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), a fund that does not promote environmental or social characteristics or have a sustainable investment objective. It must still disclose how sustainability risks are integrated into its investment decisions, or why they are not relevant.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), a fund that promotes environmental or social characteristics, provided its investee companies follow good governance practices.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), a fund that promotes environmental or social characteristics, provided its investee companies follow good governance practices. It must provide the standard pre-contractual and periodic templates. The category is a disclosure category, not a label.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), a fund that has sustainable investment as its objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), a fund that has sustainable investment as its objective. It must provide the standard pre-contractual and periodic templates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Computer systems that perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence, such as recognising patterns, generating text or making predictions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Computer systems that perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence, such as recognising patterns, generating text or making predictions. In financial services, AI is used in fraud detection, customer service, investment research and compliance, and is regulated in the EU by the AI Act.

concepts.shortDefinition: The annual review UK authorised fund managers must carry out, and publish, of whether each fund provides value to investors, considering performance, costs, economies of scale, comparable services and share classes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The annual review UK authorised fund managers must carry out, and publish, of whether each fund provides value to investors, considering performance, costs, economies of scale, comparable services and share classes. It sits alongside the Consumer Duty's price and value outcome.

concepts.shortDefinition: Deciding how to divide a portfolio between asset classes, regions and sectors.
concepts.bodyHtml: Deciding how to divide a portfolio between asset classes, regions and sectors. A strategic allocation sets the long-term mix; a tactical allocation adjusts it in the short term to take advantage of market conditions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A group of assets with similar features, such as fixed income, equities, derivatives, real assets and digital assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A group of assets with similar features, such as fixed income, equities, derivatives, real assets and digital assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A sanctions measure that requires everyone subject to the sanctions regime to freeze funds and economic resources belonging to, owned, held or controlled by a designated person, and not to make funds or economic resources available to them, directly or indirectly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A sanctions measure that requires everyone subject to the sanctions regime to freeze funds and economic resources belonging to, owned, held or controlled by a designated person, and not to make funds or economic resources available to them, directly or indirectly.

concepts.shortDefinition: Removing value from a company after acquiring it, for example through large distributions or capital reductions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Removing value from a company after acquiring it, for example through large distributions or capital reductions. The Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) restricts such actions for a period after an AIF acquires control of a non-listed company.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), a crypto-asset that aims to keep a stable value by referencing another value, right or combination, including one or more official currencies, that is not an e-money token.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), a crypto-asset that aims to keep a stable value by referencing another value, right or combination, including one or more official currencies, that is not an e-money token.

concepts.shortDefinition: The total market value of the assets a manager manages on behalf of its funds or clients.
concepts.bodyHtml: The total market value of the assets a manager manages on behalf of its funds or clients. The Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) applies in full only to AIFMs whose AUM exceeds the €100 million or €500 million thresholds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Association of the Luxembourg Fund Industry, the trade body for Luxembourg's investment fund and asset management sector.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Association of the Luxembourg Fund Industry, the trade body for Luxembourg's investment fund and asset management sector. It publishes codes of conduct, including on fund governance, and represents the industry to regulators.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent auditor's report on a service organisation's controls, used by clients to rely on outsourced providers.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent auditor's report on a service organisation's controls, used by clients to rely on outsourced providers. ISAE 3402 and its US equivalent SOC 1 cover controls relevant to financial reporting; the System and Organization Controls 2 (SOC 2) covers security and availability.

concepts.shortDefinition: Delivery versus payment in which the asset and the cash move together in one step, or not at all.
concepts.bodyHtml: Delivery versus payment in which the asset and the cash move together in one step, or not at all. It removes settlement risk but requires the cash leg to be available, and pre-funded, on the same ledger.

concepts.shortDefinition: An exchange of assets on two different blockchains that either completes on both sides or fails on both, using hashed time-locked contracts so neither party has to trust the other.
concepts.bodyHtml: An exchange of assets on two different blockchains that either completes on both sides or fails on both, using hashed time-locked contracts so neither party has to trust the other.

concepts.shortDefinition: (1) A report by an accountant on a stablecoin's reserves at a point in time, narrower than an audit.
concepts.bodyHtml: (1) A report by an accountant on a stablecoin's reserves at a point in time, narrower than an audit. (2) In Ethereum proof of stake, a validator's vote on the state of the chain.

concepts.shortDefinition: Identifying which real-world entity controls blockchain addresses, by grouping addresses likely controlled by the same entity (clustering) and linking clusters to known services or persons.
concepts.bodyHtml: Identifying which real-world entity controls blockchain addresses, by grouping addresses likely controlled by the same entity (clustering) and linking clusters to known services or persons.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent examination of a fund’s financial statements by its external auditor, planned and performed to obtain reasonable assurance that they are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, so that the auditor can give an opinion on them.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent examination of a fund’s financial statements by its external auditor, planned and performed to obtain reasonable assurance that they are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, so that the auditor can give an opinion on them.

concepts.shortDefinition: An expert review of specific code at a point in time.
concepts.bodyHtml: An expert review of specific code at a point in time. It does not cover later changes, the compiler, integrations, economic attacks or key management.

concepts.shortDefinition: A board committee, made up mainly or wholly of independent non-executive directors, that oversees financial reporting, internal controls, internal audit and the relationship with the external auditor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A board committee, made up mainly or wholly of independent non-executive directors, that oversees financial reporting, internal controls, internal audit and the relationship with the external auditor.

concepts.shortDefinition: Australia's corporate, markets, financial services and consumer credit regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Australia's corporate, markets, financial services and consumer credit regulator. It licenses financial services providers, regulates managed investment schemes and oversees markets.

concepts.term: Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre
concepts.shortDefinition: Australia's financial intelligence unit and AML/CTF regulator, which supervises reporting entities, including digital currency exchanges and other virtual asset service providers.
concepts.bodyHtml: Australia's financial intelligence unit and AML/CTF regulator, which supervises reporting entities, including digital currency exchanges and other virtual asset service providers.
concepts.sortKey: australian transaction reports and analysis centre

concepts.shortDefinition: The grant by a regulator of permission for a fund, manager or service provider to operate.
concepts.bodyHtml: The grant by a regulator of permission for a fund, manager or service provider to operate. For a fund it usually follows a review of its documents and of the parties appointed to it, which may result in additional conditions or required changes.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK fund structure in which investors are co-owners of the fund's assets under a contract, rather than shareholders in a company or beneficiaries of a trust.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK fund structure in which investors are co-owners of the fund's assets under a contract, rather than shareholders in a company or beneficiaries of a trust. ACSs are tax transparent, which makes them useful for pooling pension fund assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: In the UK, the firm that manages an authorised fund: the authorised corporate director of an open-ended investment company, or the manager of an authorised unit trust.
concepts.bodyHtml: In the UK, the firm that manages an authorised fund: the authorised corporate director of an open-ended investment company, or the manager of an authorised unit trust. It is responsible for the fund's management and for publishing an annual assessment of value.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank, broker-dealer or other trading firm that has an agreement with an exchange traded fund (ETF) to create and redeem its shares directly with the fund in large blocks (creation units), and so links the primary and secondary markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank, broker-dealer or other trading firm that has an agreement with an exchange traded fund (ETF) to create and redeem its shares directly with the fund in large blocks (creation units), and so links the primary and secondary markets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment institution that holds full authorisation and can passport in the EU, as opposed to a small payment institution that is registered under a lighter regime.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment institution that holds full authorisation and can passport in the EU, as opposed to a small payment institution that is registered under a lighter regime.

concepts.shortDefinition: Authorised push payment fraud: the victim is tricked into authorising a bank payment, often to an account a mule controls, and the funds are then converted to crypto.
concepts.bodyHtml: Authorised push payment fraud: the victim is tricked into authorising a bank payment, often to an account a mule controls, and the funds are then converted to crypto.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK authorised fund set up as a trust, with a manager and a trustee.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK authorised fund set up as a trust, with a manager and a trustee. Units are bought from and sold back to the manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: A system that clears batches of electronic payments between banks, such as the US ACH network or European clearing houses for the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A system that clears batches of electronic payments between banks, such as the US ACH network or European clearing houses for the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract that holds pools of two or more tokens and sets prices by formula, letting users trade against the pool rather than against another person's order.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract that holds pools of two or more tokens and sets prices by formula, letting users trade against the pool rather than against another person's order.

concepts.shortDefinition: A cash machine.
concepts.bodyHtml: A cash machine. In crypto, a crypto ATM or kiosk lets users buy or sell crypto-assets for cash; such machines are a known money laundering and scam risk and are regulated or banned in several countries.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Dutch conduct regulator for financial markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Dutch conduct regulator for financial markets. It supervises asset managers, investment firms, market conduct and crypto-asset service providers in the Netherlands.

concepts.term: Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution
concepts.shortDefinition: France's prudential supervisor and resolution authority for banks and insurers, attached to the Banque de France.
concepts.bodyHtml: France's prudential supervisor and resolution authority for banks and insurers, attached to the Banque de France. It also authorises payment and e-money institutions and supervises anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance in those sectors.
concepts.sortKey: autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution

concepts.shortDefinition: France's financial markets regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: France's financial markets regulator. It authorises asset management companies, approves French funds, supervises market conduct and authorises crypto-asset service providers in France.

concepts.shortDefinition: Retail apps (business-to-consumer), institutional desks and application programming interfaces (APIs) (business-to-business), and crypto services offered under another firm's brand with a crypto service provider behind it (B2B2C).
concepts.bodyHtml: Retail apps (business-to-consumer), institutional desks and application programming interfaces (APIs) (business-to-business), and crypto services offered under another firm's brand with a crypto service provider behind it (B2B2C). In B2B2C models it matters who the end customer is and who performs customer due diligence.

concepts.shortDefinition: Reserves divided by tokens in issue on a reporting date (for example “102% backed”).
concepts.bodyHtml: Reserves divided by tokens in issue on a reporting date (for example “102% backed”). A solvency snapshot — it does not show how fast the reserves turn into cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK payment system for Direct Debits and Bacs Direct Credits, such as salaries, which settle over a three-day cycle.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK payment system for Direct Debits and Bacs Direct Credits, such as salaries, which settle over a three-day cycle.

concepts.shortDefinition: In decentralised finance (DeFi) lending, a loan whose collateral is worth less than the debt and cannot be liquidated in time, leaving the protocol, its lenders or an insurance fund to absorb the loss.
concepts.bodyHtml: In decentralised finance (DeFi) lending, a loan whose collateral is worth less than the debt and cannot be liquidated in time, leaving the protocol, its lenders or an insurance fund to absorb the loss.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests in a mix of asset classes, typically equities and bonds, to provide a combination of capital growth and income.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests in a mix of asset classes, typically equities and bonds, to provide a combination of capital growth and income. Also called a mixed fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Bank for International Settlements, the bank for central banks, based in Basel.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Bank for International Settlements, the bank for central banks, based in Basel. It hosts the Basel Committee, the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI) and the Financial Stability Board (FSB) secretariat and runs the BIS Innovation Hub.

concepts.shortDefinition: A code of 8 or 11 characters that identifies a bank or other institution in international payments, defined by ISO 9362.
concepts.bodyHtml: A code of 8 or 11 characters that identifies a bank or other institution in international payments, defined by ISO 9362.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK's central bank.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK's central bank. It sets monetary policy, oversees financial stability through its Financial Policy Committee, supervises banks and insurers through the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), and regulates systemic payment systems, including any that use stablecoins.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive 2014/59/EU), which gives authorities the tools to deal with failing banks and large investment firms without taxpayer bail-outs, including recovery planning, bail-in of creditors and transferring business to a buyer or bridge bank.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive 2014/59/EU), which gives authorities the tools to deal with failing banks and large investment firms without taxpayer bail-outs, including recovery planning, bail-in of creditors and transferring business to a buyer or bridge bank.

concepts.shortDefinition: The currency in which a fund’s NAV is calculated and its accounts are kept, as stated in its prospectus.
concepts.bodyHtml: The currency in which a fund’s NAV is calculated and its accounts are kept, as stated in its prospectus. Share classes in other currencies may be hedged against movements between it and the class currency.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the global standard setter for bank prudential regulation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the global standard setter for bank prudential regulation. It sets the Basel Framework, including the standard for banks' cryptoasset exposures.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Basel Committee's prudential standard for banks' exposures to cryptoassets, part of the Basel Framework with an implementation date of 1 January 2026.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Basel Committee's prudential standard for banks' exposures to cryptoassets, part of the Basel Framework with an implementation date of 1 January 2026. It sorts cryptoassets into Group 1a (tokenised traditional assets), Group 1b (stablecoins that meet strict criteria) and Group 2 (other cryptoassets, such as unbacked crypto), with Group 2 attracting the highest capital charges.

concepts.shortDefinition: An account with essential payment features that banks must offer to consumers legally resident in the EU, including those without a fixed address, under the Payment Accounts Directive.
concepts.bodyHtml: An account with essential payment features that banks must offer to consumers legally resident in the EU, including those without a fixed address, under the Payment Accounts Directive. The UK has a similar regime.

concepts.shortDefinition: A certificate of ownership of units or shares under which whoever holds the document is the owner.
concepts.bodyHtml: A certificate of ownership of units or shares under which whoever holds the document is the owner. Funds now generally may not issue them, for anti-money laundering (AML) reasons, and use registered holdings instead.

concepts.shortDefinition: Shares owned by whoever physically holds the certificate, without registration.
concepts.bodyHtml: Shares owned by whoever physically holds the certificate, without registration. They have been abolished or immobilised in most jurisdictions because they hide ownership.

concepts.shortDefinition: An index or other reference point against which a fund’s performance is measured, or which a passive fund seeks to track.
concepts.bodyHtml: An index or other reference point against which a fund’s performance is measured, or which a passive fund seeks to track. Benchmarking is the process of comparing a fund’s performance with a comparable index or a group of similar funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation governing the provision of, contribution to and use of financial benchmarks, which funds that track or measure performance against an index must consider.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation governing the provision of, contribution to and use of financial benchmarks, which funds that track or measure performance against an index must consider. Its scope was narrowed from 1 January 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right to enjoy the benefit of property that is legally owned by someone else, such as a trustee or nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right to enjoy the benefit of property that is legally owned by someone else, such as a trustee or nominee. Each unit in a unit trust represents a beneficial interest in the trust’s assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: In property law, the person entitled to the benefit of an asset held by a legal owner (the person registered as owner or in possession of it), such as a trustee or nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: In property law, the person entitled to the benefit of an asset held by a legal owner (the person registered as owner or in possession of it), such as a trustee or nominee. In anti-money laundering (AML) law, the natural person who ultimately owns or controls an entity, for example through more than 25% of its shares or voting rights, and who must be recorded on a central register.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: In crypto, the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a client or wallet. Customer due diligence must look through intermediaries such as trusts, funds and family offices to identify them.

concepts.shortDefinition: A central register of the individuals who ultimately own or control companies and other legal entities.
concepts.bodyHtml: A central register of the individuals who ultimately own or control companies and other legal entities. Following a 2022 EU court judgment, public access in the EU is limited to those with a legitimate interest.

concepts.shortDefinition: Bermuda's integrated financial regulator and monetary authority.
concepts.bodyHtml: Bermuda's integrated financial regulator and monetary authority. It supervises a large international insurance and reinsurance market, banks, investment businesses, funds and digital asset businesses.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU requirement that EU firms make their best efforts to ensure that non-EU entities they own or control do not undermine EU sanctions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU requirement that EU firms make their best efforts to ensure that non-EU entities they own or control do not undermine EU sanctions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The obligation on investment firms, and on crypto-asset service providers executing orders, to take all sufficient steps to obtain the best possible result for clients, taking into account price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, size and nature of the order.
concepts.bodyHtml: The obligation on investment firms, and on crypto-asset service providers executing orders, to take all sufficient steps to obtain the best possible result for clients, taking into account price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, size and nature of the order.

concepts.shortDefinition: The difference between the price at which a market maker or dealer will buy an asset (the bid) and the price at which it will sell it (the offer).
concepts.bodyHtml: The difference between the price at which a market maker or dealer will buy an asset (the bid) and the price at which it will sell it (the offer). It is a cost for investors trading exchange traded fund (ETF) shares and for funds buying and selling assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) for a new type of transaction output that never puts a public key on the blockchain, as protection against future quantum attacks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) for a new type of transaction output that never puts a public key on the blockchain, as protection against future quantum attacks. It is a proposal; using it would require a change to Bitcoin's rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The first blockchain, launched in 2009, and its native coin (BTC).
concepts.bodyHtml: The first blockchain, launched in 2009, and its native coin (BTC). It uses proof of work and has a fixed maximum supply of 21 million coins.

concepts.term: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund
concepts.shortDefinition: BlackRock's tokenised money market fund, launched in March 2024.
concepts.bodyHtml: BlackRock's tokenised money market fund, launched in March 2024. Its shares are issued as tokens on public blockchains and are used as on-chain cash and collateral by institutional investors.
concepts.sortKey: blackrock usd institutional digital liquidity fund

concepts.shortDefinition: Approving a transaction without being able to see or verify what it actually does.
concepts.bodyHtml: Approving a transaction without being able to see or verify what it actually does. Blind signing was a key factor in the February 2025 Bybit hack.

concepts.shortDefinition: A type of temporary data attached to Ethereum blocks since 2024, used mainly by rollups to post transaction data cheaply.
concepts.bodyHtml: A type of temporary data attached to Ethereum blocks since 2024, used mainly by rollups to post transaction data cheaply. Blobs are deleted after around 18 days.

concepts.shortDefinition: A batch of transactions, linked to the previous block by its hash, that is added to the blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: A batch of transactions, linked to the previous block by its hash, that is added to the blockchain.

concepts.shortDefinition: A website that displays the data on a public blockchain: blocks, transactions, addresses and smart contracts.
concepts.bodyHtml: A website that displays the data on a public blockchain: blocks, transactions, addresses and smart contracts.

concepts.shortDefinition: Whoever creates a given block, whether the winning miner or the chosen validator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Whoever creates a given block, whether the winning miner or the chosen validator. The block producer can choose which transactions to include and in what order.

concepts.shortDefinition: The new coins and transaction fees paid to the miner or validator that produces a block.
concepts.bodyHtml: The new coins and transaction fees paid to the miner or validator that produces a block. On Bitcoin the new-coin subsidy halves roughly every four years.

concepts.shortDefinition: A type of distributed ledger technology (DLT) in which transactions are recorded in blocks that are linked cryptographically in a chain, making the record very hard to alter.
concepts.bodyHtml: A type of distributed ledger technology (DLT) in which transactions are recorded in blocks that are linked cryptographically in a chain, making the record very hard to alter. It underlies crypto-assets and many tokenised instruments.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A type of distributed ledger in which records are grouped into blocks, each linked to the one before by a cryptographic hash, so that any change to history is detectable.

concepts.shortDefinition: Tools that group addresses into clusters, attribute them to real-world entities, and score and trace transactions to detect illicit activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Tools that group addresses into clusters, attribute them to real-world entities, and score and trace transactions to detect illicit activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A system that maps human-readable names to blockchain addresses, so users can send funds to a name rather than a long address.
concepts.bodyHtml: A system that maps human-readable names to blockchain addresses, so users can send funds to a name rather than a long address.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain associated with the Binance exchange.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain associated with the Binance exchange. It pays network fees and gives holders discounts and other benefits on the exchange.
concepts.notes: token ticker; the Binance-linked BNB Chain token

concepts.shortDefinition: A committee of the board that looks at a specific area in more depth, such as audit, risk, remuneration or nominations.
concepts.bodyHtml: A committee of the board that looks at a specific area in more depth, such as audit, risk, remuneration or nominations. Larger and significant firms must have some committees by law; the board remains responsible.

concepts.shortDefinition: The shared values, behaviours and norms that shape how a board works in practice: who speaks, how challenge is received, how decisions are reached and how bad news is handled.
concepts.bodyHtml: The shared values, behaviours and norms that shape how a board works in practice: who speaks, how challenge is received, how decisions are reached and how bad news is handled. A board's culture strongly influences the culture of the firm.

concepts.shortDefinition: A periodic review of how well the board, its committees, the chair and individual directors are performing, usually annual, with an independent external review every few years.
concepts.bodyHtml: A periodic review of how well the board, its committees, the chair and individual directors are performing, usually annual, with an independent external review every few years. It should lead to agreed actions that are tracked to completion.

concepts.shortDefinition: The formal record of a board or committee meeting.
concepts.bodyHtml: The formal record of a board or committee meeting. Good minutes record who attended, conflicts declared, the main points of discussion and challenge, the decisions taken and the reasons for them, and the actions agreed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The body that manages and controls a company.
concepts.bodyHtml: The body that manages and controls a company. In a corporate fund it is ultimately responsible for the fund and for acting in investors’ best interests; in an externally managed fund the board of the management company (ManCo) is responsible for day-to-day management and the oversight of delegates. Boards typically meet quarterly.

concepts.shortDefinition: The set of papers circulated to directors before a board meeting: the agenda, minutes of the last meeting, management reports, papers seeking decisions and supporting information.
concepts.bodyHtml: The set of papers circulated to directors before a board meeting: the agenda, minutes of the last meeting, management reports, papers seeking decisions and supporting information. Its quality largely determines the quality of the board's oversight.

concepts.term: Bona fide purchaser for value without notice
concepts.shortDefinition: A person who acquires property in good faith and for value without knowing, or being reasonably expected to know, that it is subject to a security interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person who acquires property in good faith and for value without knowing, or being reasonably expected to know, that it is subject to a security interest. The law gives such a purchaser priority over the secured creditor, who must look to the seller instead.
concepts.sortKey: bona fide purchaser for value without notice

concepts.shortDefinition: A medium- or long-term debt instrument, with a maturity of more than one year when issued, that usually pays a fixed or floating rate of interest (the coupon) and repays the principal at maturity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A medium- or long-term debt instrument, with a maturity of more than one year when issued, that usually pays a fixed or floating rate of interest (the coupon) and repays the principal at maturity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A limit on variable pay as a multiple of fixed pay.
concepts.bodyHtml: A limit on variable pay as a multiple of fixed pay. EU banking rules cap it at 100% of fixed pay, or 200% with shareholder approval, for material risk takers at banks and the largest investment firms. The UK removed its bonus cap in 2023.

concepts.shortDefinition: Taking a loan of cash, for example to buy assets or meet redemptions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Taking a loan of cash, for example to buy assets or meet redemptions. It is a source of leverage; a UCITS may borrow only up to 10% of its net assets and only temporarily, and a fund’s prospectus states its borrowing limits.

concepts.shortDefinition: A protocol that moves value or messages between blockchains, typically by locking assets on one chain and minting a representation on the other.
concepts.bodyHtml: A protocol that moves value or messages between blockchains, typically by locking assets on one chain and minting a representation on the other. Bridges have been among the largest targets of hacks.

concepts.shortDefinition: An intermediary that executes trades on behalf of its clients and charges a fee or commission for each transaction.
concepts.bodyHtml: An intermediary that executes trades on behalf of its clients and charges a fee or commission for each transaction. A dealer, by contrast, trades on its own account; a firm acting in both capacities is a broker-dealer.

concepts.shortDefinition: A programme that rewards people who find and responsibly report vulnerabilities in a protocol's code or systems, rather than exploiting them.
concepts.bodyHtml: A programme that rewards people who find and responsibly report vulnerabilities in a protocol's code or systems, rather than exploiting them.

concepts.shortDefinition: Germany's integrated financial regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Germany's integrated financial regulator. It supervises banks, insurers, asset managers and funds, investment firms, payment and e-money institutions and crypto-asset service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: To permanently remove tokens from circulation, for example when a stablecoin is redeemed.
concepts.bodyHtml: To permanently remove tokens from circulation, for example when a stablecoin is redeemed.

concepts.shortDefinition: Planning and arrangements to keep critical operations running, or restore them quickly, after a disruption such as a system failure, cyber attack or loss of premises.
concepts.bodyHtml: Planning and arrangements to keep critical operations running, or restore them quickly, after a disruption such as a system failure, cyber attack or loss of premises. Operational resilience builds on it by focusing on the services clients rely on.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US closed-end fund that invests mainly in small and mid-sized private companies, usually through loans.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US closed-end fund that invests mainly in small and mid-sized private companies, usually through loans. It must distribute most of its income to keep pass-through tax treatment, and may be listed or unlisted.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm's documented assessment of its own money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks, as required by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 1.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm's documented assessment of its own money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks, as required by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 1. For a crypto firm it should map risks to each activity, product, customer type and blockchain it supports, using real exposure data.

concepts.shortDefinition: Business-to-business (B2B) services are sold to other firms; business-to-consumer (B2C) services are sold to individuals.
concepts.bodyHtml: Business-to-business (B2B) services are sold to other firms; business-to-consumer (B2C) services are sold to individuals. Regulators distinguish them because consumer protection rules apply mainly to B2C business.

concepts.shortDefinition: Short-term credit at the point of sale that lets customers spread a purchase over instalments, often interest-free.
concepts.bodyHtml: Short-term credit at the point of sale that lets customers spread a purchase over instalments, often interest-free. The EU's revised Consumer Credit Directive brings most BNPL into scope, and the UK is regulating it from July 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ability of a distributed system to keep reaching agreement even when some participants fail or act dishonestly.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ability of a distributed system to keep reaching agreement even when some participants fail or act dishonestly. Many proof-of-stake consensus protocols are Byzantine fault tolerant up to a set share of faulty validators, typically one-third.

concepts.shortDefinition: A request by the manager of a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, for investors to pay in part of their capital commitment so that it can make an investment.
concepts.bodyHtml: A request by the manager of a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, for investors to pay in part of their capital commitment so that it can make an investment. Also called a drawdown.

concepts.shortDefinition: The amount an investor agrees to provide to a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, which the manager draws down over time through capital calls (drawdowns) as investments are made.
concepts.bodyHtml: The amount an investor agrees to provide to a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, which the manager draws down over time through capital calls (drawdowns) as investments are made.

concepts.shortDefinition: Government limits on the flow of capital into or out of a country, such as transaction taxes, exchange controls or restrictions on repatriating the proceeds of investments.
concepts.bodyHtml: Government limits on the flow of capital into or out of a country, such as transaction taxes, exchange controls or restrictions on repatriating the proceeds of investments. They can prevent a fund investing in a market or make it expensive.

concepts.shortDefinition: A promise that an investor will get back at least the capital invested.
concepts.bodyHtml: A promise that an investor will get back at least the capital invested. Investment funds generally do not provide one; some structured funds provide capital protection through a derivative or other instrument, at a cost to the fund and indirectly the investor.

concepts.shortDefinition: Saudi Arabia's capital markets regulator, which oversees the Saudi Exchange, issuers, capital market institutions and investment funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: Saudi Arabia's capital markets regulator, which oversees the Saudi Exchange, issuers, capital market institutions and investment funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The federal regulator of capital markets in the United Arab Emirates, formerly the Securities and Commodities Authority (strong customer authentication (SCA)).
concepts.bodyHtml: The federal regulator of capital markets in the United Arab Emirates, formerly the Securities and Commodities Authority (strong customer authentication (SCA)). It was reconstituted under federal decree-laws in force from 1 January 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive 2013/36/EU), which sits alongside the Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR) and covers the authorisation of banks, supervision, governance, remuneration and capital buffers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive 2013/36/EU), which sits alongside the Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR) and covers the authorisation of banks, supervision, governance, remuneration and capital buffers. The sixth version (CRD VI) adds rules on third-country branches and on the fitness and propriety of bank managers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 575/2013), which sets the prudential requirements for banks, including capital, liquidity, leverage and large exposures, implementing the Basel standards in the EU.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 575/2013), which sets the prudential requirements for banks, including capital, liquidity, leverage and large exposures, implementing the Basel standards in the EU. Since 2025 it includes transitional rules for banks' crypto-asset exposures.

concepts.shortDefinition: The bank or e-money institution that issues a payment card to the cardholder, holds the related account and approves or declines transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The bank or e-money institution that issues a payment card to the cardholder, holds the related account and approves or declines transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The network, such as Visa or Mastercard, that sets the rules for card payments and routes authorisation, clearing and settlement messages between issuers and acquirers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The network, such as Visa or Mastercard, that sets the rules for card payments and routes authorisation, clearing and settlement messages between issuers and acquirers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A card payment made without the card being physically presented, such as online or by phone.
concepts.bodyHtml: A card payment made without the card being physically presented, such as online or by phone. CNP transactions carry higher fraud risk and require strong customer authentication in the EU and UK, subject to exemptions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native token of the Cardano blockchain, a proof-of-stake network.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native token of the Cardano blockchain, a proof-of-stake network. ADA pays transaction fees and is staked to help secure the network.

concepts.shortDefinition: The share of a private equity fund’s profits paid to the manager, usually only after investors have received a minimum return (the hurdle).
concepts.bodyHtml: The share of a private equity fund’s profits paid to the manager, usually only after investors have received a minimum return (the hurdle).

concepts.shortDefinition: The payment side of a token trade or subscription.
concepts.bodyHtml: The payment side of a token trade or subscription. It may be commercial bank money, tokenised deposits, a regulated stablecoin or wholesale central bank money. Settlement of a tokenised asset is only as safe as its cash leg.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund depositary’s duty to check that investors’ subscription monies are received and that all of a fund’s cash is booked in properly established cash accounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund depositary’s duty to check that investors’ subscription monies are received and that all of a fund’s cash is booked in properly established cash accounts. It was harmonised for AIFs by the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) and for UCITS by UCITS V.

concepts.shortDefinition: A stage in a private fund's distribution waterfall, after investors receive their preferred return, in which the manager receives most or all distributions until it has received its agreed share of total profits.
concepts.bodyHtml: A stage in a private fund's distribution waterfall, after investors receive their preferred return, in which the manager receives most or all distributions until it has received its agreed share of total profits.

concepts.shortDefinition: The financial services regulator and central bank-type authority of the Cayman Islands.
concepts.bodyHtml: The financial services regulator and central bank-type authority of the Cayman Islands. It registers and supervises investment funds (under the Mutual Funds Act and Private Funds Act), banks, insurers, securities businesses and virtual asset service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The property that no single party can prevent valid transactions from being included in the blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: The property that no single party can prevent valid transactions from being included in the blockchain. Concerns have arisen where block builders exclude transactions involving sanctioned addresses.

concepts.shortDefinition: Central bank digital currency: a direct claim on a central bank.
concepts.bodyHtml: Central bank digital currency: a direct claim on a central bank. Retail CBDCs are for the public; wholesale CBDCs for settlement between financial institutions.

concepts.shortDefinition: Ireland's central bank and single financial regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Ireland's central bank and single financial regulator. It authorises and supervises Irish funds, fund management companies, banks, insurers, investment firms, payment and e-money institutions and crypto-asset service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The central bank of the United Arab Emirates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The central bank of the United Arab Emirates. It regulates banks, insurers, finance companies, exchange houses and payment service providers onshore, including dirham-backed payment tokens.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity that places itself between the buyer and seller of a trade, becoming the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, so that each party is exposed to the CCP rather than to the other.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity that places itself between the buyer and seller of a trade, becoming the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, so that each party is exposed to the CCP rather than to the other. The European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) requires many over the counter (OTC) derivatives to be cleared through a CCP.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 909/2014), which regulates central securities depositories and sets rules on securities settlement, including penalties for settlement failures.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 909/2014), which regulates central securities depositories and sets rules on securities settlement, including penalties for settlement failures. The EU is moving to a T+1 settlement cycle from October 2027.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity that operates a securities settlement system and records securities in book-entry form, usually for a national market.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity that operates a securities settlement system and records securities in book-entry form, usually for a national market. Where a CSD acts as issuer CSD for securities a fund holds, this is not treated as delegation of the fund depositary’s custody functions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A trading platform run by a company that holds customers' assets and matches orders on its own internal ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: A trading platform run by a company that holds customers' assets and matches orders on its own internal ledger.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transferable receipt issued by a bank for a deposit of funds for a fixed term.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transferable receipt issued by a bank for a deposit of funds for a fixed term. The bank pays the principal plus interest to the holder at maturity; CDs are money market instruments.

concepts.shortDefinition: When a blockchain node replaces some recent blocks with an alternative chain that has become the valid one under the consensus rules, reversing transactions in the replaced blocks.
concepts.bodyHtml: When a blockchain node replaces some recent blocks with an alternative chain that has become the valid one under the consensus rules, reversing transactions in the replaced blocks. It is why exchanges wait for several confirmations before crediting deposits.

concepts.shortDefinition: Moving funds quickly across several blockchains and tokens, often through bridges or swap services, to break the transaction trail.
concepts.bodyHtml: Moving funds quickly across several blockchains and tokens, often through bridges or swap services, to break the transaction trail. Single-chain analytics can miss it; cross-chain tracing is needed to follow the funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The token of Chainlink, a decentralised oracle network that brings price data and other off-chain information onto blockchains for use by smart contracts.
concepts.bodyHtml: The token of Chainlink, a decentralised oracle network that brings price data and other off-chain information onto blockchains for use by smart contracts.

concepts.shortDefinition: The director who leads the board and is responsible for its effectiveness: setting the agenda, making sure directors get good information, leading discussion so that all directors contribute, and holding the chief executive officer (CEO) to account.
concepts.bodyHtml: The director who leads the board and is responsible for its effectiveness: setting the agenda, making sure directors get good information, leading discussion so that all directors contribute, and holding the chief executive officer (CEO) to account.

concepts.shortDefinition: Acquiring or increasing a holding in a regulated firm above set thresholds, usually starting at 10% of capital or voting rights, which needs the regulator's prior approval.
concepts.bodyHtml: Acquiring or increasing a holding in a regulated firm above set thresholds, usually starting at 10% of capital or voting rights, which needs the regulator's prior approval. The acquirer is assessed for reputation, financial soundness and anti-money laundering (AML) risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK's high-value, same-day sterling payment system, operated by the Bank of England and settled in central bank money.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK's high-value, same-day sterling payment system, operated by the Bank of England and settled in central bank money.

concepts.shortDefinition: A security interest over an asset, usually created by a company, that gives the creditor a right to be paid out of the asset without transferring ownership.
concepts.bodyHtml: A security interest over an asset, usually created by a company, that gives the creditor a right to be paid out of the asset without transferring ownership. It may be fixed or floating.

concepts.shortDefinition: A reversal of a card transaction initiated by the card issuer at the cardholder's request, for example because of fraud or goods not received, under the card scheme's rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: A reversal of a card transaction initiated by the card issuer at the cardholder's request, for example because of fraud or goods not received, under the card scheme's rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The senior person responsible for the compliance function, which monitors and advises on compliance with regulatory requirements and reports to management and the board.
concepts.bodyHtml: The senior person responsible for the compliance function, which monitors and advises on compliance with regulatory requirements and reports to management and the board.

concepts.shortDefinition: The most senior executive of a company, responsible for running the business day to day and accountable to the board.
concepts.bodyHtml: The most senior executive of a company, responsible for running the business day to day and accountable to the board.
