concepts.shortDefinition: The senior executive responsible for the risk management function, providing an independent view of risks to the board.
concepts.bodyHtml: The senior executive responsible for the risk management function, providing an independent view of risks to the board. In larger firms the role is independent of business lines and has direct access to the board or risk committee.

concepts.shortDefinition: A euro-denominated stablecoin issued by Circle.
concepts.bodyHtml: A euro-denominated stablecoin issued by Circle. It is issued as an e-money token under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), backed by euro reserves and redeemable at par.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US dollar stablecoin issued by Circle, backed by cash and short-dated US government securities and redeemable at par.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US dollar stablecoin issued by Circle, backed by cash and short-dated US government securities and redeemable at par. It is one of the largest stablecoins and is issued in the EU as an e-money token under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

concepts.shortDefinition: A mechanism that pauses trading or a protocol function when prices or volumes move beyond set limits, to prevent disorderly markets or exploits.
concepts.bodyHtml: A mechanism that pauses trading or a protocol function when prices or volumes move beyond set limits, to prevent disorderly markets or exploits.

concepts.shortDefinition: The number of tokens currently available to trade.
concepts.bodyHtml: The number of tokens currently available to trade. Total supply includes tokens issued but locked; maximum supply is the most that can ever exist, if capped.

concepts.shortDefinition: A court action against property rather than a person, to forfeit assets traced to crime.
concepts.bodyHtml: A court action against property rather than a person, to forfeit assets traced to crime. An example is the June 2025 US Department of Justice complaint seeking forfeiture of more than US$225 million in tether US dollar stablecoin (USDT). A complaint states allegations, not findings.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal system based on a comprehensive written code of rules, much less dependent on precedent, as in Luxembourg and most of continental Europe.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal system based on a comprehensive written code of rules, much less dependent on precedent, as in Luxembourg and most of continental Europe. It generally does not recognise the trust.

concepts.shortDefinition: Recovering variable pay that has already been paid, for example after misconduct or material errors come to light.
concepts.bodyHtml: Recovering variable pay that has already been paid, for example after misconduct or material errors come to light. It applies for set periods after payment.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share class whose management fee does not include commission payable to distributors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share class whose management fee does not include commission payable to distributors. A bundled share class, by contrast, includes that commission in the management fee. Clean classes are needed where commission is banned.

concepts.shortDefinition: The signing device shows the transaction in readable form (destination, asset, amount), so the signer can verify it independently of a web screen.
concepts.bodyHtml: The signing device shows the transaction in readable form (destination, asset, amount), so the signer can verify it independently of a web screen.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process between trading and settlement in which obligations are confirmed and, where a central counterparty (CCP) is used, the CCP becomes the counterparty to both sides.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process between trading and settlement in which obligations are confirmed and, where a central counterparty (CCP) is used, the CCP becomes the counterparty to both sides. The European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) requires certain over the counter (OTC) derivatives to be centrally cleared.

concepts.shortDefinition: An account designated as holding money or assets belonging to clients, such as a fund or its investors, rather than the account holder.
concepts.bodyHtml: An account designated as holding money or assets belonging to clients, such as a fund or its investors, rather than the account holder. The bank cannot then set off the balance against the account holder’s own debts.

concepts.shortDefinition: The part of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Handbook that sets the rules for how firms protect client money and assets, including segregation, reconciliation and record keeping.
concepts.bodyHtml: The part of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Handbook that sets the rules for how firms protect client money and assets, including segregation, reconciliation and record keeping. Specific chapters cover safeguarding by payment and e-money firms and cryptoasset custody.

concepts.shortDefinition: Classifying clients as retail clients, professional clients or eligible counterparties under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), which determines how much protection they receive.
concepts.bodyHtml: Classifying clients as retail clients, professional clients or eligible counterparties under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), which determines how much protection they receive. Some retail clients can opt up to professional status if they meet set criteria.

concepts.shortDefinition: Money a regulated investment firm receives or holds for clients, which must be protected, for example by holding it in segregated trust accounts, so it is returned to clients if the firm fails.
concepts.bodyHtml: Money a regulated investment firm receives or holds for clients, which must be protected, for example by holding it in segregated trust accounts, so it is returned to clients if the firm fails.

concepts.shortDefinition: An annual report by an auditor on a firm's compliance with client money and asset rules, which UK firms must submit to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
concepts.bodyHtml: An annual report by an auditor on a firm's compliance with client money and asset rules, which UK firms must submit to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

concepts.shortDefinition: The financial risks from climate change: physical risks from more frequent or severe weather and long-term shifts, and transition risks from policy, technology and market changes as economies decarbonise.
concepts.bodyHtml: The financial risks from climate change: physical risks from more frequent or severe weather and long-term shifts, and transition risks from policy, technology and market changes as economies decarbonise.

concepts.shortDefinition: The exclusions applying to EU Climate Transition Benchmarks – broadly, companies involved in controversial weapons or tobacco and companies violating international norms – which a fund using transition, social or governance terms in its name must apply under the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)’s fund names guidelines).
concepts.bodyHtml: The exclusions applying to EU Climate Transition Benchmarks – broadly, companies involved in controversial weapons or tobacco and companies violating international norms – which a fund using transition, social or governance terms in its name must apply under the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)’s fund names guidelines).

concepts.shortDefinition: Relationships between a regulated firm and other persons through control or a 20% or more holding.
concepts.bodyHtml: Relationships between a regulated firm and other persons through control or a 20% or more holding. Regulators must be satisfied that close links do not prevent effective supervision.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that issues units or shares at launch and does not redeem them on demand.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that issues units or shares at launch and does not redeem them on demand. Investors exit by selling to another investor or when the fund is terminated. Many private equity, private credit and real estate funds are closed-ended.

concepts.shortDefinition: Using computing resources provided over the internet by a cloud service provider.
concepts.bodyHtml: Using computing resources provided over the internet by a cloud service provider. Use of cloud for critical functions is subject to outsourcing and information and communication technology (ICT) third-party risk rules, such as the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).

concepts.shortDefinition: A group of addresses believed to be controlled by the same entity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A group of addresses believed to be controlled by the same entity.

concepts.shortDefinition: Grouping addresses likely to be controlled by one entity, using heuristics such as common-input ownership and change detection.
concepts.bodyHtml: Grouping addresses likely to be controlled by one entity, using heuristics such as common-input ownership and change detection. An inference, not proof; CoinJoin is designed to defeat it.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment made alongside a private fund directly into a portfolio company, usually offered to selected investors with low or no fees.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment made alongside a private fund directly into a portfolio company, usually offered to selected investors with low or no fees. It raises conflicts over allocation and the sharing of expenses.

concepts.shortDefinition: A technique in which many users combine their bitcoin transactions into one, making it harder to tell which input paid which output.
concepts.bodyHtml: A technique in which many users combine their bitcoin transactions into one, making it harder to tell which input paid which output.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are generated and kept offline, away from the internet, to protect against remote attack, and used only in controlled, witnessed procedures.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are generated and kept offline, away from the internet, to protect against remote attack, and used only in controlled, witnessed procedures. Custodians typically hold most client assets in cold storage; Hong Kong requires 98% and Japan 95%. Withdrawals are slow by design.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assets provided to secure an obligation, for example in derivatives, securities lending and repo transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assets provided to secure an obligation, for example in derivatives, securities lending and repo transactions. It may be provided by title transfer, where full ownership passes to the receiver, or by a security interest, where the provider keeps ownership but grants a pledge or charge. Collateral over cash and financial instruments benefits from reduced formalities under the Financial Collateral Directive.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Assets pledged to secure a loan or position, which can be sold (liquidated) if their value falls below a threshold.

concepts.shortDefinition: The processes for taking, valuing, holding and returning collateral to reduce counterparty risk, including eligibility criteria, haircuts, margin calls, diversification and reinvestment limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The processes for taking, valuing, holding and returning collateral to reduce counterparty risk, including eligibility criteria, haircuts, margin calls, diversification and reinvestment limits.

concepts.shortDefinition: The value of collateral divided by the value of the loan or tokens it backs.
concepts.bodyHtml: The value of collateral divided by the value of the loan or tokens it backs. Over-collateralised decentralised finance (DeFi) loans and stablecoins require ratios above 100%.

concepts.shortDefinition: A collective investment scheme: an arrangement that pools money from many investors and invests it on their behalf, such as a unit trust, open-ended investment company (OEIC), UCITS or alternative investment fund (AIF).
concepts.bodyHtml: A collective investment scheme: an arrangement that pools money from many investors and invests it on their behalf, such as a unit trust, open-ended investment company (OEIC), UCITS or alternative investment fund (AIF). The term is used in UK law and in the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) standards.

concepts.shortDefinition: The regulated activity of managing a UCITS or AIF, including investment management, administration and marketing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The regulated activity of managing a UCITS or AIF, including investment management, administration and marketing. Only authorised management companies and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) may carry it on.

concepts.term: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores
concepts.shortDefinition: Spain's securities markets regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Spain's securities markets regulator. It authorises Spanish funds and their managers, supervises investment firms and markets, and authorises crypto-asset service providers in Spain.
concepts.sortKey: comisión nacional del mercado de valores

concepts.term: Comissão do Mercado de Valores Mobiliários
concepts.shortDefinition: Portugal's securities markets regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Portugal's securities markets regulator. It supervises investment funds and their managers, investment firms and market conduct.
concepts.sortKey: comissão do mercado de valores mobiliários

concepts.shortDefinition: An exclusion from payment regulation for commercial agents authorised to negotiate or conclude sales on behalf of only the payer or only the payee.
concepts.bodyHtml: An exclusion from payment regulation for commercial agents authorised to negotiate or conclude sales on behalf of only the payer or only the payee. Marketplaces that act for both sides generally cannot use it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Money held as deposits at commercial banks, which is a claim on the bank rather than on the central bank.
concepts.bodyHtml: Money held as deposits at commercial banks, which is a claim on the bank rather than on the central bank. Most money used for payments is commercial bank money.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short-term unsecured debt instrument issued by companies, normally sold at a discount (like a zero-coupon bond) with a maturity of less than 365 days.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short-term unsecured debt instrument issued by companies, normally sold at a discount (like a zero-coupon bond) with a maturity of less than 365 days. It is a money market instrument.

concepts.shortDefinition: Client assets mixed with a firm's own in the same wallet or account.
concepts.bodyHtml: Client assets mixed with a firm's own in the same wallet or account. Commingling blurs ownership and puts client assets at risk if the firm becomes insolvent.

concepts.shortDefinition: Luxembourg's insurance and reinsurance supervisor, which also supervises Luxembourg pension funds and insurance intermediaries.
concepts.bodyHtml: Luxembourg's insurance and reinsurance supervisor, which also supervises Luxembourg pension funds and insurance intermediaries.

concepts.term: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier
concepts.shortDefinition: Luxembourg's financial regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Luxembourg's financial regulator. It supervises Luxembourg investment funds and their managers, banks, investment firms, payment and e-money institutions and crypto-asset service providers.
concepts.sortKey: commission de surveillance du secteur financier

concepts.term: Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa
concepts.shortDefinition: Italy's securities markets regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Italy's securities markets regulator. It supervises investment services, market conduct, listed companies and prospectuses, and with the Banca d'Italia authorises crypto-asset service providers in Italy.
concepts.sortKey: commissione nazionale per le società e la borsa

concepts.shortDefinition: A method of measuring the global exposure or leverage of a fund by converting each derivative position into the market value of the equivalent position in the underlying assets, allowing for netting and hedging.
concepts.bodyHtml: A method of measuring the global exposure or leverage of a fund by converting each derivative position into the market value of the equivalent position in the underlying assets, allowing for netting and hedging. A UCITS using it may not have exposure from derivatives exceeding 100% of NAV.

concepts.term: Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures
concepts.shortDefinition: The Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures, hosted by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
concepts.bodyHtml: The Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures, hosted by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS). It sets global standards for payment, clearing and settlement systems, including the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures with the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO).
concepts.sortKey: committee on payments and market infrastructures

concepts.shortDefinition: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the US regulator of futures, options and swaps markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the US regulator of futures, options and swaps markets. It treats bitcoin and some other crypto-assets as commodities and polices crypto derivatives markets.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Irish contractual fund, constituted by a deed of constitution between the management company (ManCo) and the fund depositary.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Irish contractual fund, constituted by a deed of constitution between the management company (ManCo) and the fund depositary. It is tax-transparent and its units may not be held by individuals, so it is used for institutional pooling, for example of a multinational group’s pension assets. It may be a UCITS or an alternative investment fund (AIF).

concepts.term: Common Framework for the Supervision of Internationally Active Insurance Groups
concepts.shortDefinition: The International Association of Insurance Supervisors (IAIS) standards for supervising large, internationally active insurance groups, including group-wide governance, risk management and the Insurance Capital Standard.
concepts.bodyHtml: The International Association of Insurance Supervisors (IAIS) standards for supervising large, internationally active insurance groups, including group-wide governance, risk management and the Insurance Capital Standard.
concepts.sortKey: common framework for the supervision of internationally active insurance groups

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal system based on practice and precedent, in which earlier court decisions are used to interpret and define the law, as in Ireland, the UK and the US.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal system based on practice and precedent, in which earlier court decisions are used to interpret and define the law, as in Ireland, the UK and the US. It recognises the trust.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) standard for automatic exchange of financial account information between tax authorities.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) standard for automatic exchange of financial account information between tax authorities. Financial institutions, including funds, must identify account holders' tax residence and report accounts of reportable persons each year; the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework applies the same approach to crypto-assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Rules requiring firms to have procedures to receive, investigate and respond to complaints fairly and within set times, and to tell customers about their right to refer to an ombudsman.
concepts.bodyHtml: Rules requiring firms to have procedures to receive, investigate and respond to complaints fairly and within set times, and to tell customers about their right to refer to an ombudsman.

concepts.shortDefinition: A product, such as most alternative investment funds (AIFs) or a structured UCITS, whose risks are considered difficult for a retail investor to understand.
concepts.bodyHtml: A product, such as most alternative investment funds (AIFs) or a structured UCITS, whose risks are considered difficult for a retail investor to understand. It cannot be sold on an execution-only basis.

concepts.shortDefinition: The independent function within a management company (ManCo) or other regulated firm that monitors and assesses compliance with regulatory obligations and advises management and staff.
concepts.bodyHtml: The independent function within a management company (ManCo) or other regulated firm that monitors and assesses compliance with regulatory obligations and advises management and staff. With risk management, it forms the second line of defence.

concepts.shortDefinition: A risk-based plan of reviews and tests carried out by the compliance function to check that the firm complies with regulatory requirements and that its controls work.
concepts.bodyHtml: A risk-based plan of reviews and tests carried out by the compliance function to check that the firm complies with regulatory requirements and that its controls work.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of breaching regulatory requirements, such as investment restrictions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of breaching regulatory requirements, such as investment restrictions. Breaches may be advertent (caused by the manager’s actions, requiring immediate correction and possibly compensation) or inadvertent (caused by factors such as market movements).

concepts.shortDefinition: An assessment of the regulatory obligations that apply to a firm and the risk of breaching them, used to prioritise compliance monitoring and advice.
concepts.bodyHtml: An assessment of the regulatory obligations that apply to a firm and the risk of breaching them, used to prioritise compliance monitoring and advice.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ability of decentralised finance (DeFi) protocols to connect and build on one another, like building blocks.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ability of decentralised finance (DeFi) protocols to connect and build on one another, like building blocks. It enables innovation but also transmits failures.

concepts.shortDefinition: The redemption of an investor’s units or shares at the fund’s initiative, for example because the investor is no longer eligible or because the fund is being terminated after its NAV has fallen below a set threshold.
concepts.bodyHtml: The redemption of an investor’s units or shares at the fund’s initiative, for example because the investor is no longer eligible or because the fund is being terminated after its NAV has fallen below a set threshold.

concepts.shortDefinition: An automated market maker design in which liquidity providers choose the price range in which their liquidity is used.
concepts.bodyHtml: An automated market maker design in which liquidity providers choose the price range in which their liquidity is used. It uses capital more efficiently but requires active management, and providers earn no fees when the price moves outside their range.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss from holding a large exposure to a single issuer, counterparty, sector, market or service provider.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss from holding a large exposure to a single issuer, counterparty, sector, market or service provider. Regulation limits concentration for funds sold to retail investors, and managers diversify to reduce it.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Dependence on one asset, venue, custodian, bank or service provider. In crypto markets many firms rely on the same few providers, so the risk can be shared across a whole sector.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that a firm's behaviour, or that of its staff, leads to poor outcomes for customers or harms the integrity of markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that a firm's behaviour, or that of its staff, leads to poor outcomes for customers or harms the integrity of markets. It is driven by culture, incentives, governance and the design of products and processes, and is assessed by regulators through outcomes rather than policies.

concepts.shortDefinition: Basic standards of personal conduct that apply to individuals in regulated firms, such as acting with integrity, due skill, care and diligence, and being open with regulators.
concepts.bodyHtml: Basic standards of personal conduct that apply to individuals in regulated firms, such as acting with integrity, due skill, care and diligence, and being open with regulators. In the UK they apply to almost all staff, with extra rules for senior managers.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Luxembourg, a person who effectively conducts the business of a management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) and is approved by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
concepts.bodyHtml: In Luxembourg, a person who effectively conducts the business of a management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) and is approved by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). A ManCo must have at least two; together they form the management committee and share responsibility for areas such as investment management, risk management, compliance and valuation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A situation in which the interests of a manager, its staff, its group or a service provider differ from those of the fund or its investors, or the interests of different investors differ.
concepts.bodyHtml: A situation in which the interests of a manager, its staff, its group or a service provider differ from those of the fund or its investors, or the interests of different investors differ. Management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must identify, prevent or manage and disclose conflicts, for example by separating functions.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: In tokenisation, one firm or group often sits on several sides of the same token, for example keeping the register, valuing the assets and running the trading venue. Separating these roles structurally is stronger than managing them by policy alone.

concepts.shortDefinition: A record of the types of conflicts of interest that have arisen or may arise and how each is managed, which regulated firms must keep and review.
concepts.bodyHtml: A record of the types of conflicts of interest that have arisen or may arise and how each is managed, which regulated firms must keep and review.

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules by which the nodes of a network agree on one version of the ledger: which transactions are valid and in what order.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules by which the nodes of a network agree on one version of the ledger: which transactions are valid and in what order. Proof of work and proof of stake are the main types. Whoever can influence consensus can influence the record.

concepts.shortDefinition: Where the national law has a consent regime, a firm that has reported suspicion asks the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) for consent before dealing with the funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: Where the national law has a consent regime, a firm that has reported suspicion asks the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) for consent before dealing with the funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Something of value given in exchange for a promise.
concepts.bodyHtml: Something of value given in exchange for a promise. Without consideration a promise is generally not enforceable as a contract unless it is made by deed.

concepts.shortDefinition: A permissioned blockchain governed by a group of organisations, such as banks or market infrastructures, which control who can join and validate.
concepts.bodyHtml: A permissioned blockchain governed by a group of organisations, such as banks or market infrastructures, which control who can join and validate.

concepts.shortDefinition: A money market fund that keeps a stable share price, usually 1.00, by valuing its assets at amortised cost.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money market fund that keeps a stable share price, usually 1.00, by valuing its assets at amortised cost. Under the EU Money Market Funds Regulation, CNAV funds must invest at least 99.5% in public debt instruments.

concepts.shortDefinition: An MMF that uses amortised cost accounting to keep the value of its shares at a constant level, such as €1.
concepts.bodyHtml: An MMF that uses amortised cost accounting to keep the value of its shares at a constant level, such as €1. Under the Money Market Funds Regulation (MMFR), only public debt constant net asset value (CNAV) MMFs may do so for all their assets; such funds must invest at least 99.5% in public debt instruments, reverse repos secured on public debt and cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: The pricing rule used by many automated market makers: the product of the quantities of the two tokens in a pool must stay constant.
concepts.bodyHtml: The pricing rule used by many automated market makers: the product of the quantities of the two tokens in a pool must stay constant. Buying one token reduces its quantity in the pool and raises its price.

concepts.shortDefinition: The document that establishes a fund and sets out its basic rules, such as its instrument of incorporation or memorandum and articles of association, trust deed, deed of constitution, management regulations or partnership agreement.
concepts.bodyHtml: The document that establishes a fund and sets out its basic rules, such as its instrument of incorporation or memorandum and articles of association, trust deed, deed of constitution, management regulations or partnership agreement. Also called the fund rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: EU rules on consumer credit.
concepts.bodyHtml: EU rules on consumer credit. The revised directive, Directive (EU) 2023/2225, extends the regime to buy now pay later and small loans, strengthens creditworthiness assessments and applies from 20 November 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) rule requiring firms to act to deliver good outcomes for retail customers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) rule requiring firms to act to deliver good outcomes for retail customers. It covers products and services, price and value, consumer understanding and consumer support, and requires boards to review annually whether the firm is delivering good outcomes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The four outcomes of the UK Consumer Duty: products and services, price and value, consumer understanding and consumer support.
concepts.bodyHtml: The four outcomes of the UK Consumer Duty: products and services, price and value, consumer understanding and consumer support. Firms must monitor and evidence good outcomes for retail customers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The spread of losses or loss of confidence from one firm, token or market to others through exposures, shared collateral or shared sentiment.
concepts.bodyHtml: The spread of losses or loss of confidence from one firm, token or market to others through exposures, shared collateral or shared sentiment.

concepts.shortDefinition: A new vehicle set up by a private fund manager to buy one or more assets from an existing fund, giving investors the choice of cashing out or rolling into the new fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A new vehicle set up by a private fund manager to buy one or more assets from an existing fund, giving investors the choice of cashing out or rolling into the new fund. Because the manager is on both sides, these deals need careful conflict management and a fair price, usually supported by a fairness opinion.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legally binding agreement: an exchange of promises between two or more parties to do, or refrain from doing, certain things.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legally binding agreement: an exchange of promises between two or more parties to do, or refrain from doing, certain things. A valid contract requires offer, acceptance and consideration, an intention to create legal relations, real consent, capacity, a lawful object and, where required, a particular form. Remedies for breach include damages, specific performance and an injunction.

concepts.shortDefinition: A derivative that pays the difference between an asset's price when the contract is opened and when it is closed, without ownership of the asset.
concepts.bodyHtml: A derivative that pays the difference between an asset's price when the contract is opened and when it is closed, without ownership of the asset. Retail CFDs in the EU and UK are subject to leverage limits, margin close-out rules, negative balance protection and risk warnings.

concepts.shortDefinition: A confirmation issued by the transfer agent (TA) after an order has been dealt, showing the number of units or shares, the price and the settlement date.
concepts.bodyHtml: A confirmation issued by the transfer agent (TA) after an order has been dealt, showing the number of units or shares, the price and the settlement date.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund constituted under contract law, by a deed of constitution (Ireland) or management regulations (Luxembourg), with no legal personality.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund constituted under contract law, by a deed of constitution (Ireland) or management regulations (Luxembourg), with no legal personality. Investors are co-owners of the assets, and the management company (ManCo) and depositary contract on the fund’s behalf.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Luxembourg, an entity that oversees the issuance of dematerialised securities, such as fund units issued on distributed ledger technology (DLT), and the reconciliation of the securities in circulation.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Luxembourg, an entity that oversees the issuance of dematerialised securities, such as fund units issued on distributed ledger technology (DLT), and the reconciliation of the securities in circulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond that gives its holder the option to convert it into other securities, usually shares of the issuer, at a predetermined conversion price.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond that gives its holder the option to convert it into other securities, usually shares of the issuer, at a predetermined conversion price.

concepts.shortDefinition: A period after a purchase or agreement during which the customer may withdraw without penalty.
concepts.bodyHtml: A period after a purchase or agreement during which the customer may withdraw without penalty. UK rules give first-time investors in high-risk investments, including crypto-assets, a 24-hour cooling-off period before their first investment.

concepts.shortDefinition: Coordinated Universal Time, the global time standard.
concepts.bodyHtml: Coordinated Universal Time, the global time standard. Blockchains and trading systems use UTC timestamps so that records from different time zones can be compared.

concepts.shortDefinition: An event initiated by an issuer that affects its securities, such as a dividend, rights issue, stock split, merger or conversion.
concepts.bodyHtml: An event initiated by an issuer that affects its securities, such as a dividend, rights issue, stock split, merger or conversion. It may be mandatory or voluntary for holders.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund established as a company with its own legal personality, managed by a board of directors and issuing shares to investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund established as a company with its own legal personality, managed by a board of directors and issuing shares to investors. It may have variable or fixed capital.

concepts.shortDefinition: The system by which a company is directed and controlled, including the role of its board, management, controls and accountability to shareholders.
concepts.bodyHtml: The system by which a company is directed and controlled, including the role of its board, management, controls and accountability to shareholders. It applies both to funds and their management companies (ManCos) and, through stewardship, to the companies in which funds invest.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2464), which requires large companies to report on sustainability matters using the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS).
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2464), which requires large companies to report on sustainability matters using the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). Its scope and timing have been cut back by the EU's omnibus simplification package.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ethereum staking, an additional slashing penalty that grows with the number of validators slashed in the same period, punishing common failures.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ethereum staking, an additional slashing penalty that grows with the number of validators slashed in the same period, punishing common failures.

concepts.shortDefinition: An arrangement in which one bank (the correspondent) provides payment and other services to another (the respondent), often in another country, holding accounts for each other (nostro and vostro accounts).
concepts.bodyHtml: An arrangement in which one bank (the correspondent) provides payment and other services to another (the respondent), often in another country, holding accounts for each other (nostro and vostro accounts). It carries elevated money laundering risk and requires enhanced due diligence.

concepts.shortDefinition: Banks exiting or restricting a whole sector or jurisdiction they see as high risk, rather than managing risk client by client.
concepts.bodyHtml: Banks exiting or restricting a whole sector or jurisdiction they see as high risk, rather than managing risk client by client. Often the first visible cost of a financial crime failure.

concepts.shortDefinition: An international organisation of 46 European states, separate from the EU, that promotes human rights, democracy and the rule of law.
concepts.bodyHtml: An international organisation of 46 European states, separate from the EU, that promotes human rights, democracy and the rule of law. It sets conventions on money laundering, cybercrime and data protection, and hosts MONEYVAL.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU institution in which ministers of member state governments meet to adopt EU law with the European Parliament.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU institution in which ministers of member state governments meet to adopt EU law with the European Parliament. Financial services files go through the Economic and Financial Affairs Council (ECOFIN), the meeting of finance ministers. Not to be confused with the European Council or the Council of Europe.

concepts.shortDefinition: Countering proliferation financing: measures to stop funds reaching programmes for weapons of mass destruction, including targeted financial sanctions and risk assessments required by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards.
concepts.bodyHtml: Countering proliferation financing: measures to stop funds reaching programmes for weapons of mass destruction, including targeted financial sanctions and risk assessments required by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards.

concepts.shortDefinition: Countering the financing of terrorism: measures to stop funds, including small sums and crypto-assets, reaching terrorists or terrorist organisations.
concepts.bodyHtml: Countering the financing of terrorism: measures to stop funds, including small sums and crypto-assets, reaching terrorists or terrorist organisations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that the other party to a transaction, such as an over the counter (OTC) derivative, securities lending or repo agreement, or an unsettled trade, defaults before meeting its obligations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that the other party to a transaction, such as an over the counter (OTC) derivative, securities lending or repo agreement, or an unsettled trade, defaults before meeting its obligations.

concepts.shortDefinition: Risk-based checks that a crypto service provider carries out on another provider it transacts with or serves, covering its licence or registration, its anti-money laundering (AML) programme and its customer base, as set out in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) guidance (2021).
concepts.bodyHtml: Risk-based checks that a crypto service provider carries out on another provider it transacts with or serves, covering its licence or registration, its anti-money laundering (AML) programme and its customer base, as set out in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) guidance (2021).

concepts.shortDefinition: The interest paid periodically on a bond, at a fixed or floating rate, expressed as a percentage of its face value.
concepts.bodyHtml: The interest paid periodically on a bond, at a fixed or floating rate, expressed as a percentage of its face value.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)’s Fund Management Companies Guidance and related rules, issued in December 2016 after a consultation of that number and applying to existing fund management companies (FMCs) from 1 July 2018.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)’s Fund Management Companies Guidance and related rules, issued in December 2016 after a consultation of that number and applying to existing fund management companies (FMCs) from 1 July 2018. It covers delegate oversight, managerial functions and designated persons, organisational effectiveness, directors’ time commitments, record retrievability and the location of directors and designated persons.

concepts.shortDefinition: The large block of exchange traded fund (ETF) shares in which an authorised participant (AP) creates or redeems directly with the ETF.
concepts.bodyHtml: The large block of exchange traded fund (ETF) shares in which an authorised participant (AP) creates or redeems directly with the ETF. Creation and redemption may be in kind, against a basket of securities, or in cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: An undertaking whose business is to take deposits or other repayable funds from the public and to grant credits for its own account, authorised and supervised under the EU's banking rules (the Capital Requirements Directive (CRD) and the Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR)).
concepts.bodyHtml: An undertaking whose business is to take deposits or other repayable funds from the public and to grant credits for its own account, authorised and supervised under the EU's banking rules (the Capital Requirements Directive (CRD) and the Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR)).

concepts.shortDefinition: An assessment by a credit rating agency of an issuer’s or debt instrument’s creditworthiness.
concepts.bodyHtml: An assessment by a credit rating agency of an issuer’s or debt instrument’s creditworthiness. A downgrade can reduce a bond’s price.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that assesses and rates the creditworthiness of issuers and debt instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that assesses and rates the creditworthiness of issuers and debt instruments. In the EU credit rating agencies are supervised directly by the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)).

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss because an issuer or borrower fails to pay interest or repay capital when due, or because its creditworthiness deteriorates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss because an issuer or borrower fails to pay interest or repay capital when due, or because its creditworthiness deteriorates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Managing and collecting payments on loans, including collecting interest and principal and dealing with borrowers in difficulty.
concepts.bodyHtml: Managing and collecting payments on loans, including collecting interest and principal and dealing with borrowers in difficulty. Since AIFMD II, alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) may service loans as an ancillary activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A document supplementing an ISDA master agreement that governs the collateral exchanged between the parties to over the counter (OTC) derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A document supplementing an ISDA master agreement that governs the collateral exchanged between the parties to over the counter (OTC) derivatives. An English law Credit Support Annex works by title transfer; a New York law one by a security interest.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment in which the payer instructs their provider to transfer funds from their account to the payee's account.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment in which the payer instructs their provider to transfer funds from their account to the payee's account. It is a push payment, initiated by the payer.

concepts.shortDefinition: The order in which a liquidator applies an insolvent company’s assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The order in which a liquidator applies an insolvent company’s assets. Broadly, fixed-charge creditors are paid from their security, the costs of the winding-up and preferential debts are paid before floating-charge holders and unsecured creditors, and members rank last.

concepts.shortDefinition: The liquidation of an insolvent company, which is controlled by its creditors or by the court rather than by its shareholders.
concepts.bodyHtml: The liquidation of an insolvent company, which is controlled by its creditors or by the court rather than by its shareholders.

concepts.shortDefinition: A lender's assessment, before granting credit, of whether the borrower can repay without significant financial difficulty, using relevant information about income, expenses and other commitments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A lender's assessment, before granting credit, of whether the borrower can repay without significant financial difficulty, using relevant information about income, expenses and other commitments.

concepts.shortDefinition: An information and communication technology (ICT) service provider, such as a large cloud provider, designated under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) as critical to the EU financial sector and overseen directly by the European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs).
concepts.bodyHtml: An information and communication technology (ICT) service provider, such as a large cloud provider, designated under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) as critical to the EU financial sector and overseen directly by the European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs).

concepts.shortDefinition: A function whose disruption would materially impair a firm's financial performance, the soundness or continuity of its services, or its compliance with its authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A function whose disruption would materially impair a firm's financial performance, the soundness or continuity of its services, or its compliance with its authorisation. Outsourcing or information and communication technology (ICT) arrangements that support such functions face stricter rules under EU law, including the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).

concepts.shortDefinition: A transaction between two funds or accounts managed by the same manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transaction between two funds or accounts managed by the same manager. It is allowed only where in the interests of both, at a fair market price and with conflicts managed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The marketing and sale of investment funds to investors in countries other than the fund's home country.
concepts.bodyHtml: The marketing and sale of investment funds to investors in countries other than the fund's home country. In the EU it is governed by passporting rules and by the 2019 package of rules on cross-border distribution.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2019/1160), which amended the UCITS Directive and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) to harmonise rules on pre-marketing, de-notification and the facilities that funds must provide to investors in host countries.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2019/1160), which amended the UCITS Directive and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) to harmonise rules on pre-marketing, de-notification and the facilities that funds must provide to investors in host countries.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Cross-Border Distribution of Funds Directive (CBDFD) and the Cross-Border Distribution of Funds Regulation (CBDFR), adopted in 2019 and applying in full since 2 August 2021.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Cross-Border Distribution of Funds Directive (CBDFD) and the Cross-Border Distribution of Funds Regulation (CBDFR), adopted in 2019 and applying in full since 2 August 2021. They harmonise pre-marketing, de-notification, facilities for investors and marketing communications and require national regulators to publish their marketing rules and fees.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2019/1156), which sets common rules on fund marketing communications, regulatory fees and the publication of national marketing rules, to make cross-border distribution of funds easier.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2019/1156), which sets common rules on fund marketing communications, regulatory fees and the publication of national marketing rules, to make cross-border distribution of funds easier.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2021/1230), which requires charges for cross-border euro payments in the EU to match those for domestic payments in the national currency and sets transparency rules for currency conversion.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2021/1230), which requires charges for cross-border euro payments in the EU to match those for domestic payments in the national currency and sets transparency rules for currency conversion.

concepts.shortDefinition: The G20's programme, coordinated by the Financial Stability Board (FSB) and the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI), to make cross-border payments faster, cheaper, more transparent and more accessible by 2027, through measures on messaging standards, data, access to payment systems and anti-money laundering (AML).
concepts.bodyHtml: The G20's programme, coordinated by the Financial Stability Board (FSB) and the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI), to make cross-border payments faster, cheaper, more transparent and more accessible by 2027, through measures on messaging standards, data, access to payment systems and anti-money laundering (AML).

concepts.shortDefinition: Protocols that let smart contracts on one blockchain send verified messages and instructions to contracts on another, underpinning bridges and multi-chain applications.
concepts.bodyHtml: Protocols that let smart contracts on one blockchain send verified messages and instructions to contracts on another, underpinning bridges and multi-chain applications.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investment by one sub-fund of an umbrella in another sub-fund of the same umbrella, permitted in Ireland and Luxembourg subject to conditions designed to avoid circular holdings and double charging of fees.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investment by one sub-fund of an umbrella in another sub-fund of the same umbrella, permitted in Ireland and Luxembourg subject to conditions designed to avoid circular holdings and double charging of fees. In Luxembourg, the voting rights of the target shares are suspended while held.

concepts.shortDefinition: A machine that exchanges cash for crypto-assets or the reverse.
concepts.bodyHtml: A machine that exchanges cash for crypto-assets or the reverse. They are used by fraudsters to get victims to send money, and several countries have banned or restricted them; in the UK, operating one requires the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) registration and the FCA has prosecuted unregistered operators.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment card linked to a crypto-asset balance, which converts crypto-assets into fiat currency when the card is used.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment card linked to a crypto-asset balance, which converts crypto-assets into fiat currency when the card is used. The card is issued by a regulated card issuer, often an e-money institution.

concepts.shortDefinition: Lending clients' crypto-assets to borrowers, or using them in yield strategies, in return for interest paid to the clients.
concepts.bodyHtml: Lending clients' crypto-assets to borrowers, or using them in yield strategies, in return for interest paid to the clients. Centralised lenders take custody of the assets, which can leave clients as unsecured creditors if the lender fails.

concepts.shortDefinition: A listed company whose main strategy is to buy and hold a crypto-asset, often funded by issuing shares or debt.
concepts.bodyHtml: A listed company whose main strategy is to buy and hold a crypto-asset, often funded by issuing shares or debt. Its shares can trade at a premium or discount to its crypto holdings.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ability of a system to switch cryptographic algorithms quickly, for example to post-quantum cryptography.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ability of a system to switch cryptographic algorithms quickly, for example to post-quantum cryptography.

concepts.shortDefinition: A digital representation of value or rights that can be transferred and stored electronically using distributed ledger technology (DLT), such as bitcoin.
concepts.bodyHtml: A digital representation of value or rights that can be transferred and stored electronically using distributed ledger technology (DLT), such as bitcoin. Crypto-assets that are not financial instruments are regulated by the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). Fund exposure to them is restricted, particularly for UCITS and retail alternative investment funds (AIFs).

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A digital representation of value or rights that can be transferred and stored electronically using DLT. The term used in MiCA.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) standard for the automatic exchange of tax information on crypto-asset transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) standard for the automatic exchange of tax information on crypto-asset transactions. Crypto-asset service providers collect information on their customers' transactions and report it to tax authorities, which exchange it with the customers' countries of residence. The EU implements it through DAC8.

concepts.shortDefinition: Crypto-asset service provider: the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) term for a firm authorised to provide one or more of ten crypto-asset services, with a passport across the EU.
concepts.bodyHtml: Crypto-asset service provider: the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) term for a firm authorised to provide one or more of ten crypto-asset services, with a passport across the EU.

concepts.shortDefinition: The disclosure document that must be published before crypto-assets are offered to the public or admitted to trading in the EU under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
concepts.bodyHtml: The disclosure document that must be published before crypto-assets are offered to the public or admitted to trading in the EU under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). It describes the issuer, the project, the rights attached, the underlying technology, the risks and the environmental impact. Those responsible are liable for its contents.

concepts.shortDefinition: A coin minted against crypto worth more than the coins issued, with automatic liquidation if cover falls (for example DAI, now Sky (formerly MakerDAO) dollar stablecoins (USDS) under Sky).
concepts.bodyHtml: A coin minted against crypto worth more than the coins issued, with automatic liquidation if cover falls (for example DAI, now Sky (formerly MakerDAO) dollar stablecoins (USDS) under Sky). It fails if collateral crashes faster than liquidations work, as on 12 March 2020.

concepts.shortDefinition: For a floating charge, its conversion into a fixed charge over the assets the company then holds, triggered by an event such as default.
concepts.bodyHtml: For a floating charge, its conversion into a fixed charge over the assets the company then holds, triggered by an event such as default. For a performance fee, the point at which the fee becomes payable to the manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share class denominated in a currency other than the fund’s base currency that seeks to reduce the effect on its investors of exchange-rate movements between the base currency and the class currency.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share class denominated in a currency other than the fund’s base currency that seeks to reduce the effect on its investors of exchange-rate movements between the base currency and the class currency. For UCITS, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) accepts hedging at share class level only for currency risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: Whether a firm holds or controls the keys on the client's behalf (custodial) or the client holds them alone (non-custodial).
concepts.bodyHtml: Whether a firm holds or controls the keys on the client's behalf (custodial) or the client holds them alone (non-custodial). A provider that keeps a recovery share or a signing veto is custodial in substance for that share.

concepts.shortDefinition: Historically, the party appointed to hold the assets of a corporate fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: Historically, the party appointed to hold the assets of a corporate fund. The term has largely been superseded by “depositary” for regulated funds, but is still used for entities, including sub-custodians, that hold assets in custody.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The firm that safekeeps a fund's assets and, in many funds, oversees the administrator. Where the assets are tokens, it holds or oversees the keys.

concepts.shortDefinition: The holding of financial instruments in safekeeping, in accounts opened in the name of the fund and segregated from the custodian’s own assets so that they are protected if it fails.
concepts.bodyHtml: The holding of financial instruments in safekeeping, in accounts opened in the name of the fund and segregated from the custodian’s own assets so that they are protected if it fails. It is part of the fund depositary’s safekeeping duty.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Holding assets, or the means of accessing them, on behalf of others. For virtual assets, the custodian controls the keys.
sectorNotes.defi: In DeFi, users usually keep their own assets in self-hosted wallets and interact with smart contracts directly. Assets deposited into a protocol are controlled by its code and by whoever holds its admin or upgrade keys, rather than by a custodian.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) service of safekeeping or controlling crypto-assets or the means of access to them, such as private keys, on behalf of clients.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) service of safekeeping or controlling crypto-assets or the means of access to them, such as private keys, on behalf of clients. Providers must segregate client assets and are liable for losses from incidents attributable to them.

concepts.shortDefinition: The anti-money laundering (AML) process of identifying and verifying an investor and its beneficial owners, understanding the purpose of the relationship and monitoring it on an ongoing basis.
concepts.bodyHtml: The anti-money laundering (AML) process of identifying and verifying an investor and its beneficial owners, understanding the purpose of the relationship and monitoring it on an ongoing basis. For funds it is usually carried out by the transfer agent (TA) or distributor.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Identifying and verifying the customer and its beneficial owners and understanding the relationship (FATF Recommendation 10). Enhanced due diligence adds measures for higher risk, such as evidence of source of funds and wealth. The firm remains responsible, including when it relies on third parties.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm's assessment of the money laundering and terrorist financing risk posed by an individual customer, based on factors such as the customer's profile, products, channels and geography.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm's assessment of the money laundering and terrorist financing risk posed by an individual customer, based on factors such as the customer's profile, products, channels and geography. It determines the level of due diligence applied.

concepts.shortDefinition: The latest time a payment order is treated as received that business day.
concepts.bodyHtml: The latest time a payment order is treated as received that business day. The execution time is the maximum time to credit the payee's provider; the value date is when funds start to earn or cost interest.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss or disruption from attacks on, or failures of, information systems, including data theft, ransomware and fraud.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss or disruption from attacks on, or failures of, information systems, including data theft, ransomware and fraud.

concepts.shortDefinition: Protecting systems, networks, data and assets from attack, damage or unauthorised access.
concepts.bodyHtml: Protecting systems, networks, data and assets from attack, damage or unauthorised access. For financial firms it covers prevention, detection, response and recovery, and is a central part of operational resilience.

concepts.shortDefinition: Cyprus's securities regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Cyprus's securities regulator. It supervises investment firms, many of which serve clients across the EU, along with fund managers, funds and crypto-asset service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2023/2226), which requires crypto-asset service providers to collect and report information on their EU customers' crypto-asset transactions to tax authorities from 2026, in line with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)'s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2023/2226), which requires crypto-asset service providers to collect and report information on their EU customers' crypto-asset transactions to tax authorities from 2026, in line with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)'s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assets of an MMF that mature, or can be turned into cash, within one working day or one week.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assets of an MMF that mature, or can be turned into cash, within one working day or one week. The Money Market Funds Regulation (MMFR) sets minimum proportions of between 7.5% and 30%, depending on the type of MMF and asset.

concepts.shortDefinition: Money awarded to the injured party for breach of contract, intended to put it in the position it would have been in had the contract been performed.
concepts.bodyHtml: Money awarded to the injured party for breach of contract, intended to put it in the position it would have been in had the contract been performed. Damages may cover loss of profits, but loss that is too remote is not recoverable and contracts often exclude indirect or consequential loss.

concepts.shortDefinition: An online marketplace reachable through anonymising networks, used to sell drugs, stolen data and other illicit goods, usually for crypto-assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: An online marketplace reachable through anonymising networks, used to sell drugs, stolen data and other illicit goods, usually for crypto-assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: The guarantee that the data behind a blockchain's transactions has been published and can be checked by anyone.
concepts.bodyHtml: The guarantee that the data behind a blockchain's transactions has been published and can be checked by anyone. It is a key issue for rollups, which post their transaction data to a base layer or to a separate data availability layer.

concepts.shortDefinition: An assessment the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires before processing that is likely to result in high risk to individuals, such as large-scale profiling or new technologies.
concepts.bodyHtml: An assessment the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires before processing that is likely to result in high risk to individuals, such as large-scale profiling or new technologies.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person that organisations must appoint under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in certain cases, for example where their core activities involve large-scale monitoring or processing of special category data, to advise on and monitor data protection compliance.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person that organisations must appoint under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in certain cases, for example where their core activities involve large-scale monitoring or processing of special category data, to advise on and monitor data protection compliance.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent provider of market data, such as asset prices and corporate action information, used by administrators to value assets and reflect corporate actions.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent provider of market data, such as asset prices and corporate action information, used by administrators to value assets and reflect corporate actions. Also called a pricing service or data service provider.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Dutch central bank and prudential supervisor of banks, insurers, pension funds, payment and e-money institutions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Dutch central bank and prudential supervisor of banks, insurers, pension funds, payment and e-money institutions. It also supervises anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance by many financial firms.

concepts.shortDefinition: The harmonised procedure for ceasing to market a fund in a host Member State.
concepts.bodyHtml: The harmonised procedure for ceasing to market a fund in a host Member State. The manager must offer to repurchase investors’ units free of charges for at least 30 working days, publicise its intention and end arrangements with intermediaries.

concepts.shortDefinition: Ending or restricting business relationships with whole categories of customers or countries to avoid risk, rather than managing the risk case by case.
concepts.bodyHtml: Ending or restricting business relationships with whole categories of customers or countries to avoid risk, rather than managing the risk case by case. Regulators and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) have warned that it can exclude legitimate customers and push activity into less transparent channels.

concepts.shortDefinition: The deadline by which orders must reach the transfer agent to be dealt on a given dealing day.
concepts.bodyHtml: The deadline by which orders must reach the transfer agent to be dealt on a given dealing day. Later orders are held over to the next dealing day.

concepts.shortDefinition: A day on which an open-ended fund accepts subscriptions and redemptions, as set out in its prospectus.
concepts.bodyHtml: A day on which an open-ended fund accepts subscriptions and redemptions, as set out in its prospectus. Orders received before the dealing cut-off are dealt at the price calculated at the next valuation point.

concepts.shortDefinition: A letter from a regulator to the chief executives of a group of firms setting out its expectations or concerns about a sector or issue.
concepts.bodyHtml: A letter from a regulator to the chief executives of a group of firms setting out its expectations or concerns about a sector or issue. It is not formal rules, but firms are expected to act on it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond backed only by the general creditworthiness of the issuing company and so unsecured.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond backed only by the general creditworthiness of the issuing company and so unsecured. UK debentures, by contrast, are generally secured on the issuer’s assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A contractual obligation of an issuer to repay borrowed money, with interest, to the holder on a set schedule.
concepts.bodyHtml: A contractual obligation of an issuer to repay borrowed money, with interest, to the holder on a set schedule. Examples include bonds, debentures, treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit.

concepts.shortDefinition: A group that governs a protocol through token-holder votes executed on-chain.
concepts.bodyHtml: A group that governs a protocol through token-holder votes executed on-chain. Courts have treated some DAOs as associations or partnerships (Ooki, Lido).

concepts.shortDefinition: A trading protocol that runs on smart contracts, letting users trade from their own wallets without a central operator holding the assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A trading protocol that runs on smart contracts, letting users trade from their own wallets without a central operator holding the assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Lending, trading, staking and other services built from smart contracts that anyone can use.
concepts.bodyHtml: Lending, trading, staking and other services built from smart contracts that anyone can use. Control is usually spread across several parties rather than absent.

concepts.shortDefinition: Approaches that let individuals hold verifiable credentials about themselves in a wallet and share them selectively, rather than relying on a central identity provider.
concepts.bodyHtml: Approaches that let individuals hold verifiable credentials about themselves in a wallet and share them selectively, rather than relying on a central identity provider.

concepts.shortDefinition: Decentralised physical infrastructure networks: projects that use tokens to reward people for providing real-world infrastructure, such as wireless coverage, data storage or computing power.
concepts.bodyHtml: Decentralised physical infrastructure networks: projects that use tokens to reward people for providing real-world infrastructure, such as wireless coverage, data storage or computing power.

concepts.shortDefinition: Networks that store files across many independent nodes, rather than a single provider, often with token incentives.
concepts.bodyHtml: Networks that store files across many independent nodes, rather than a single provider, often with token incentives. Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and decentralised finance (DeFi) front ends sometimes use them.

concepts.shortDefinition: The interface, usually an application programming interface (API), that a bank or other account provider must offer under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) so that third-party providers can access payment accounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: The interface, usually an application programming interface (API), that a bank or other account provider must offer under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) so that third-party providers can access payment accounts. Screen scraping, logging into the customer's online banking with their credentials, is allowed only as a fallback.

concepts.shortDefinition: A written document executed with special formalities, such as signing and sealing.
concepts.bodyHtml: A written document executed with special formalities, such as signing and sealing. A promise made by deed is enforceable without consideration, and some contracts must be made by deed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The deed, executed under seal between the management company (ManCo) and the fund depositary, that constitutes an Irish common contractual fund (CCF) and sets out the rights of the co-owners and the duties of the parties.
concepts.bodyHtml: The deed, executed under seal between the management company (ManCo) and the fund depositary, that constitutes an Irish common contractual fund (CCF) and sets out the rights of the co-owners and the duties of the parties.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal agreement in which a company promises to cover a director's costs and liabilities arising from their role, to the extent the law allows.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal agreement in which a company promises to cover a director's costs and liabilities arising from their role, to the extent the law allows. Its value depends on the company having the assets to pay.

concepts.shortDefinition: AI-generated video, audio or images that impersonate a real person, used to defeat liveness checks or to instruct payments (Arup, 2024).
concepts.bodyHtml: AI-generated video, audio or images that impersonate a real person, used to defeat liveness checks or to instruct payments (Arup, 2024).

concepts.shortDefinition: In the UK, permission from the National Crime Agency to proceed with a transaction a firm suspects involves criminal property.
concepts.bodyHtml: In the UK, permission from the National Crime Agency to proceed with a transaction a firm suspects involves criminal property. Obtaining it gives the firm a defence to money laundering offences.

concepts.shortDefinition: Paying part of variable pay over several years rather than immediately, so it can be reduced if risks materialise.
concepts.bodyHtml: Paying part of variable pay over several years rather than immediately, so it can be reduced if risks materialise. Remuneration rules require deferral for material risk takers in larger firms.

concepts.shortDefinition: Settling payments between participants periodically on a net basis rather than one by one.
concepts.bodyHtml: Settling payments between participants periodically on a net basis rather than one by one. It saves liquidity but creates credit exposure between settlement times.

concepts.shortDefinition: In the UK, interest-free credit repayable in 12 or fewer instalments within 12 months, commonly called buy now pay later.
concepts.bodyHtml: In the UK, interest-free credit repayable in 12 or fewer instalments within 12 months, commonly called buy now pay later. Third-party lenders offering it have been regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) since 15 July 2026; merchants offering their own credit remain exempt.

concepts.shortDefinition: The website or app through which users reach a decentralised protocol.
concepts.bodyHtml: The website or app through which users reach a decentralised protocol. Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) guidance (2021), a person who runs it and keeps control or sufficient influence, for example through admin keys and fees, may be a virtual asset service provider.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal act adopted by the European Commission, under powers given by an EU regulation or directive, to supplement or amend non-essential elements of that law.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal act adopted by the European Commission, under powers given by an EU regulation or directive, to supplement or amend non-essential elements of that law. The Parliament and Council can object to it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A form of proof of stake in which token holders vote for a limited number of delegates who validate blocks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A form of proof of stake in which token holders vote for a limited number of delegates who validate blocks. It is fast but concentrates control.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entrusting by a management company (ManCo) or fund of the performance of a function or task, such as portfolio management or administration, to a third party.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entrusting by a management company (ManCo) or fund of the performance of a function or task, such as portfolio management or administration, to a third party. The delegating entity remains responsible, must have an objective reason for the delegation and must oversee the delegate.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Ethereum feature, introduced in May 2025, that lets an ordinary wallet delegate its behaviour to smart contract code by signing an authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Ethereum feature, introduced in May 2025, that lets an ordinary wallet delegate its behaviour to smart contract code by signing an authorisation.

concepts.shortDefinition: Settlement in which the transfer of an asset happens if, and only if, payment is made.
concepts.bodyHtml: Settlement in which the transfer of an asset happens if, and only if, payment is made.

concepts.shortDefinition: North Korea.
concepts.bodyHtml: North Korea. Hacking groups linked to its state, such as the Lazarus Group, are responsible for some of the largest thefts of crypto-assets, and its activities are subject to UN and national sanctions.

concepts.shortDefinition: When a stablecoin's market price departs from its target value.
concepts.bodyHtml: When a stablecoin's market price departs from its target value.

concepts.shortDefinition: A scheme that repays depositors if their bank fails, up to a limit (in the EU, €100,000 per depositor per bank).
concepts.bodyHtml: A scheme that repays depositors if their bank fails, up to a limit (in the EU, €100,000 per depositor per bank). Money held with payment and e-money institutions is not covered.

concepts.shortDefinition: The written contract appointing a fund’s depositary, required under the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD).
concepts.bodyHtml: The written contract appointing a fund’s depositary, required under the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD). It sets out the fund depositary’s safekeeping and oversight duties, proper instructions, fees, liability, sub-custodians, termination and conflicts of interest; for unit trusts and contractual funds the trust deed or deed of constitution may specify the duties.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund depositary’s liability for loss of assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund depositary’s liability for loss of assets. Under the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) it must return an identical financial instrument, or the corresponding amount, without undue delay if one held in custody is lost, unless the loss arose from an external event beyond its reasonable control; an AIF depositary may in specific circumstances discharge liability to a sub-custodian.

concepts.shortDefinition: A financial instrument, such as a future, forward, option or swap, whose value is derived from the price of an underlying asset, index, rate or other reference.
concepts.bodyHtml: A financial instrument, such as a future, forward, option or swap, whose value is derived from the price of an underlying asset, index, rate or other reference. Funds use derivatives for hedging, efficient portfolio management or investment, and they can create leverage.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A contract whose value is derived from an underlying asset, such as a future, option or perpetual swap.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish private limited company that has a specific objects clause limiting its activities.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish private limited company that has a specific objects clause limiting its activities. DACs are often used for regulated entities and special purpose vehicles.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ireland, an individual responsible for overseeing one of the six managerial functions of a fund management company (FMC) under CP86.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ireland, an individual responsible for overseeing one of the six managerial functions of a fund management company (FMC) under CP86. A designated person need not be a director but holds a pre-approval controlled function (PCF).
