It has no legal personality, so it cannot be self-managed. It can be a UCITS, a Part II fund, a specialised investment fund (SIF) or a reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF).

concepts.term: For or on behalf of another
concepts.shortDefinition: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF)'s qualifier: only services provided to other people are virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF)'s qualifier: only services provided to other people are virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity. Own-account trading or validation is generally outside, though other regimes may still apply.
concepts.sortKey: for or on behalf of another

concepts.shortDefinition: Moving tokens without the holder's signature, for example after a court order, death, insolvency or theft.
concepts.bodyHtml: Moving tokens without the holder's signature, for example after a court order, death, insolvency or theft. It needs a legal basis in the documents, approval and a log.

concepts.shortDefinition: US legislation requiring financial institutions outside the US, including funds, to identify accounts held by US persons and report them, usually through their local tax authority under an intergovernmental agreement, or face 30% withholding on certain US payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: US legislation requiring financial institutions outside the US, including funds, to identify accounts held by US persons and report them, usually through their local tax authority under an intergovernmental agreement, or face 30% withholding on certain US payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: Government limits on foreign investors buying the securities of domestic companies, such as caps on the proportion of a company’s equity that overseas investors may hold.
concepts.bodyHtml: Government limits on foreign investors buying the securities of domestic companies, such as caps on the proportion of a company’s equity that overseas investors may hold.

concepts.shortDefinition: Foreign exchange: the exchange of one currency for another.
concepts.bodyHtml: Foreign exchange: the exchange of one currency for another. FX costs and FX hedging are significant for funds investing across currencies and for cross-border payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A change to a blockchain's rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: A change to a blockchain's rules. A soft fork is backward-compatible; a hard fork is not and can split the chain into two.

concepts.shortDefinition: A confidential report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission by registered advisers to private funds above certain size thresholds, used to monitor systemic risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: A confidential report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission by registered advisers to private funds above certain size thresholds, used to monitor systemic risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: Using mathematical methods to prove that a smart contract or system behaves according to a formal specification.
concepts.bodyHtml: Using mathematical methods to prove that a smart contract or system behaves according to a formal specification. It can rule out whole classes of bugs but only for the properties specified.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bilateral over the counter (OTC) contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, tailored to the needs of the parties.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bilateral over the counter (OTC) contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, tailored to the needs of the parties. Funds commonly use currency forwards for hedging.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dealing at the price calculated at the next valuation point after an order is received, so that the price is not known when the order is placed.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dealing at the price calculated at the next valuation point after an order is received, so that the price is not known when the order is placed. It prevents investors trading on out-of-date prices.

concepts.shortDefinition: Holdings of less than one whole share, offered by some brokers and platforms so investors can invest small amounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: Holdings of less than one whole share, offered by some brokers and platforms so investors can invest small amounts. They are usually held through a nominee and may not carry voting rights directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under payment services rules, the agreement governing a series of future payments, such as an account agreement, which requires detailed prior information and two months' notice of changes.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under payment services rules, the agreement governing a series of future payments, such as an account agreement, which requires detailed prior information and two months' notice of changes. A single payment contract covers a one-off payment with lighter requirements.

concepts.shortDefinition: The value of fraudulent transactions divided by total value over a period.
concepts.bodyHtml: The value of fraudulent transactions divided by total value over a period. Payment providers must stay below reference fraud rates to use the transaction risk analysis exemption from strong customer authentication.

concepts.shortDefinition: Stopping a wallet, or the whole token, from transacting: a sanctions and court-order tool.
concepts.bodyHtml: Stopping a wallet, or the whole token, from transacting: a sanctions and court-order tool. Only useful if the right person can use it quickly and lawfully.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract function that lets the issuer stop an address from moving tokens.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract function that lets the issuer stop an address from moving tokens. It is both a financial crime control and a custody risk, so issuers and custodians need a written policy on when and how it is used.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of common questions and their answers.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of common questions and their answers. Regulators often publish questions and answerses (Q&As) or FAQs to explain how they apply their rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: Trading ahead of a known pending order to profit from its expected price impact.
concepts.bodyHtml: Trading ahead of a known pending order to profit from its expected price impact. In traditional markets it is market abuse by a firm handling client orders; on public blockchains it is done by watching pending transactions in the mempool.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ending of a contract because, without the fault of either party, it has become impossible to perform, for example because its subject matter has been destroyed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ending of a contract because, without the fault of either party, it has become impossible to perform, for example because its subject matter has been destroyed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK's regime bringing cryptoasset activities within the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK's regime bringing cryptoasset activities within the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026. It creates new regulated activities, such as operating a cryptoasset trading platform, dealing, arranging, safeguarding, staking and issuing qualifying stablecoins, which require the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) authorisation. The regime fully commences on 25 October 2027.

concepts.shortDefinition: A node that checks every block and transaction against the network's rules itself.
concepts.bodyHtml: A node that checks every block and transaction against the network's rules itself. Running a full node is the strongest way for a firm to verify its own deposits and balances.

concepts.shortDefinition: A measure of staffing that converts part-time and full-time posts into an equivalent number of full-time staff.
concepts.bodyHtml: A measure of staffing that converts part-time and full-time posts into an equivalent number of full-time staff. Regulators use FTE figures when assessing whether a firm has enough substance and resources.

concepts.shortDefinition: Fully diluted valuation: a token's price multiplied by its maximum supply, including tokens not yet released.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fully diluted valuation: a token's price multiplied by its maximum supply, including tokens not yet released. It shows how large a project's value would be if all tokens were in circulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A regulated activity that a management company (ManCo) must perform for the funds it manages: investment management (portfolio and risk management), administration and marketing.
concepts.bodyHtml: A regulated activity that a management company (ManCo) must perform for the funds it manages: investment management (portfolio and risk management), administration and marketing. The tasks making up a function may be delegated, but the ManCo remains responsible.

concepts.shortDefinition: Maintaining a fund’s books and records, including its list of investments, cash, income, fees and expense accruals, so that the NAV can be calculated and financial statements prepared.
concepts.bodyHtml: Maintaining a fund’s books and records, including its list of investments, cash, income, fees and expense accruals, so that the NAV can be calculated and financial statements prepared. It is a core fund administration activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The activities that support the ongoing operation of a fund, including fund accounting, valuation and pricing, maintaining the investor register, processing issues and redemptions, distributing income, compliance monitoring and record keeping.
concepts.bodyHtml: The activities that support the ongoing operation of a fund, including fund accounting, valuation and pricing, maintaining the investor register, processing issues and redemptions, distributing income, compliance monitoring and record keeping.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract appointing a fund administrator, describing its services, such as NAV calculation, fee calculation, financial statements, assistance with the audit, regulatory filings and, often, transfer agent (TA) services.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract appointing a fund administrator, describing its services, such as NAV calculation, fee calculation, financial statements, assistance with the audit, regulatory filings and, often, transfer agent (TA) services.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entity, usually appointed by the management company (ManCo), that performs fund administration, in particular calculating the NAV, keeping the fund’s accounts and often acting as transfer agent.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entity, usually appointed by the management company (ManCo), that performs fund administration, in particular calculating the NAV, keeping the fund’s accounts and often acting as transfer agent. In Ireland administrators are authorised by the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) under the Investment Intermediaries Act 1995 (IIA); in Luxembourg their activities are governed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) Circular 22/811.

concepts.shortDefinition: The independent entity, usually a bank or specialist trust company, appointed to safekeep a fund’s assets and to oversee the fund’s operation, including subscriptions and redemptions, NAV calculation, cash flows and compliance with investment limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The independent entity, usually a bank or specialist trust company, appointed to safekeep a fund’s assets and to oversee the fund’s operation, including subscriptions and redemptions, NAV calculation, cash flows and compliance with investment limits. Every UCITS, and every AIF managed by an authorised alternative investment fund manager (AIFM), must appoint one. The term has largely superseded “custodian” and “trustee”.

concepts.shortDefinition: A unit or share in a regulated fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A unit or share in a regulated fund. A token that simply represents one is regulated as a fund interest under fund rules, not as a virtual asset.

concepts.shortDefinition: The stages of a fund’s life: its design and establishment, its distribution to investors, its management, investment and administration, and its termination and winding up.
concepts.bodyHtml: The stages of a fund’s life: its design and establishment, its distribution to investors, its management, investment and administration, and its termination and winding up.

concepts.shortDefinition: Closing a fund by selling its assets, paying its liabilities and distributing the remaining proceeds to investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: Closing a fund by selling its assets, paying its liabilities and distributing the remaining proceeds to investors. It usually needs regulatory notification or approval and must treat all investors fairly.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ireland, the collective term for UCITS management companies (ManCos), alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) and self-managed investment companies to which the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)’s CP86 framework applies.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ireland, the collective term for UCITS management companies (ManCos), alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) and self-managed investment companies to which the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)’s CP86 framework applies.

concepts.shortDefinition: The combination of two or more funds, in which the assets of one or more merging funds are transferred to a receiving fund and investors receive units in it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The combination of two or more funds, in which the assets of one or more merging funds are transferred to a receiving fund and investors receive units in it. UCITS mergers require prior authorisation and at least 30 days’ information to investors; alternative investment fund (AIF) mergers are governed by national law.

concepts.shortDefinition: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)’s Guidelines on funds’ names using environmental, social and governance (ESG) or sustainability-related terms, which apply from 21 November 2024 for new funds and 21 May 2025 for existing funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)’s Guidelines on funds’ names using environmental, social and governance (ESG) or sustainability-related terms, which apply from 21 November 2024 for new funds and 21 May 2025 for existing funds. A fund using such terms must invest at least 80% of its assets in line with its characteristics or objectives and apply PAB or CTB exclusions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests principally in other funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests principally in other funds. It may be “fettered” (investing only in funds of its own manager or group) or “unfettered” (investing also or only in third-party funds). Investors may bear fees at both levels.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm, usually an asset management group, that initiates a fund, designs its strategy and markets it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm, usually an asset management group, that initiates a fund, designs its strategy and markets it. It typically sets up or appoints the management company (ManCo) and acts as, or appoints, the investment manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: The constitutional document of a contractual or unit trust fund, setting out its objectives, investment powers, dealing arrangements, fees and the duties of the manager and trustee or depositary.
concepts.bodyHtml: The constitutional document of a contractual or unit trust fund, setting out its objectives, investment powers, dealing arrangements, fees and the duties of the manager and trustee or depositary. Corporate funds use articles of association or an instrument of incorporation instead.

concepts.shortDefinition: The periodic payment between long and short positions on perpetual futures.
concepts.bodyHtml: The periodic payment between long and short positions on perpetual futures. It provides a synthetic dollar's yield — and becomes a cost when it turns negative.

concepts.shortDefinition: Interchangeable, unit for unit, like coins or shares of the same class.
concepts.bodyHtml: Interchangeable, unit for unit, like coins or shares of the same class. Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) are non-fungible.

concepts.shortDefinition: A standardised, exchange-traded contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, with margin exchanged through a central counterparty (CCP).
concepts.bodyHtml: A standardised, exchange-traded contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, with margin exchanged through a central counterparty (CCP).

concepts.shortDefinition: The difference between the exchange rate a provider gives a customer and a reference rate, which is a hidden cost in cross-border payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The difference between the exchange rate a provider gives a customer and a reference rate, which is a hidden cost in cross-border payments. EU rules require currency conversion charges to be shown as a percentage mark-up over the European Central Bank (ECB) reference rate for euro payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fee paid to process a transaction or run a smart contract on Ethereum and similar networks.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fee paid to process a transaction or run a smart contract on Ethereum and similar networks.

concepts.shortDefinition: A mechanism by which governance token holders vote to direct a protocol's token rewards to particular liquidity pools.
concepts.bodyHtml: A mechanism by which governance token holders vote to direct a protocol's token rewards to particular liquidity pools. Projects may pay voters 'bribes' or incentives to vote for their pools.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), the EU's law on the processing of personal data.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), the EU's law on the processing of personal data. It sets principles such as lawfulness, data minimisation and purpose limitation, gives individuals rights over their data and imposes significant fines. Its interaction with immutable blockchains is a known tension.

concepts.shortDefinition: The partner that manages a limited partnership and has unlimited liability for its debts.
concepts.bodyHtml: The partner that manages a limited partnership and has unlimited liability for its debts. In a fund LP it usually appoints an external alternative investment fund manager (AIFM).

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the EU AI Act, an artificial intelligence (AI) model that can perform a wide range of distinct tasks and be integrated into many systems, such as large language models.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the EU AI Act, an artificial intelligence (AI) model that can perform a wide range of distinct tasks and be integrated into many systems, such as large language models. Providers have documentation and copyright duties, and models with systemic risk face extra obligations.

concepts.shortDefinition: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems that produce new content, such as text, images, code or audio, in response to prompts, usually based on large language models or similar models trained on large datasets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems that produce new content, such as text, images, code or audio, in response to prompts, usually based on large language models or similar models trained on large datasets.

concepts.shortDefinition: The first block of a blockchain, hard-coded into its software, from which all later blocks descend.
concepts.bodyHtml: The first block of a blockchain, hard-coded into its software, from which all later blocks descend.

aliases: Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act
concepts.shortDefinition: The US federal law, signed in July 2025, that creates a regulatory framework for payment stablecoins.
concepts.bodyHtml: The US federal law, signed in July 2025, that creates a regulatory framework for payment stablecoins. It requires issuers to be licensed, to back stablecoins one-for-one with high-quality liquid assets, to publish reserve reports and to give holders redemption rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: Policies controlling the giving and receiving of gifts and entertainment to prevent bribery and conflicts of interest, usually with value limits, approval and a register.
concepts.bodyHtml: Policies controlling the giving and receiving of gifts and entertainment to prevent bribery and conflicts of interest, usually with value limits, approval and a register.

concepts.shortDefinition: The exposure of a UCITS arising from its use of derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: The exposure of a UCITS arising from its use of derivatives. Under the commitment approach, which converts derivative positions into the equivalent position in the underlying assets, it may not exceed 100% of NAV; alternatively it is measured using a value-at-risk approach.

concepts.shortDefinition: A hedge fund strategy that takes positions across currencies, interest rates, equities and commodities based on views of economic and political developments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A hedge fund strategy that takes positions across currencies, interest rates, equities and commodities based on views of economic and political developments.

concepts.shortDefinition: The addition by a Member State of national requirements on top of those in EU legislation, for example on fund marketing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The addition by a Member State of national requirements on top of those in EU legislation, for example on fund marketing. The Commission’s Market Integration and Supervision proposals would stop host Member States doing so.

concepts.shortDefinition: Taking control of a protocol's governance, for example by buying or borrowing enough governance tokens, to pass proposals that benefit the attacker, such as draining the treasury.
concepts.bodyHtml: Taking control of a protocol's governance, for example by buying or borrowing enough governance tokens, to pass proposals that benefit the attacker, such as draining the treasury.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token that gives its holders votes on changes to a protocol.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token that gives its holders votes on changes to a protocol. Concentrated holdings can let a few holders control it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond issued by a national government, such as an Irish government bond.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond issued by a national government, such as an Irish government bond. Governments also issue short-term bills. Also called a sovereign bond.

concepts.shortDefinition: A provision requiring a private fund manager to return carried interest it has received if, at the end of the fund's life, it has been paid more than its entitlement, for example because later investments performed badly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A provision requiring a private fund manager to return carried interest it has received if, at the end of the fund's life, it has been paid more than its entitlement, for example because later investments performed badly.

concepts.shortDefinition: The practice of deliberately understating or ceasing to disclose the sustainability features of products – for example, reclassifying Article 9 funds as Article 8 or removing environmental, social and governance (ESG) terms from fund names – to reduce regulatory, legal or reputational risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: The practice of deliberately understating or ceasing to disclose the sustainability features of products – for example, reclassifying Article 9 funds as Article 8 or removing environmental, social and governance (ESG) terms from fund names – to reduce regulatory, legal or reputational risk. It deprives investors of information and is the opposite risk to greenwashing. Also called greenhushing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Sustainability-related statements, declarations, actions or communications that do not clearly and fairly reflect the underlying sustainability profile of an entity or product, and that may mislead investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: Sustainability-related statements, declarations, actions or communications that do not clearly and fairly reflect the underlying sustainability profile of an entity or product, and that may mislead investors. It is a supervisory priority for the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI), the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)).

concepts.shortDefinition: The total value of a fund's assets before deducting liabilities such as borrowings.
concepts.bodyHtml: The total value of a fund's assets before deducting liabilities such as borrowings. Some real estate and private credit funds charge fees on it, which rewards leverage.

concepts.shortDefinition: A method of calculating an AIF’s leverage that adds together the absolute values of all its positions, without netting or hedging.
concepts.bodyHtml: A method of calculating an AIF’s leverage that adds together the absolute values of all its positions, without netting or hedging. Alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must calculate leverage under both the gross and the commitment methods.

concepts.shortDefinition: A high degree of carelessness, beyond ordinary negligence.
concepts.bodyHtml: A high degree of carelessness, beyond ordinary negligence. Under payment services rules a payer who is grossly negligent in protecting their security credentials may bear the full loss of unauthorised transactions; providers bear the burden of proving it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Council of Europe body that monitors its member states' compliance with anti-corruption standards through peer evaluations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Council of Europe body that monitors its member states' compliance with anti-corruption standards through peer evaluations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Group of Twenty, a forum of 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Group of Twenty, a forum of 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union. It sets the agenda for international financial reform, carried out through the Financial Stability Board (FSB) and the standard setters.

concepts.shortDefinition: The tendency of a cohesive group to reach consensus without a realistic appraisal of alternatives or risks.
concepts.bodyHtml: The tendency of a cohesive group to reach consensus without a realistic appraisal of alternatives or risks. Warning signs on a board include quick unanimous decisions on contested topics and directors keeping their doubts to themselves.

concepts.shortDefinition: A quantum algorithm that speeds up brute-force search.
concepts.bodyHtml: A quantum algorithm that speeds up brute-force search. It weakens hashes and symmetric keys, but 256-bit versions remain strong.

concepts.shortDefinition: The financial services regulator of the Bailiwick of Guernsey, a Crown Dependency.
concepts.bodyHtml: The financial services regulator of the Bailiwick of Guernsey, a Crown Dependency. It regulates banking, insurance, investment business and funds, fiduciary services and lending, and supervises anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance.

concepts.term: Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act 2025
concepts.shortDefinition: The US federal stablecoin law, signed 18 July 2025 and effective by 18 January 2027 at the latest.
concepts.bodyHtml: The US federal stablecoin law, signed 18 July 2025 and effective by 18 January 2027 at the latest. It requires 1:1 reserves, monthly reserve examination and bans issuer interest; issuers are Bank Secrecy Act financial institutions.
concepts.sortKey: guiding and establishing national innovation for us stablecoins act 2025

concepts.shortDefinition: The discount applied to an asset's market value when it is used as collateral or counted towards capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: The discount applied to an asset's market value when it is used as collateral or counted towards capital. Haircuts can be set by models or from historical price falls.

concepts.shortDefinition: When a generative AI system produces information that is false or invented but presented as fact, such as fake citations or wrong figures.
concepts.bodyHtml: When a generative AI system produces information that is false or invented but presented as fact, such as fake citations or wrong figures.

concepts.shortDefinition: The scheduled halving of the new bitcoin issued to miners, about every four years (most recently April 2024).
concepts.bodyHtml: The scheduled halving of the new bitcoin issued to miners, about every four years (most recently April 2024). Supply is capped at 21 million.

concepts.shortDefinition: Certified tamper-resistant hardware, usually in a data centre, that stores keys and signs.
concepts.bodyHtml: Certified tamper-resistant hardware, usually in a data centre, that stores keys and signs. The control point becomes whoever administers the HSM.

concepts.shortDefinition: A small physical device that stores private keys offline and signs transactions on the device.
concepts.bodyHtml: A small physical device that stores private keys offline and signs transactions on the device.

concepts.shortDefinition: Recording encrypted data today in order to decrypt it once a quantum computer exists.
concepts.bodyHtml: Recording encrypted data today in order to decrypt it once a quantum computer exists. A live risk now for long-lived confidential data, such as Travel Rule messages.

concepts.shortDefinition: A function that turns any input into a short, fixed-length fingerprint.
concepts.bodyHtml: A function that turns any input into a short, fixed-length fingerprint. Any change to the input changes the output completely, and the input cannot be worked out from the output. Hashing makes tampering with a record visible, not impossible.

concepts.shortDefinition: The total computing power used to mine and secure a proof-of-work blockchain, measured in hashes per second.
concepts.bodyHtml: The total computing power used to mine and secure a proof-of-work blockchain, measured in hashes per second. A higher hash rate makes a 51% attack more expensive.

concepts.shortDefinition: A traditional informal system for transferring value through a network of brokers who settle balances between themselves, without moving money directly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A traditional informal system for transferring value through a network of brokers who settle balances between themselves, without moving money directly. Unregistered operation is illegal in most jurisdictions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The person responsible for the internal audit function, which gives independent assurance to the board on governance, risk management and controls.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person responsible for the internal audit function, which gives independent assurance to the board on governance, risk management and controls. They usually report to the audit committee.

concepts.shortDefinition: In decentralised finance (DeFi) lending, a measure of how safe a loan is.
concepts.bodyHtml: In decentralised finance (DeFi) lending, a measure of how safe a loan is. Below 1, the collateral can be liquidated.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment fund, usually an alternative investment fund (AIF), that uses flexible strategies and techniques such as short selling, leverage and derivatives to seek returns in different market conditions.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment fund, usually an alternative investment fund (AIF), that uses flexible strategies and techniques such as short selling, leverage and derivatives to seek returns in different market conditions. It has no definition in EU law.

concepts.shortDefinition: Using a derivative or other position to offset the risk of an adverse price movement in an asset or currency.
concepts.bodyHtml: Using a derivative or other position to offset the risk of an adverse price movement in an asset or currency.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wealthy individual investor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wealthy individual investor. Depending on the rules, such an individual may elect to be treated as a professional client, or qualify as a qualifying investor or well-informed investor.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the EU AI Act, an artificial intelligence (AI) system used in an area listed as high-risk, such as creditworthiness assessment, or as a safety component of a regulated product.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the EU AI Act, an artificial intelligence (AI) system used in an area listed as high-risk, such as creditworthiness assessment, or as a safety component of a regulated product. Providers and deployers must meet requirements on risk management, data, transparency, human oversight and accuracy.

concepts.shortDefinition: A merchant whose business carries elevated fraud, chargeback or legal risk, such as gambling, adult content, travel or crypto.
concepts.bodyHtml: A merchant whose business carries elevated fraud, chargeback or legal risk, such as gambling, adult content, travel or crypto. Acquirers apply enhanced onboarding, monitoring and reserves.

concepts.shortDefinition: The highest NAV per share previously reached by a fund, used as a reference point so that a performance fee is paid only on new gains above it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The highest NAV per share previously reached by a fund, used as a reference point so that a performance fee is paid only on new gains above it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dealing in fund units at the price calculated at the last valuation point before the order was received.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dealing in fund units at the price calculated at the last valuation point before the order was received. Most regulators require or prefer forward pricing because historic pricing lets informed investors trade on stale prices.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK government's finance ministry.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK government's finance ministry. It sets the legislative framework for financial services, including the scope of regulation, and makes the statutory instruments that bring new activities, such as cryptoassets, into regulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A cap on how much of a central bank digital currency an individual could hold, intended to stop large shifts of bank deposits into the CBDC, especially in a crisis.
concepts.bodyHtml: A cap on how much of a central bank digital currency an individual could hold, intended to stop large shifts of bank deposits into the CBDC, especially in a crisis.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised and whose regulator supervises it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised and whose regulator supervises it. Its product and licensing rules apply wherever the fund is marketed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Hong Kong's central banking institution.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Hong Kong's central banking institution. It supervises banks and stored value facilities and licenses fiat-referenced stablecoin issuers.

concepts.shortDefinition: One transfer between addresses.
concepts.bodyHtml: One transfer between addresses. Analytics counts the hops between a deposit and a risky source; confidence usually falls with each hop, but the risk does not disappear.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Member State, other than the home Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised, in which the fund is marketed or the manager operates under a passport, and whose local marketing rules apply.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Member State, other than the home Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised, in which the fund is marketed or the manager operates under a passport, and whose local marketing rules apply.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are held by a service provider on the customer's behalf.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are held by a service provider on the customer's behalf. Also called a custodial wallet.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are online, so that it can pay withdrawals quickly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are online, so that it can pay withdrawals quickly. It is the most exposed to attack.

concepts.shortDefinition: High-quality liquid assets: cash and assets such as short-dated government debt that can be sold quickly near full value.
concepts.bodyHtml: High-quality liquid assets: cash and assets such as short-dated government debt that can be sold quickly near full value. Central to stablecoin reserves where there is no central bank to hold deposits.

concepts.shortDefinition: Arrangements that let people monitor, understand and intervene in an artificial intelligence (AI) system's operation.
concepts.bodyHtml: Arrangements that let people monitor, understand and intervene in an artificial intelligence (AI) system's operation. The EU AI Act requires it for high-risk AI systems.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum return that investors must receive before the manager earns a performance fee or carried interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum return that investors must receive before the manager earns a performance fee or carried interest. Also called the hurdle.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss from the failure, compromise or misuse of information and communication technology systems and data, including cyber attacks, at the manager or its service providers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss from the failure, compromise or misuse of information and communication technology systems and data, including cyber attacks, at the manager or its service providers. Under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), managers must have an ICT risk management framework.

concepts.shortDefinition: A contract with an ICT third-party service provider which, under Article 30 of the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), must include mandatory terms such as a description of the services, data locations, service levels, incident assistance, cooperation with regulators and termination rights and, for critical or important functions, audit rights and exit strategies.
concepts.bodyHtml: A contract with an ICT third-party service provider which, under Article 30 of the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), must include mandatory terms such as a description of the services, data locations, service levels, incident assistance, cooperation with regulators and termination rights and, for critical or important functions, audit rights and exit strategies.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that provides digital and data services, such as cloud, software, data and hosting, to a financial entity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that provides digital and data services, such as cloud, software, data and hosting, to a financial entity. Under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), financial entities must manage the risks from these providers, keep a register of the arrangements and include required terms in contracts.

concepts.shortDefinition: In practice, "very costly to change" rather than "impossible to change".
concepts.bodyHtml: In practice, "very costly to change" rather than "impossible to change". How immutable a blockchain is depends on how widely its network is spread; majority control can rewrite recent history.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investing with the intention of generating, and measuring, positive environmental or social effects alongside a financial return.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investing with the intention of generating, and measuring, positive environmental or social effects alongside a financial return.

concepts.shortDefinition: The maximum disruption to an important business service that a firm can tolerate before harm becomes intolerable.
concepts.bodyHtml: The maximum disruption to an important business service that a firm can tolerate before harm becomes intolerable. A concept from the UK operational resilience rules, now widely used elsewhere.

concepts.shortDefinition: The loss a liquidity provider in an automated market maker suffers, compared with simply holding the tokens, when the relative price of the tokens in the pool changes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The loss a liquidity provider in an automated market maker suffers, compared with simply holding the tokens, when the relative price of the tokens in the pool changes. It becomes permanent if the provider withdraws before prices return.

concepts.shortDefinition: Technical rules, often templates, formats and procedures, drafted by an ESA and adopted by the Commission as an implementing act, that specify how firms and supervisors apply EU law.
concepts.bodyHtml: Technical rules, often templates, formats and procedures, drafted by an ESA and adopted by the Commission as an implementing act, that specify how firms and supervisors apply EU law.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service a firm provides to clients or the market whose disruption could cause intolerable harm to clients or risk to market integrity or the firm's viability.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service a firm provides to clients or the market whose disruption could cause intolerable harm to clients or risk to market integrity or the firm's viability. Operational resilience rules require firms to identify these services and set impact tolerances for them.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ethereum proof of stake, the gradual draining of offline validators' stake when the chain cannot finalise.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ethereum proof of stake, the gradual draining of offline validators' stake when the chain cannot finalise.

concepts.shortDefinition: A breach of an investment restriction caused by factors outside the manager’s control, such as market movements or subscriptions and redemptions.
concepts.bodyHtml: A breach of an investment restriction caused by factors outside the manager’s control, such as market movements or subscriptions and redemptions. It must be remedied as a priority, taking due account of investors’ interests, but compensation is generally not payable.

concepts.shortDefinition: The processes for detecting, escalating, responding to, recovering from and learning from operational incidents, including reporting to regulators and customers where required.
concepts.bodyHtml: The processes for detecting, escalating, responding to, recovering from and learning from operational incidents, including reporting to regulators and customers where required.

concepts.shortDefinition: The plan and process for detecting, containing, investigating and recovering from an operational or security incident, including decisions on escalation and notification of regulators, clients and law enforcement.
concepts.bodyHtml: The plan and process for detecting, containing, investigating and recovering from an operational or security incident, including decisions on escalation and notification of regulators, clients and law enforcement.

concepts.shortDefinition: Costs that arise only in certain conditions, such as performance fees and carried interest, shown separately in the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID).
concepts.bodyHtml: Costs that arise only in certain conditions, such as performance fees and carried interest, shown separately in the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID).

concepts.shortDefinition: Investment advice that, under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), is based on a sufficiently wide range of products.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investment advice that, under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), is based on a sufficiently wide range of products. A firm giving it may not keep inducements from fund managers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A director who has no relationship with the promoter, manager or service providers that could affect his or her judgement.
concepts.bodyHtml: A director who has no relationship with the promoter, manager or service providers that could affect his or her judgement. The Irish Funds Corporate Governance Code provides for at least one, and the Association Luxembourgeoise des Fonds d’Investissement (ALFI) Code of Conduct recommends at least one; under CP86 an independent director takes the organisational effectiveness role.

concepts.shortDefinition: The requirement under Article 19 of the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) that an AIF’s assets be valued properly and independently, either by an external valuer or by the AIFM itself if the valuation task is functionally independent from portfolio management.
concepts.bodyHtml: The requirement under Article 19 of the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) that an AIF’s assets be valued properly and independently, either by an external valuer or by the AIFM itself if the valuation task is functionally independent from portfolio management.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that seeks to replicate the performance of a market index by holding all, or a representative sample, of its constituents or by using derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that seeks to replicate the performance of a market index by holding all, or a representative sample, of its constituents or by using derivatives. Also called a tracker fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that reads blockchain data and organises it into databases that applications can search quickly, such as balances and transaction histories.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that reads blockchain data and organises it into databases that applications can search quickly, such as balances and transaction histories.

concepts.shortDefinition: An estimate of an exchange traded fund (ETF)’s NAV per share calculated and published at frequent intervals during the trading day, to help investors judge whether the market price is fair.
concepts.bodyHtml: An estimate of an exchange traded fund (ETF)’s NAV per share calculated and published at frequent intervals during the trading day, to help investors judge whether the market price is fair.

concepts.shortDefinition: Using a payment system through an account at a direct participant, usually a bank, rather than as a member.
concepts.bodyHtml: Using a payment system through an account at a direct participant, usually a bank, rather than as a member. Direct participants settle in the system themselves; indirect participants rely on their sponsor.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Irish framework introduced by the Central Bank (Individual Accountability Framework) Act 2023.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Irish framework introduced by the Central Bank (Individual Accountability Framework) Act 2023. Its conduct standards and enhanced fitness and probity rules have applied since 29 December 2023, including to fund management companies (FMCs) and funds; its Senior Executive Accountability Regime (SEAR) element does not apply to FMCs.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fee, commission or non-monetary benefit paid to or received by an intermediary from a third party, such as a fund manager, in connection with a service to a client.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fee, commission or non-monetary benefit paid to or received by an intermediary from a third party, such as a fund manager, in connection with a service to a client. The Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) restricts inducements and bans them for independent advice and portfolio management.

concepts.shortDefinition: The hardware, software, networks and data systems an organisation uses to process and communicate information.
concepts.bodyHtml: The hardware, software, networks and data systems an organisation uses to process and communicate information. In financial services, ICT risk is regulated in the EU by the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).

concepts.shortDefinition: Protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information.
concepts.bodyHtml: Protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information. ISO/IEC 27001 is the international standard for information security management systems.

concepts.shortDefinition: The use of computers, software and networks to store, process and transmit data.
concepts.bodyHtml: The use of computers, software and networks to store, process and transmit data. Often used interchangeably with information and communication technology (ICT).

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund, usually closed-ended and structured like a private equity fund, that invests in long-life assets such as transport, energy, utilities and digital infrastructure, typically through equity or debt in project companies.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund, usually closed-ended and structured like a private equity fund, that invests in long-life assets such as transport, energy, utilities and digital infrastructure, typically through equity or debt in project companies.

concepts.shortDefinition: Risk before controls are taken into account, usually rated by impact and likelihood.
concepts.bodyHtml: Risk before controls are taken into account, usually rated by impact and likelihood. A crypto custodian's inherent risk of theft is high by definition.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum capital a payment or e-money institution must hold at authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum capital a payment or e-money institution must hold at authorisation. Under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) it ranges from €20,000 for money remittance to €125,000 for most payment services; e-money institutions need €350,000. The Third Payment Services Directive (PSD3) raises these amounts.

concepts.shortDefinition: A sale of newly created tokens to the public to raise funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: A sale of newly created tokens to the public to raise funds. Variants include the initial exchange offering (IEO), run by an exchange for its users, and the initial DEX offering (IDO), run through a decentralised exchange or launchpad.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token sale run through a decentralised exchange or launchpad, where investors buy newly issued tokens directly with crypto-assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token sale run through a decentralised exchange or launchpad, where investors buy newly issued tokens directly with crypto-assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token sale run by a centralised crypto exchange for its users, with the exchange vetting the project and handling the sale.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token sale run by a centralised crypto exchange for its users, with the exchange vetting the project and handling the sale.

concepts.shortDefinition: The period at a fund’s launch during which units or shares are offered at a fixed initial offer price.
concepts.bodyHtml: The period at a fund’s launch during which units or shares are offered at a fixed initial offer price. Afterwards, they are issued at the NAV per share on each dealing day.

concepts.shortDefinition: The first sale of a company's shares to the public, usually with a listing on a stock exchange.
concepts.bodyHtml: The first sale of a company's shares to the public, usually with a listing on a stock exchange.

concepts.shortDefinition: A court order requiring a party to do, or more commonly to refrain from doing, something, for example to stop a breach of a contractual promise.
concepts.bodyHtml: A court order requiring a party to do, or more commonly to refrain from doing, something, for example to stop a breach of a contractual promise.

concepts.shortDefinition: Information of a precise nature, not made public, relating to an issuer or financial instrument, which would be likely to have a significant effect on its price if made public.
concepts.bodyHtml: Information of a precise nature, not made public, relating to an issuer or financial instrument, which would be likely to have a significant effect on its price if made public. Using or improperly disclosing it is prohibited.

concepts.shortDefinition: Using inside information to buy or sell, or cancel or amend an order for, a financial instrument or crypto-asset to which it relates, or recommending or inducing another person to do so.
concepts.bodyHtml: Using inside information to buy or sell, or cancel or amend an order for, a financial instrument or crypto-asset to which it relates, or recommending or inducing another person to do so.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of everyone with access to inside information about an issuer or crypto-asset, which issuers and those acting for them must keep under market abuse rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of everyone with access to inside information about an issuer or crypto-asset, which issuers and those acting for them must keep under market abuse rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The inability of a company to pay its debts as they fall due.
concepts.bodyHtml: The inability of a company to pay its debts as they fall due. A company can be insolvent even if its assets exceed its liabilities.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/886), which requires payment service providers that offer euro credit transfers to offer instant transfers, at no more than the price of standard transfers, and to provide a verification of payee service that checks the payee's name matches the account.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/886), which requires payment service providers that offer euro credit transfers to offer instant transfers, at no more than the price of standard transfers, and to provide a verification of payee service that checks the payee's name matches the account. The rules apply in stages, and payment and e-money institutions gain access to payment systems.

concepts.shortDefinition: An organisation, such as a pension scheme, insurer, bank, company or another fund, that invests on its own account or on behalf of others, usually in large amounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: An organisation, such as a pension scheme, insurer, bank, company or another fund, that invests on its own account or on behalf of others, usually in large amounts. Institutional investors are generally professional investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: Occupational pension schemes regulated under the EU IORP Directive (2016/2341), which sets governance, risk management and disclosure rules for workplace pension funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: Occupational pension schemes regulated under the EU IORP Directive (2016/2341), which sets governance, risk management and disclosure rules for workplace pension funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The constitutional document of an Irish collective asset-management vehicle (ICAV), equivalent to a company’s memorandum and articles of association.
concepts.bodyHtml: The constitutional document of an Irish collective asset-management vehicle (ICAV), equivalent to a company’s memorandum and articles of association.

concepts.shortDefinition: A reserve kept by a derivatives exchange to cover losses when a liquidated position cannot be closed at a price that covers its debt.
concepts.bodyHtml: A reserve kept by a derivatives exchange to cover losses when a liquidated position cannot be closed at a price that covers its debt. If the fund is exhausted, the exchange may use auto-deleveraging, forcibly closing profitable opposing positions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A design in which users state the outcome they want, such as swap A for at least X of B, and competing solvers find and execute the best route.
concepts.bodyHtml: A design in which users state the outcome they want, such as swap A for at least X of B, and competing solvers find and execute the best route. It can reduce maximal extractable value (MEV) but relies on solvers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A benchmark interest rate at which banks are assumed to lend to each other, such as Euro Interbank Offered Rate (EURIBOR).
concepts.bodyHtml: A benchmark interest rate at which banks are assumed to lend to each other, such as Euro Interbank Offered Rate (EURIBOR). The London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) has ceased and been replaced by risk-free rates.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fee paid by the acquirer to the card issuer on each card transaction.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fee paid by the acquirer to the card issuer on each card transaction. In the EU, interchange fees on consumer cards are capped at 0.2% of the transaction value for debit cards and 0.3% for credit cards.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2015/751), which caps interchange fees on consumer card transactions in the EU at 0.2% for debit and 0.3% for credit cards, and sets rules on card scheme and processing separation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2015/751), which caps interchange fees on consumer card transactions in the EU at 0.2% for debit and 0.3% for credit cards, and sets rules on card scheme and processing separation. The UK retained it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that stands between an investor and a fund or issuer, such as a financial adviser, bank, broker, platform or wealth manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that stands between an investor and a fund or issuer, such as a financial adviser, bank, broker, platform or wealth manager. In financial markets the main intermediaries are investment banks and broker-dealers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The function that provides independent assurance to management and the board on the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management and governance.
concepts.bodyHtml: The function that provides independent assurance to management and the board on the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management and governance. Company law does not require it, but UCITS and alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) rules do in certain cases; it is the third line of defence.

concepts.term: Internal capital adequacy and risk assessment
concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which an investment firm assesses the capital and liquid assets it needs for its risks and for an orderly wind-down, and documents the results for its board and regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which an investment firm assesses the capital and liquid assets it needs for its risks and for an orderly wind-down, and documents the results for its board and regulator.
concepts.sortKey: internal capital adequacy and risk assessment

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank's own assessment of the capital it needs to cover its risks, reviewed by supervisors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank's own assessment of the capital it needs to cover its risks, reviewed by supervisors. The equivalent for liquidity is the ILAAP. Investment firms use the internal capital adequacy and risk assessment (ICARA) instead.

concepts.shortDefinition: A centralised platform's own record of customer balances.
concepts.bodyHtml: A centralised platform's own record of customer balances. Customers hold a claim on the platform, not coins recorded in their own name on the blockchain.

concepts.shortDefinition: The global standard setter for insurance supervision.
concepts.bodyHtml: The global standard setter for insurance supervision. It sets the Insurance Core Principles and the Insurance Capital Standard for internationally active insurance groups.

concepts.shortDefinition: A standard format for identifying a bank account across borders, made up of a country code, check digits and the domestic account number.
concepts.bodyHtml: A standard format for identifying a bank account across borders, made up of a country code, check digits and the domestic account number. It is used for the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payments and many international transfers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A central securities depository (CSD) that settles internationally traded securities, such as eurobonds, across many markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A central securities depository (CSD) that settles internationally traded securities, such as eurobonds, across many markets. Many Irish exchange traded funds (ETFs) settle through an ICSD, which allows a share class to be cross-listed on several exchanges and settled in a single pool.

concepts.shortDefinition: The accounting standards issued by the International Accounting Standards Board and used by listed companies in the EU and many other countries.
concepts.bodyHtml: The accounting standards issued by the International Accounting Standards Board and used by listed companies in the EU and many other countries. The IFRS Foundation also oversees the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)'s sustainability disclosure standards.

concepts.shortDefinition: The International Investment Funds Association, a global body of national investment fund associations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The International Investment Funds Association, a global body of national investment fund associations. It represents the regulated fund industry in dialogue with international standard setters such as the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) and the Financial Stability Board (FSB).

concepts.shortDefinition: The International Monetary Fund, which promotes global monetary cooperation and financial stability.
concepts.bodyHtml: The International Monetary Fund, which promotes global monetary cooperation and financial stability. It assesses countries' financial sectors and anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) regimes and has published policy guidance on crypto-assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: International Organization of Securities Commissions: 18 crypto and digital-asset recommendations (November 2023) and nine on decentralised finance (DeFi) (December 2023) — conflicts, market abuse, custody, retail distribution, cooperation.
concepts.bodyHtml: International Organization of Securities Commissions: 18 crypto and digital-asset recommendations (November 2023) and nine on decentralised finance (DeFi) (December 2023) — conflicts, market abuse, custody, retail distribution, cooperation.

concepts.shortDefinition: International Standard on Assurance Engagements, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board.
concepts.bodyHtml: International Standard on Assurance Engagements, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. ISAE 3402 covers assurance reports on a service organisation's controls, the international counterpart of the US SOC 1 report.

concepts.shortDefinition: The board, set up by the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Foundation, that issues global sustainability disclosure standards, IFRS S1 (general requirements) and IFRS S2 (climate-related disclosures).
concepts.bodyHtml: The board, set up by the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Foundation, that issues global sustainability disclosure standards, IFRS S1 (general requirements) and IFRS S2 (climate-related disclosures).

concepts.shortDefinition: The International Swaps and Derivatives Association, the trade body for over-the-counter derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: The International Swaps and Derivatives Association, the trade body for over-the-counter derivatives. Its ISDA Master Agreement is the standard contract for most over the counter (OTC) derivative trades.

concepts.shortDefinition: Internet Protocol: the rules that route data between computers on the internet.
concepts.bodyHtml: Internet Protocol: the rules that route data between computers on the internet. An IP address identifies a device or network; crypto firms use IP data to detect sanctions evasion and fraud.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ability of different blockchains, or of blockchains and traditional systems, to exchange data and value.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ability of different blockchains, or of blockchains and traditional systems, to exchange data and value. It relies on bridges, messaging protocols and common standards, each of which brings its own risks.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US registered closed-end fund that offers to repurchase a set percentage of its shares at regular intervals, providing limited liquidity for less liquid assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US registered closed-end fund that offers to repurchase a set percentage of its shares at regular intervals, providing limited liquidity for less liquid assets. Tender offer funds offer repurchases at the board's discretion.

concepts.shortDefinition: The common data standard for Travel Rule messages, so that different networks (TRP, TRUST, Sygna Bridge, Notabene) describe originators and beneficiaries the same way.
concepts.bodyHtml: The common data standard for Travel Rule messages, so that different networks (TRP, TRUST, Sygna Bridge, Notabene) describe originators and beneficiaries the same way.

concepts.shortDefinition: Outsourcing to another company in the same group.
concepts.bodyHtml: Outsourcing to another company in the same group. It is subject to outsourcing rules, though risks may be managed differently because the firm has more control.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), the provision of a personal recommendation to a client in respect of transactions in financial instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), the provision of a personal recommendation to a client in respect of transactions in financial instruments. A firm giving advice must assess suitability.

concepts.shortDefinition: A breach of a fund's investment limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: A breach of a fund's investment limits. An active breach results from the manager's actions and must be corrected immediately, usually with compensation for any loss; a passive breach results from market movements or redemptions and must be corrected within a reasonable time in investors' interests.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish public limited company established as a fund under Part 24 of the Companies Act 2014, usually with variable capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish public limited company established as a fund under Part 24 of the Companies Act 2014, usually with variable capital. It may be a UCITS or an alternative investment fund (AIF) and may be an umbrella with segregated liability.

concepts.shortDefinition: The main US law regulating investment companies, including mutual funds, closed-end funds and exchange traded funds (ETFs), covering registration, governance, leverage, custody and affiliated transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The main US law regulating investment companies, including mutual funds, closed-end funds and exchange traded funds (ETFs), covering registration, governance, leverage, custody and affiliated transactions. Private funds generally rely on exemptions from it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Investment Company Institute, the association representing regulated investment funds in the United States and, through ICI Global, internationally.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Investment Company Institute, the association representing regulated investment funds in the United States and, through ICI Global, internationally. It publishes industry research and statistics.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation and directive (Regulation (EU) 2019/2033 and Directive (EU) 2019/2034), which set the prudential rules for most the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID) investment firms, scaling capital and liquidity requirements to the risks a firm poses to clients, markets and itself.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation and directive (Regulation (EU) 2019/2033 and Directive (EU) 2019/2034), which set the prudential rules for most the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID) investment firms, scaling capital and liquidity requirements to the risks a firm poses to clients, markets and itself. The largest firms remain under the bank rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: A vehicle that pools the money of multiple investors and invests it collectively in assets, such as shares and bonds, for their mutual benefit, under a defined investment policy.
concepts.bodyHtml: A vehicle that pools the money of multiple investors and invests it collectively in assets, such as shares and bonds, for their mutual benefit, under a defined investment policy. Also called a mutual fund, collective investment undertaking, collective investment scheme or pooled investment vehicle.

concepts.shortDefinition: Instructions from a fund’s manager or directors to the investment manager about the nature or mode of acquisition of investments, in addition to the objective, policies and restrictions in the prospectus – for example, limiting the proportion of non-base currency assets that may be hedged.
concepts.bodyHtml: Instructions from a fund’s manager or directors to the investment manager about the nature or mode of acquisition of investments, in addition to the objective, policies and restrictions in the prospectus – for example, limiting the proportion of non-base currency assets that may be hedged.

concepts.shortDefinition: Irish legislation regulating investment business firms and intermediaries.
concepts.bodyHtml: Irish legislation regulating investment business firms and intermediaries. Much of its scope has been replaced by rules implementing the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID), but it still applies to certain intermediaries.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Irish limited partnership fund vehicle.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Irish limited partnership fund vehicle. It can only be an alternative investment fund (AIF) (a retail investor AIF (RIAIF) or qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF)) and is mostly used for closed-ended private equity, infrastructure and similar funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The combination of portfolio management and risk management, which is the core function of a management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) and is often delegated in part to an investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: The combination of portfolio management and risk management, which is the core function of a management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) and is often delegated in part to an investment manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract appointing an investment manager, setting out how the fund’s portfolio is to be managed and invested and the operational terms of the service, such as dealing, delegation, fees and reporting.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract appointing an investment manager, setting out how the fund’s portfolio is to be managed and invested and the operational terms of the service, such as dealing, delegation, fees and reporting. Also called the investment mandate.

concepts.shortDefinition: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)'s standing committee on investment management.
concepts.bodyHtml: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)'s standing committee on investment management. It prepares ESMA's work on UCITS, the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), money market funds and related fund rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm that manages the fund’s portfolio and takes investment decisions on which assets to buy and sell, within the fund’s investment objective, policies and restrictions, usually under a delegation from the management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM).
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm that manages the fund’s portfolio and takes investment decisions on which assets to buy and sell, within the fund’s investment objective, policies and restrictions, usually under a delegation from the management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM).

concepts.shortDefinition: The fundamental aim of a fund, set out in its prospectus, for example long-term capital growth or a high level of income, usually indicating the main types of asset and markets in which it will invest.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fundamental aim of a fund, set out in its prospectus, for example long-term capital growth or a high level of income, usually indicating the main types of asset and markets in which it will invest.

concepts.shortDefinition: The period, usually several years, during which a closed-ended fund such as a private equity fund makes new investments and draws down commitments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The period, usually several years, during which a closed-ended fund such as a private equity fund makes new investments and draws down commitments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that lets investors or advisers buy, hold and switch funds and other investments in one account, usually holding them through a nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that lets investors or advisers buy, hold and switch funds and other investments in one account, usually holding them through a nominee.

concepts.shortDefinition: The detailed description in a fund’s prospectus of how the investment manager will try to achieve the investment objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: The detailed description in a fund’s prospectus of how the investment manager will try to achieve the investment objective.

concepts.shortDefinition: The way in which a portfolio manager executes a fund’s investment strategy, made up of asset allocation, security selection, portfolio construction and risk control.
concepts.bodyHtml: The way in which a portfolio manager executes a fund’s investment strategy, made up of asset allocation, security selection, portfolio construction and risk control.

concepts.shortDefinition: Limits on a fund’s powers of investment, such as the maximum exposure to one issuer or the maximum leverage, imposed by regulation, the fund documents, a stock exchange or the fund’s directors, to limit its exposure to risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: Limits on a fund’s powers of investment, such as the maximum exposure to one issuer or the maximum leverage, imposed by regulation, the fund documents, a stock exchange or the fund’s directors, to limit its exposure to risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The gain or loss on an investment over a period, from income and capital growth, expressed as a percentage of the amount invested.
concepts.bodyHtml: The gain or loss on an investment over a period, from income and capital growth, expressed as a percentage of the amount invested.

concepts.shortDefinition: Fraud in which victims are persuaded to invest in fake opportunities, often crypto-related.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fraud in which victims are persuaded to invest in fake opportunities, often crypto-related. In romance or relationship investment scams the fraudster builds trust over weeks or months before steering the victim to a fake platform.

concepts.shortDefinition: The services regulated by the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), including reception and transmission of orders, execution of orders, dealing on own account, portfolio management, investment advice and placing of financial instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The services regulated by the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), including reception and transmission of orders, execution of orders, dealing on own account, portfolio management, investment advice and placing of financial instruments.

concepts.shortDefinition: The approach a fund’s manager takes to achieve its investment objective, such as active or passive management, income or growth, or a particular asset class, region or theme.
concepts.bodyHtml: The approach a fund’s manager takes to achieve its investment objective, such as active or passive management, income or growth, or a particular asset class, region or theme.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK closed-ended investment company whose shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange, so that investors can exit by selling to other investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK closed-ended investment company whose shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange, so that investors can exit by selling to other investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Irish regime under which funds are not taxed on their income or gains but may have to deduct tax on payments to Irish-resident investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Irish regime under which funds are not taxed on their income or gains but may have to deduct tax on payments to Irish-resident investors. Non-Irish investors are generally exempt if they make the required declaration.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Investor Compensation Company DAC, the body that runs Ireland's investor compensation scheme.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Investor Compensation Company DAC, the body that runs Ireland's investor compensation scheme. It pays compensation, within limits, when an investment firm fails and cannot return clients' money or investments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A scheme that compensates clients of a failed investment firm that cannot return their money or assets, up to a limit.
concepts.bodyHtml: A scheme that compensates clients of a failed investment firm that cannot return their money or assets, up to a limit. It does not cover falls in market value. Ireland’s scheme pays 90% of a net loss up to €20,000.

concepts.shortDefinition: The information an AIFM must make available to investors before they invest in an AIF under Article 23 of the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), such as its strategy, risks, leverage, parties, valuation, liquidity management, liquidity management tools (LMTs), fees and performance, together with material changes and periodic disclosures.
concepts.bodyHtml: The information an AIFM must make available to investors before they invest in an AIF under Article 23 of the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), such as its strategy, risks, leverage, parties, valuation, liquidity management, liquidity management tools (LMTs), fees and performance, together with material changes and periodic disclosures.

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules that protect investors, such as product restrictions, disclosure, conduct rules and independent safekeeping of assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules that protect investors, such as product restrictions, disclosure, conduct rules and independent safekeeping of assets. Its level depends on the category of investor, with retail investors receiving the most.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish corporate fund vehicle with variable capital, established under the ICAV Act 2015 specifically for investment funds and registered and supervised by the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI).
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish corporate fund vehicle with variable capital, established under the ICAV Act 2015 specifically for investment funds and registered and supervised by the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI). It may be a UCITS or an alternative investment fund (AIF), can be an umbrella with segregated liability, may dispense with its annual general meeting (AGM) and can elect to be treated as transparent for US tax purposes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standard contract published by the International Swaps and Derivatives Association under which most over the counter (OTC) derivatives are documented.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standard contract published by the International Swaps and Derivatives Association under which most over the counter (OTC) derivatives are documented. Its annexes, such as a Credit Support Annex, set out the collateral or security a fund provides.

concepts.term: Isle of Man Financial Services Authority
concepts.shortDefinition: The financial services regulator of the Isle of Man, a Crown Dependency.
concepts.bodyHtml: The financial services regulator of the Isle of Man, a Crown Dependency. It regulates banking, investment, insurance, pensions and corporate and trust services, and supervises anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance.
