concepts.sortKey: isle of man financial services authority

concepts.shortDefinition: The international messaging standard for financial messages, which carries richer, structured data than older formats.
concepts.bodyHtml: The international messaging standard for financial messages, which carries richer, structured data than older formats. Major payment systems and SWIFT have migrated to it, supporting better screening and the revised the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) travel rule.

concepts.shortDefinition: A decentralised finance (DeFi) lending design in which each market has its own collateral and borrowed asset, so a problem in one market does not spread to others, unlike pooled designs.
concepts.bodyHtml: A decentralised finance (DeFi) lending design in which each market has its own collateral and borrowed asset, so a problem in one market does not spread to others, unlike pooled designs.

concepts.shortDefinition: The typical return pattern of a private equity fund: negative in the early years, as fees are paid before investments mature, and rising later as investments are realised.
concepts.bodyHtml: The typical return pattern of a private equity fund: negative in the early years, as fees are paid before investments mature, and rising later as investments are realised.

concepts.shortDefinition: The financial services regulator of Jersey, a Crown Dependency.
concepts.bodyHtml: The financial services regulator of Jersey, a Crown Dependency. It supervises banking, funds, investment business, trust and company services, insurance and money services, and is the island's anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) supervisor.

concepts.term: Joint Committee of the European Supervisory Authorities
concepts.shortDefinition: The forum through which the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the European Banking Authority (EBA) and the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) coordinate on cross-sector issues, including packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) key information documents, sustainability disclosures under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure…
concepts.bodyHtml: The forum through which the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the European Banking Authority (EBA) and the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) coordinate on cross-sector issues, including packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) key information documents, sustainability disclosures under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), financial conglomerates, anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) and the oversight of critical information and communication technology (ICT) third-party providers under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).
concepts.sortKey: joint committee of the european supervisory authorities

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the EU Investment Firms Regulation and the UK's equivalent regime, a measure of the risk an investment firm poses to clients, markets or itself, such as assets under management or client money held, used to calculate its capital requirement.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the EU Investment Firms Regulation and the UK's equivalent regime, a measure of the risk an investment firm poses to clients, markets or itself, such as assets under management or client money held, used to calculate its capital requirement.

concepts.shortDefinition: The German law that regulates investment funds and their managers, implementing the UCITS Directive and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) in Germany.
concepts.bodyHtml: The German law that regulates investment funds and their managers, implementing the UCITS Directive and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) in Germany.

concepts.shortDefinition: A German investment management company authorised under the kapitalanlagegesetzbuch (KAGB) to manage UCITS or alternative investment funds (AIFs).
concepts.bodyHtml: A German investment management company authorised under the kapitalanlagegesetzbuch (KAGB) to manage UCITS or alternative investment funds (AIFs).

concepts.shortDefinition: An automated agent that triggers protocol functions, such as liquidations or rebalances, usually in return for a fee or reward.
concepts.bodyHtml: An automated agent that triggers protocol functions, such as liquidations or rebalances, usually in return for a fee or reward.

concepts.shortDefinition: A scripted, witnessed and recorded procedure to generate, use, rotate or recover cryptographic keys.
concepts.bodyHtml: A scripted, witnessed and recorded procedure to generate, use, rotate or recover cryptographic keys. Good practice keeps the script, attendance record, video and signed minutes.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person, other than a member of the management body, who has significant influence over the direction of a regulated firm, such as the heads of risk management, compliance and internal audit, the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) and the CFO.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person, other than a member of the management body, who has significant influence over the direction of a regulated firm, such as the heads of risk management, compliance and internal audit, the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) and the CFO. Many EU and national regimes require their suitability to be assessed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standardised pre-contractual document of no more than three sides of A4 that must be given to retail investors in good time before they invest in a packaged retail and insurance-based investment product (PRIIP), including a UCITS or an alternative investment fund (AIF) sold to retail investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standardised pre-contractual document of no more than three sides of A4 that must be given to retail investors in good time before they invest in a packaged retail and insurance-based investment product (PRIIP), including a UCITS or an alternative investment fund (AIF) sold to retail investors. It explains the product, its risks (including the summary risk indicator (SRI)), four performance scenarios (stress, unfavourable, moderate and favourable) and costs.

concepts.shortDefinition: The short UCITS disclosure document introduced by UCITS IV.
concepts.bodyHtml: The short UCITS disclosure document introduced by UCITS IV. Since 1 January 2023 it has been replaced by the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID) for UCITS sold to retail investors and survives only where no KID is produced.

concepts.shortDefinition: A measurable value that shows how well an organisation or process is achieving a key objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: A measurable value that shows how well an organisation or process is achieving a key objective. Boards use KPIs to monitor performance and service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A term in a private fund's agreement that suspends new investments, or gives investors rights to end the investment period, if named individuals stop devoting enough time to the fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A term in a private fund's agreement that suspends new investments, or gives investors rights to end the investment period, if named individuals stop devoting enough time to the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A metric that signals a change in risk and can trigger an alert when it crosses a threshold, such as hot-wallet balances, failed withdrawals or reconciliation breaks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A metric that signals a change in risk and can trigger an alert when it crosses a threshold, such as hot-wallet balances, failed withdrawals or reconciliation breaks.

concepts.shortDefinition: Replacing cryptographic keys periodically or after a suspected compromise.
concepts.bodyHtml: Replacing cryptographic keys periodically or after a suspected compromise. For crypto custody it usually means moving assets to new addresses controlled by new keys.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dependence on one individual for decisions or know-how — a founder no one can challenge, or one engineer who knows key recovery.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dependence on one individual for decisions or know-how — a founder no one can challenge, or one engineer who knows key recovery.

concepts.shortDefinition: Know your customer: the process of identifying and verifying customers and understanding their activities, as part of customer due diligence under anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: Know your customer: the process of identifying and verifying customers and understanding their activities, as part of customer due diligence under anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: Poland's integrated financial supervisor, covering banks, insurers, capital markets, pension funds and payment institutions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Poland's integrated financial supervisor, covering banks, insurers, capital markets, pension funds and payment institutions.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent rating of rollups.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent rating of rollups. Stage 0: the operator can override. Stage 1: proofs are live but a security council can intervene. Stage 2: no override.

concepts.shortDefinition: An artificial intelligence (AI) model trained on very large amounts of text to understand and generate language.
concepts.bodyHtml: An artificial intelligence (AI) model trained on very large amounts of text to understand and generate language. LLMs power chatbots and generative AI tools and can be used as the reasoning engine of AI agents.

concepts.shortDefinition: Accepting an order to buy or sell fund shares after the dealing cut-off but processing it at that day's price.
concepts.bodyHtml: Accepting an order to buy or sell fund shares after the dealing cut-off but processing it at that day's price. It lets the investor benefit from information available after the cut-off, at the expense of other investors, and is prohibited.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that runs token sales for issuers, usually for a fee plus a share of the tokens.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that runs token sales for issuers, usually for a fee plus a share of the tokens. Providing services for an issuer's offer or sale is one of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) virtual asset activities; issuing tokens alone generally is not.

concepts.shortDefinition: Layer 0 connects chains; layer 1 is the base chain and final record; layer 2 executes transactions and settles to layer 1; layer 3 settles to a layer 2.
concepts.bodyHtml: Layer 0 connects chains; layer 1 is the base chain and final record; layer 2 executes transactions and settles to layer 1; layer 3 settles to a layer 2.

concepts.shortDefinition: A base blockchain, such as Bitcoin, Ethereum or Solana, that settles transactions itself.
concepts.bodyHtml: A base blockchain, such as Bitcoin, Ethereum or Solana, that settles transactions itself.

concepts.shortDefinition: A network built on top of a layer 1 that processes transactions more cheaply and posts the results, or proofs of them, back to the layer 1.
concepts.bodyHtml: A network built on top of a layer 1 that processes transactions more cheaply and posts the results, or proofs of them, back to the layer 1. Rollups are the main type.

concepts.shortDefinition: A layer 2 is a network that processes transactions off a base blockchain and settles them back to it; a layer 3 is built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.
concepts.bodyHtml: A layer 2 is a network that processes transactions off a base blockchain and settles them back to it; a layer 3 is built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.

concepts.shortDefinition: A network built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.
concepts.bodyHtml: A network built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.

concepts.shortDefinition: The second stage of money laundering, in which funds are moved through many transactions to obscure their origin.
concepts.bodyHtml: The second stage of money laundering, in which funds are moved through many transactions to obscure their origin.

concepts.shortDefinition: North Korean state-linked hacking group; the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the Bybit theft to North Korea ("TraderTraitor").
concepts.bodyHtml: North Korean state-linked hacking group; the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the Bybit theft to North Korea ("TraderTraitor"). Its proceeds raise sanctions and proliferation-financing issues.

concepts.shortDefinition: A record of who owns what and who has paid whom.
concepts.bodyHtml: A record of who owns what and who has paid whom. A blockchain is a ledger shared and maintained by many participants rather than kept by one record-keeper.

concepts.shortDefinition: The law firm, sometimes called outside legal counsel, appointed to advise a fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The law firm, sometimes called outside legal counsel, appointed to advise a fund. It prepares applications to the regulator, drafts the constitutional documents and prospectus, negotiates service agreements, coordinates the launch and updates documents for later changes in law.

concepts.shortDefinition: The legal structure in which a fund is constituted: corporate, unit trust, contractual or limited partnership.
concepts.bodyHtml: The legal structure in which a fund is constituted: corporate, unit trust, contractual or limited partnership. It is distinct from the fund’s regulatory type (UCITS or alternative investment fund (AIF)).

concepts.shortDefinition: The person registered as the owner of an asset or in possession of it, who may hold it for the benefit of a different beneficial owner, such as a trustee or nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person registered as the owner of an asset or in possession of it, who may hold it for the benefit of a different beneficial owner, such as a trustee or nominee.

concepts.shortDefinition: The legal capacity of an entity to own assets, enter into contracts and sue or be sued in its own name.
concepts.bodyHtml: The legal capacity of an entity to own assets, enter into contracts and sue or be sued in its own name. Corporate funds have it; unit trusts, contractual funds and most limited partnerships do not, so their management company (ManCo), trustee or general partner (GP) acts for them.

concepts.shortDefinition: The status of money that must, in general, be accepted in payment of debts.
concepts.bodyHtml: The status of money that must, in general, be accepted in payment of debts. In the euro area, euro banknotes and coins are legal tender, and the proposed digital euro would be too.

concepts.shortDefinition: A central bank's power to lend to solvent but illiquid institutions in a crisis.
concepts.bodyHtml: A central bank's power to lend to solvent but illiquid institutions in a crisis. Stablecoin issuers have no lender of last resort, so their reserves must be safe and liquid by design, as the circle US dollar stablecoin (USDC) depeg during the Silicon Valley Bank failure (March 2023) showed.

concepts.shortDefinition: A decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol in which users supply crypto-assets to pools to earn interest and others borrow from the pools against over-collateralised positions, with interest rates set by algorithm and automatic liquidations.
concepts.bodyHtml: A decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol in which users supply crypto-assets to pools to earn interest and others borrow from the pools against over-collateralised positions, with interest rates set by algorithm and automatic liquidations.

concepts.shortDefinition: A management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) that has delegated so much, or retains so little expertise, resources or decision-making power, that it can no longer be considered the manager of the fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) that has delegated so much, or retains so little expertise, resources or decision-making power, that it can no longer be considered the manager of the fund. Regulation prohibits a manager from becoming one.

concepts.shortDefinition: The layers of EU financial regulation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The layers of EU financial regulation. Level 1 is the directive or regulation agreed by the Parliament and Council. Level 2 is the detailed delegated and implementing acts adopted by the Commission, often based on technical standards drafted by the European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs). Level 3 is guidelines and questions and answerses (Q&As) from the ESAs.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the fair value hierarchy in accounting standards, an asset valued using significant unobservable inputs, such as a model with management assumptions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the fair value hierarchy in accounting standards, an asset valued using significant unobservable inputs, such as a model with management assumptions. Level 1 assets have quoted prices in active markets; Level 2 assets use observable inputs.

concepts.shortDefinition: Any method by which a fund increases its exposure beyond its NAV, whether through borrowing cash or securities, or leverage embedded in derivative positions or by any other means.
concepts.bodyHtml: Any method by which a fund increases its exposure beyond its NAV, whether through borrowing cash or securities, or leverage embedded in derivative positions or by any other means. It magnifies both gains and losses. Also called gearing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Card scheme rules that move fraud liability from the merchant to the issuer when a transaction is authenticated with 3-D Secure or processed with chip and PIN.
concepts.bodyHtml: Card scheme rules that move fraud liability from the merchant to the issuer when a transaction is authenticated with 3-D Secure or processed with chip and PIN.

concepts.shortDefinition: Lido staked ether: a liquid staking token issued by the Lido protocol in exchange for ether deposited for staking.
concepts.bodyHtml: Lido staked ether: a liquid staking token issued by the Lido protocol in exchange for ether deposited for staking. It earns staking rewards and can be traded or used in decentralised finance (DeFi).

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a creditor in possession of a debtor’s asset to retain it until the debt is paid.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a creditor in possession of a debtor’s asset to retain it until the debt is paid. The holder generally cannot sell the asset and loses the lien if it parts with possession. Depositary agreements often give the fund depositary a lien.

concepts.shortDefinition: Bitcoin's payment-channel network: two on-chain transactions to open and close, many off-chain payments in between.
concepts.bodyHtml: Bitcoin's payment-channel network: two on-chain transactions to open and close, many off-chain payments in between.

concepts.shortDefinition: An open-ended fund that offers redemptions less frequently than normally required.
concepts.bodyHtml: An open-ended fund that offers redemptions less frequently than normally required. In Ireland, a retail investor AIF (RIAIF) offering less than monthly, or a qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF) less than quarterly, redemptions.

concepts.shortDefinition: An exclusion from payment and e-money regulation for instruments usable only within a limited network of service providers or for a very limited range of goods or services, such as store cards.
concepts.bodyHtml: An exclusion from payment and e-money regulation for instruments usable only within a limited network of service providers or for a very limited range of goods or services, such as store cards. Large networks must notify the regulator.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investor in a limited partnership, whose liability for its debts is generally limited to its capital contribution or commitment and who does not take part in managing it.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investor in a limited partnership, whose liability for its debts is generally limited to its capital contribution or commitment and who does not take part in managing it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A partnership with at least one general partner, which manages it and has unlimited liability, and limited partners, whose liability is limited to their capital contribution.
concepts.bodyHtml: A partnership with at least one general partner, which manages it and has unlimited liability, and limited partners, whose liability is limited to their capital contribution. Fund LPs can only be alternative investment funds (AIFs), are mostly closed-ended and are used for professional investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract governing a limited partnership fund, setting out its strategy, investment period, fees, carried interest, distributions, investor rights and the general partner's duties.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract governing a limited partnership fund, setting out its strategy, investment period, fees, carried interest, distributions, investor rights and the general partner's duties.

concepts.shortDefinition: A licence granted for a set period, or with limits on volumes, activities or client types, before a full licence is given (for example Bermuda's Class M licence).
concepts.bodyHtml: A licence granted for a set period, or with limits on volumes, activities or client types, before a full licence is given (for example Bermuda's Class M licence). The conditions act as the main controls while the firm builds a track record.

concepts.shortDefinition: The requirement under the EU Investment Firms Regulation and the UK MIFIDPRU regime for investment firms to hold liquid assets equal to at least one third of their fixed overheads requirement, with additional liquidity assessed through the internal capital adequacy and risk assessment (ICARA) in the UK.
concepts.bodyHtml: The requirement under the EU Investment Firms Regulation and the UK MIFIDPRU regime for investment firms to hold liquid assets equal to at least one third of their fixed overheads requirement, with additional liquidity assessed through the internal capital adequacy and risk assessment (ICARA) in the UK.

concepts.shortDefinition: A liquid restaking token: a tradable token representing assets restaked through a restaking protocol to secure additional services.
concepts.bodyHtml: A liquid restaking token: a tradable token representing assets restaked through a restaking protocol to secure additional services. It carries both the rewards and the extra slashing risk of restaking.

concepts.shortDefinition: Staking through a pool that issues a tradable receipt token (a liquid staking token) representing the staked asset and its rewards.
concepts.bodyHtml: Staking through a pool that issues a tradable receipt token (a liquid staking token) representing the staked asset and its rewards.

concepts.shortDefinition: A tradable receipt for staked tokens, such as lido staked ether (stETH) or cbETH, representing the staked asset and its rewards.
concepts.bodyHtml: A tradable receipt for staked tokens, such as lido staked ether (stETH) or cbETH, representing the staked asset and its rewards. It can trade below the value of the tokens behind it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process of winding up a company’s affairs, in which a liquidator realises its assets and distributes the proceeds to creditors and then members in a prescribed order.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process of winding up a company’s affairs, in which a liquidator realises its assets and distributes the proceeds to creditors and then members in a prescribed order. A liquidator cannot use property the company holds on trust or in a fiduciary capacity to pay its creditors. Also called winding up.

concepts.shortDefinition: The forced sale of a borrower's or trader's collateral when a loan or leveraged position falls below the required margin.
concepts.bodyHtml: The forced sale of a borrower's or trader's collateral when a loan or leveraged position falls below the required margin. In decentralised finance (DeFi) lending, the protocol does this automatically when a loan's health factor falls below 1, and liquidators are paid a bonus for doing so.

concepts.shortDefinition: In decentralised finance (DeFi) lending, the level of collateral value relative to debt at which a borrower's position becomes eligible for liquidation.
concepts.bodyHtml: In decentralised finance (DeFi) lending, the level of collateral value relative to debt at which a borrower's position becomes eligible for liquidation.

concepts.shortDefinition: The person appointed to wind up a company: to gather in and sell its assets, pay its creditors in a prescribed order and distribute any surplus to its members.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person appointed to wind up a company: to gather in and sell its assets, pay its creditors in a prescribed order and distribute any surplus to its members. A liquidator cannot use assets held on trust or in a fiduciary capacity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ease with which an asset can be turned into cash quickly without a significant loss of value.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ease with which an asset can be turned into cash quickly without a significant loss of value. Cash is the most liquid asset; real estate and loans are illiquid.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: How easily an asset can be bought or sold quickly without moving its price.

concepts.shortDefinition: Grouping a fund's assets by how quickly they could be sold without materially moving prices, for example within one day, two to seven days and so on, and comparing the result with the investors' redemption profile.
concepts.bodyHtml: Grouping a fund's assets by how quickly they could be sold without materially moving prices, for example within one day, two to seven days and so on, and comparing the result with the investors' redemption profile.

concepts.shortDefinition: Cash and liquid assets held by a fund to meet redemptions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Cash and liquid assets held by a fund to meet redemptions. Holding too much lowers returns, so it must be balanced against the fund’s dealing terms.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fee charged on redemptions to reflect the cost to the fund of providing liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fee charged on redemptions to reflect the cost to the fund of providing liquidity. Under the Money Market Funds Regulation (MMFR), a public debt constant net asset value (CNAV) or LVNAV MMF must consider or apply liquidity fees when its weekly maturing assets fall below set levels.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum share of reserves that must be available as cash within a set time — same day, five days, 30 days — sized to the worst observed outflow.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum share of reserves that must be available as cash within a set time — same day, five days, 30 days — sized to the worst observed outflow. The fix for a coin that is solvent but illiquid.

concepts.shortDefinition: A tool used to manage redemptions in an open-ended fund, such as suspension, redemption gates, extended notice periods, redemption in kind, redemption fees, swing pricing, dual pricing, anti-dilution levies and side pockets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A tool used to manage redemptions in an open-ended fund, such as suspension, redemption gates, extended notice periods, redemption in kind, redemption fees, swing pricing, dual pricing, anti-dilution levies and side pockets. Since 16 April 2026 UCITS and open-ended alternative investment funds (AIFs) must select at least two from the harmonised lists, other than suspension and side pockets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A difference between how often investors can redeem from a fund and how quickly its assets can be sold without loss.
concepts.bodyHtml: A difference between how often investors can redeem from a fund and how quickly its assets can be sold without loss.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Tokens that move 24/7 over assets that take days or months to sell. The FSB's first tokenisation vulnerability: run risk where the token looks more liquid than the asset.

concepts.shortDefinition: A pool of tokens locked in a smart contract that traders swap against, or borrowers borrow from.
concepts.bodyHtml: A pool of tokens locked in a smart contract that traders swap against, or borrowers borrow from. Liquidity providers deposit the tokens and earn fees or interest.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person or firm that deposits tokens into an automated market maker (AMM) pool, or quotes prices, so that others can trade.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person or firm that deposits tokens into an automated market maker (AMM) pool, or quotes prices, so that others can trade.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that a fund cannot sell assets quickly enough, or at a fair price, to meet redemptions or other obligations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that a fund cannot sell assets quickly enough, or at a fair price, to meet redemptions or other obligations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which a manager keeps a fund’s liquidity consistent with its redemption terms, including setting dealing terms, holding liquid assets, monitoring the investor base and liquidity stress testing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which a manager keeps a fund’s liquidity consistent with its redemption terms, including setting dealing terms, holding liquid assets, monitoring the investor base and liquidity stress testing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Testing how a fund’s liquidity would cope with severe but plausible conditions, such as large redemptions or falling market liquidity, in line with the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) guidelines.
concepts.bodyHtml: Testing how a fund’s liquidity would cope with severe but plausible conditions, such as large redemptions or falling market liquidity, in line with the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) guidelines.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that arranges the admission of a fund’s shares, such as exchange traded fund (ETF) shares, to trading on a stock exchange.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that arranges the admission of a fund’s shares, such as exchange traded fund (ETF) shares, to trading on a stock exchange.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native coin of Litecoin, a proof-of-work cryptocurrency launched in 2011 as a faster, lighter variant of Bitcoin.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native coin of Litecoin, a proof-of-work cryptocurrency launched in 2011 as a faster, lighter variant of Bitcoin.

concepts.shortDefinition: Checks in remote identity verification that confirm a real person is present, rather than a photo, video, mask or deepfake.
concepts.bodyHtml: Checks in remote identity verification that confirm a real person is present, rather than a photo, video, mask or deepfake.

concepts.shortDefinition: Granting a loan directly as original lender, or indirectly through a third party or special purpose vehicle.
concepts.bodyHtml: Granting a loan directly as original lender, or indirectly through a third party or special purpose vehicle. UCITS may not grant loans.

concepts.shortDefinition: An alternative investment fund (AIF) whose strategy is mainly to originate loans, or whose originated loans have a notional value of at least 50% of its NAV.
concepts.bodyHtml: An alternative investment fund (AIF) whose strategy is mainly to originate loans, or whose originated loans have a notional value of at least 50% of its NAV. Under AIFMD II it must retain 5% of the notional value of loans it sells, its leverage is capped at 175% (open-ended) or 300% (closed-ended), and it must be closed-ended unless its manager can show that its liquidity management is compatible with open-ended redemption.

concepts.shortDefinition: A former category of Irish qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF) permitted to originate loans.
concepts.bodyHtml: A former category of Irish qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF) permitted to originate loans. The revised AIF Rulebook removed it on 5 May 2026, and Irish alternative investment funds (AIFs) that originate loans now follow the AIFMD II rules.
concepts.notes: Ireland; replaced by the AIFMD II loan origination rules

concepts.shortDefinition: The ratio of a loan to the value of the collateral securing it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ratio of a loan to the value of the collateral securing it. Decentralised finance (DeFi) lending protocols set a maximum loan-to-value for each type of collateral.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person a foreign fund must appoint in some countries where it is marketed, for example to handle investor requests and payments, provide documents or act as contact with the regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person a foreign fund must appoint in some countries where it is marketed, for example to handle investor requests and payments, provide documents or act as contact with the regulator. EU rules since 2021 let funds provide many facilities electronically instead.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bridge design in which tokens are locked in a contract on one blockchain and an equivalent wrapped token is minted on another.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bridge design in which tokens are locked in a contract on one blockchain and an equivalent wrapped token is minted on another. The wrapped token is only as safe as the bridge holding the locked tokens.

concepts.shortDefinition: A period after investing during which an investor may not redeem from a fund, common in hedge funds and in closed-ended or limited liquidity alternative investment funds (AIFs).
concepts.bodyHtml: A period after investing during which an investor may not redeem from a fund, common in hedge funds and in closed-ended or limited liquidity alternative investment funds (AIFs).

concepts.shortDefinition: A benchmark interest rate for interbank lending in several currencies.
concepts.bodyHtml: A benchmark interest rate for interbank lending in several currencies. It was discontinued after manipulation scandals and replaced by risk-free rates such as Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) and Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR); the final settings ended in 2023.

concepts.shortDefinition: The London Stock Exchange Group, which operates the London Stock Exchange and provides market data, indices and clearing services.
concepts.bodyHtml: The London Stock Exchange Group, which operates the London Stock Exchange and provides market data, indices and clearing services.

concepts.shortDefinition: Quantum attacks on public keys already visible on-chain (long), or on a key revealed while a transaction waits to be confirmed (short).
concepts.bodyHtml: Quantum attacks on public keys already visible on-chain (long), or on a key revealed while a transaction waits to be confirmed (short).

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK authorised open-ended fund designed to invest in long-term, illiquid assets such as private equity, private credit, infrastructure and property, with dealing no more often than monthly and a notice period of at least 90 days.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK authorised open-ended fund designed to invest in long-term, illiquid assets such as private equity, private credit, infrastructure and property, with dealing no more often than monthly and a notice period of at least 90 days.

concepts.shortDefinition: A hedge fund strategy that buys shares expected to rise and sells short those expected to fall, aiming to profit from stock selection while reducing exposure to the market as a whole.
concepts.bodyHtml: A hedge fund strategy that buys shares expected to rise and sells short those expected to fall, aiming to profit from stock selection while reducing exposure to the market as a whole.

concepts.shortDefinition: Considering the underlying exposure of an instrument rather than only its legal form.
concepts.bodyHtml: Considering the underlying exposure of an instrument rather than only its legal form. The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has advised a stricter look-through test so that a UCITS cannot use instruments such as exchange-traded notes to gain significant exposure to assets it could not hold directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: An incident that caused a financial loss or other harm, such as a processing error or fraud.
concepts.bodyHtml: An incident that caused a financial loss or other harm, such as a processing error or fraud. Recording loss events and near misses helps firms understand operational risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: A type of money market fund under the EU Money Market Funds Regulation whose share price can stay constant as long as the value of its assets stays within 0.2% of that price.
concepts.bodyHtml: A type of money market fund under the EU Money Market Funds Regulation whose share price can stay constant as long as the value of its assets stays within 0.2% of that price. It can use amortised cost only for assets maturing within 75 days.

concepts.term: Low volatility net asset value MMF
concepts.shortDefinition: A money market fund (MMF) permitted to deal at a constant NAV, using amortised cost for assets maturing within 75 days, while that NAV stays within 20 basis points of its mark-to-market NAV.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money market fund (MMF) permitted to deal at a constant NAV, using amortised cost for assets maturing within 75 days, while that NAV stays within 20 basis points of its mark-to-market NAV.
concepts.sortKey: low volatility net asset value mmf

concepts.shortDefinition: A committee of representatives of a private fund's largest investors that reviews conflicts of interest, valuation questions and other matters reserved to it by the partnership agreement.
concepts.bodyHtml: A committee of representatives of a private fund's largest investors that reviews conflicts of interest, valuation questions and other matters reserved to it by the partnership agreement. It is advisory and does not manage the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Luxembourg Stock Exchange, a major listing venue for bonds and investment funds and home to the Luxembourg Green Exchange for sustainable securities.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Luxembourg Stock Exchange, a major listing venue for bonds and investment funds and home to the Luxembourg Green Exchange for sustainable securities.

concepts.shortDefinition: A branch of artificial intelligence in which systems learn patterns from data rather than following explicit rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: A branch of artificial intelligence in which systems learn patterns from data rather than following explicit rules. In finance it is used for fraud detection, credit scoring, trading and anti-money laundering (AML) monitoring.

concepts.shortDefinition: The live production version of a blockchain on which real assets are transacted.
concepts.bodyHtml: The live production version of a blockchain on which real assets are transacted. A testnet is a separate network using tokens with no value, for testing software before release on mainnet.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), an ICT-related incident that has a high adverse impact on the network and information systems that support critical or important functions of a financial entity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), an ICT-related incident that has a high adverse impact on the network and information systems that support critical or important functions of a financial entity. It must be classified using set criteria and reported to the regulator within strict deadlines.

concepts.shortDefinition: The obligation to report serious operational or security incidents to the regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: The obligation to report serious operational or security incidents to the regulator. In the EU, payment institutions now report ICT-related incidents under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) rather than the earlier the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) guidelines.

concepts.shortDefinition: The sanctions prohibition on providing funds or economic resources, directly or indirectly, to or for the benefit of a designated person.
concepts.bodyHtml: The sanctions prohibition on providing funds or economic resources, directly or indirectly, to or for the benefit of a designated person. It goes beyond freezing assets the person already holds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Malta's single financial services regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Malta's single financial services regulator. It supervises banks, insurers, investment services firms, funds, payment and e-money institutions and crypto-asset service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: Reducing or cancelling unvested variable pay because of misconduct, poor performance or risk failures.
concepts.bodyHtml: Reducing or cancelling unvested variable pay because of misconduct, poor performance or risk failures. Clawback goes further, recovering pay already received.

concepts.shortDefinition: In EU financial regulation, the body or bodies that set a firm's strategy, objectives and overall direction and oversee and monitor management decision-making.
concepts.bodyHtml: In EU financial regulation, the body or bodies that set a firm's strategy, objectives and overall direction and oversee and monitor management decision-making. It includes both the management and supervisory functions, such as the executive and non-executive directors of a board.

concepts.shortDefinition: The acquisition of a company by an external management team, which replaces the incumbent management, often financed by a private equity fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The acquisition of a company by an external management team, which replaces the incumbent management, often financed by a private equity fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The acquisition of a company by its existing management team, often financed by a private equity fund and debt.
concepts.bodyHtml: The acquisition of a company by its existing management team, often financed by a private equity fund and debt.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entity responsible for the management of an externally managed fund, including investment management, administration and marketing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entity responsible for the management of an externally managed fund, including investment management, administration and marketing. In the EEA it is either a UCITS ManCo or an alternative investment fund manager (AIFM), and it retains regulatory responsibility for any tasks it delegates. A ManCo may be proprietary (part of the promoter's group) or third-party (independent, serving many promoters), and a super ManCo holds both UCITS and AIFM authorisations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The periodic fee, usually a percentage of NAV, paid from a fund’s assets to its manager for managing it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The periodic fee, usually a percentage of NAV, paid from a fund’s assets to its manager for managing it. It is the main part of a fund’s ongoing charges.

concepts.shortDefinition: An arrangement that reduces a private fund's management fee by some or all of the transaction, monitoring or director fees the manager or its affiliates receive from portfolio companies.
concepts.bodyHtml: An arrangement that reduces a private fund's management fee by some or all of the transaction, monitoring or director fees the manager or its affiliates receive from portfolio companies.

concepts.shortDefinition: The reports and data management provides to the board and senior managers to monitor the business, its risks and its controls.
concepts.bodyHtml: The reports and data management provides to the board and senior managers to monitor the business, its risks and its controls. Good MI is accurate, timely, concise and focused on trends and exceptions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A letter from the external auditor to management and the board setting out control weaknesses and recommendations found during the audit.
concepts.bodyHtml: A letter from the external auditor to management and the board setting out control weaknesses and recommendations found during the audit.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a UCITS management company (ManCo) or EEA alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) authorised in its home Member State to manage funds domiciled in another Member State, either directly or through a branch, after notifying its home regulator, without being authorised again.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a UCITS management company (ManCo) or EEA alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) authorised in its home Member State to manage funds domiciled in another Member State, either directly or through a branch, after notifying its home regulator, without being authorised again.

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules, drawn up by the management company (ManCo), that constitute a Luxembourg fonds commun de placement (FCP) and set out unitholders’ rights.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules, drawn up by the management company (ManCo), that constitute a Luxembourg fonds commun de placement (FCP) and set out unitholders’ rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under CP86, the six functions of an Irish fund management company (FMC) that must each be overseen by a designated person: investment management, fund risk management, operational risk management, regulatory compliance, distribution, and capital and financial management.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under CP86, the six functions of an Irish fund management company (FMC) that must each be overseen by a designated person: investment management, fund risk management, operational risk management, regulatory compliance, distribution, and capital and financial management.

concepts.shortDefinition: The authority a payer gives a payee and payment service provider to collect payments from the payer's account, for example for a direct debit or variable recurring payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The authority a payer gives a payee and payment service provider to collect payments from the payer's account, for example for a direct debit or variable recurring payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm that creates a financial product.
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm that creates a financial product. Under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) a manufacturer defines a target market; under the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Regulation the manufacturer of a fund, usually its management company (ManCo), produces the Key Information Document (KID).

concepts.shortDefinition: Collateral exchanged to cover exposure on derivatives, such as futures and over the counter (OTC) derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: Collateral exchanged to cover exposure on derivatives, such as futures and over the counter (OTC) derivatives. The European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) requires margin to be exchanged on many non-cleared OTC derivatives.

concepts.shortDefinition: Trading with borrowed funds or on a deposit (margin) so that positions exceed the trader's capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: Trading with borrowed funds or on a deposit (margin) so that positions exceed the trader's capital. Losses beyond the margin lead to liquidation; many regulators restrict or ban leveraged crypto products for retail clients.

concepts.shortDefinition: Valuing an asset at readily available closing prices from independent sources.
concepts.bodyHtml: Valuing an asset at readily available closing prices from independent sources. Where this is not possible, the asset is valued conservatively using a model based on market inputs (mark-to-model).

concepts.shortDefinition: Valuing an asset using a model based on market inputs where a readily available market price does not exist.
concepts.bodyHtml: Valuing an asset using a model based on market inputs where a readily available market price does not exist. The Money Market Funds Regulation (MMFR) requires it to be done conservatively.

concepts.shortDefinition: Insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of inside information and market manipulation.
concepts.bodyHtml: Insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of inside information and market manipulation. In the EU it is prohibited for financial instruments by the Market Abuse Regulation and for crypto-assets by Title VI of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 596/2014), which bans insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of inside information and market manipulation in financial instruments, and requires issuers to disclose inside information promptly.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 596/2014), which bans insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of inside information and market manipulation in financial instruments, and requires issuers to disclose inside information promptly. Similar rules for crypto-assets are in Title VI of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

concepts.shortDefinition: The circulating supply of a crypto-asset multiplied by its price.
concepts.bodyHtml: The circulating supply of a crypto-asset multiplied by its price. It can be misleading for tokens with small circulating supply or thin liquidity.

concepts.shortDefinition: European Commission proposals of 4 December 2025, not yet law, to integrate EU capital markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: European Commission proposals of 4 December 2025, not yet law, to integrate EU capital markets. For funds, they would allow notification of cross-border marketing at authorisation, stop gold-plating, change the pre-marketing rules, delete the UCITS Key Investor Information Document (KIID) obligation and give the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) a role in the supervision of large cross-border asset management groups. They would also give ESMA direct supervision of significant market infrastructures and of crypto-asset service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that undertakes to quote prices at which it will buy and sell a security continuously, providing liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that undertakes to quote prices at which it will buy and sell a security continuously, providing liquidity. Exchange traded fund (ETF) market makers quote two-way prices on exchange within a maximum spread.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A firm that continuously quotes buy and sell prices to provide liquidity, earning the spread.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that quotes buy and sell prices for a token, often paid by the issuer in borrowed tokens with call options.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that quotes buy and sell prices for a token, often paid by the issuer in borrowed tokens with call options. A legitimate service, but open to abuse through wash trading, as the US Operation Token Mirrors (2024) showed.

concepts.shortDefinition: Transactions, orders or behaviour that give false or misleading signals about supply, demand or price, secure an artificial price, use deception, or spread false or misleading information.
concepts.bodyHtml: Transactions, orders or behaviour that give false or misleading signals about supply, demand or price, secure an artificial price, use deception, or spread false or misleading information. Examples include wash trading, spoofing and pump-and-dump schemes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss from movements in market prices, such as interest rates, equity prices, commodity prices and exchange rates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss from movements in market prices, such as interest rates, equity prices, commodity prices and exchange rates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Monitoring orders and trades to detect market abuse such as insider dealing, spoofing and wash trading.
concepts.bodyHtml: Monitoring orders and trades to detect market abuse such as insider dealing, spoofing and wash trading. Crypto trading platforms and firms that arrange or execute transactions must have surveillance under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) and must report suspicions.

concepts.shortDefinition: Frequent short-term trading in and out of a fund to exploit stale prices, for example where a fund's NAV does not yet reflect market moves in other time zones.
concepts.bodyHtml: Frequent short-term trading in and out of a fund to exploit stale prices, for example where a fund's NAV does not yet reflect market moves in other time zones. It dilutes the returns of long-term investors and is controlled through fair value pricing, swing pricing and trading restrictions.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), a direct or indirect offering or placement, at the initiative of the AIFM or on its behalf, of units or shares of an AIF it manages to or with investors domiciled or with a registered office in the EEA.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), a direct or indirect offering or placement, at the initiative of the AIFM or on its behalf, of units or shares of an AIF it manages to or with investors domiciled or with a registered office in the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: Any message about a fund that promotes it, such as a fact sheet, advertisement, website or social media post.
concepts.bodyHtml: Any message about a fund that promotes it, such as a fact sheet, advertisement, website or social media post. Under the Cross-Border Distribution of Funds Regulation (CBDFR) and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) guidelines it must be identifiable as such, describe risks and rewards equally prominently, be fair, clear and not misleading, and be consistent with the prospectus and Key Information Document (KID).

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a UCITS to be marketed to retail and professional investors, and of an EEA AIF managed by an authorised EEA alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) to be marketed to professional investors, in other Member States after a notification procedure.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a UCITS to be marketed to retail and professional investors, and of an EEA AIF managed by an authorised EEA alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) to be marketed to professional investors, in other Member States after a notification procedure.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114), which has applied in full since 30 December 2024 and regulates issuers of, and service providers in, crypto-assets that are not financial instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114), which has applied in full since 30 December 2024 and regulates issuers of, and service providers in, crypto-assets that are not financial instruments. It does not regulate investment funds, and tokenised fund units fall outside it.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The EU Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114). Its stablecoin rules applied from 30 June 2024 and its rules for crypto-asset service providers from 30 December 2024. The transitional period for firms operating under earlier national regimes ended on 1 July 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU framework for investment services and activities, made up of Directive 2014/65/EU and the directly applicable the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation (MiFIR), which has applied since 3 January 2018.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU framework for investment services and activities, made up of Directive 2014/65/EU and the directly applicable the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation (MiFIR), which has applied since 3 January 2018. It covers portfolio management, advice and distribution of funds, including product governance, suitability, appropriateness and inducements.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 600/2014), which sits alongside the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II).
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 600/2014), which sits alongside the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II). It sets directly applicable rules on trade transparency, transaction reporting, trading obligations and product intervention.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund in a master-feeder structure into which one or more feeder funds invest and where the trading takes place.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund in a master-feeder structure into which one or more feeder funds invest and where the trading takes place. A master UCITS must have at least one feeder, cannot itself be a feeder and may not charge the feeder subscription or redemption fees.

concepts.shortDefinition: A structure in which one or more feeder funds, often domiciled in different jurisdictions, invest all or most of their assets in a single master fund, where the trading takes place.
concepts.bodyHtml: A structure in which one or more feeder funds, often domiciled in different jurisdictions, invest all or most of their assets in a single master fund, where the trading takes place.

concepts.shortDefinition: The system of a trading platform that matches buy and sell orders according to its rules, usually by price and then time.
concepts.bodyHtml: The system of a trading platform that matches buy and sell orders according to its rules, usually by price and then time.

concepts.shortDefinition: Staff whose activities have a material impact on a firm's risk profile, to whom stricter remuneration rules apply.
concepts.bodyHtml: Staff whose activities have a material impact on a firm's risk profile, to whom stricter remuneration rules apply. UCITS and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) use the term identified staff.

concepts.shortDefinition: The level of NAV error, expressed as a percentage of NAV, above which an error must be corrected, investors and the fund compensated and the regulator informed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The level of NAV error, expressed as a percentage of NAV, above which an error must be corrected, investors and the fund compensated and the regulator informed. Also called the tolerance threshold; in Luxembourg the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) Circular 24/856 sets 0.20% for money market funds (MMFs), 0.50% for bond and mixed funds and 1.00% for equity and other funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The level above which a fund pricing error must be corrected and investors compensated, often expressed as a percentage of NAV, such as 0.5% for many equity funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: The level above which a fund pricing error must be corrected and investors compensated, often expressed as a percentage of NAV, such as 0.5% for many equity funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A formal list of decisions that only the board can take, such as approving strategy, the risk appetite, major contracts, key appointments and financial statements.
concepts.bodyHtml: A formal list of decisions that only the board can take, such as approving strategy, the risk appetite, major contracts, key appointments and financial statements. Everything not reserved can be delegated, with reporting back to the board.

concepts.shortDefinition: The profit that can be made by including, excluding or reordering transactions in a block, for example by front-running a trade.
concepts.bodyHtml: The profit that can be made by including, excluding or reordering transactions in a block, for example by front-running a trade.

concepts.shortDefinition: The liquidation of a solvent company at the choice of its directors and shareholders, who control the process.
concepts.bodyHtml: The liquidation of a solvent company at the choice of its directors and shareholders, who control the process. It is the usual way to wind up a corporate fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token driven by internet culture and speculation, typically with no rights or underlying business.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token driven by internet culture and speculation, typically with no rights or underlying business.

concepts.shortDefinition: The pool of transactions that have been broadcast but not yet included in a block.
concepts.bodyHtml: The pool of transactions that have been broadcast but not yet included in a block.

concepts.shortDefinition: A four-digit code assigned to merchants to classify their business.
concepts.bodyHtml: A four-digit code assigned to merchants to classify their business. It is used for fees, rewards and risk controls, such as blocking gambling transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entity that sells to the customer and is legally responsible for the transaction, including refunds, chargebacks and often tax.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entity that sells to the customer and is legally responsible for the transaction, including refunds, chargebacks and often tax. Marketplaces and payment facilitators may act as merchant of record for smaller sellers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The checks an acquirer or payment facilitator performs before accepting a merchant, and continues afterwards, covering identity, ownership, business model, website content, fraud and chargeback levels.
concepts.bodyHtml: The checks an acquirer or payment facilitator performs before accepting a merchant, and continues afterwards, covering identity, ownership, business model, website content, fraud and chargeback levels.

concepts.shortDefinition: The total fee an acquirer charges a merchant for accepting card payments, made up of interchange, scheme fees and the acquirer's margin.
concepts.bodyHtml: The total fee an acquirer charges a merchant for accepting card payments, made up of interchange, scheme fees and the acquirer's margin.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short proof that a record is included in a set summarised by a Merkle root, consisting of the hashes needed to recompute the root.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short proof that a record is included in a set summarised by a Merkle root, consisting of the hashes needed to recompute the root. It lets clients check proof-of-reserves inclusion or light clients verify transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A data structure that summarises many records into a single cryptographic hash, so that anyone can prove a record is included without revealing the others.
concepts.bodyHtml: A data structure that summarises many records into a single cryptographic hash, so that anyone can prove a record is included without revealing the others. Blockchains use it to summarise transactions in a block, and proof-of-reserves exercises use it to commit to client balances.

aliases: Prudential sourcebook for MiFID investment firms
concepts.shortDefinition: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)'s prudential sourcebook for MiFID investment firms, in force since 1 January 2022, setting own funds, K-factor, liquidity, concentration, internal capital adequacy and risk assessment (ICARA), remuneration and disclosure requirements.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)'s prudential sourcebook for MiFID investment firms, in force since 1 January 2022, setting own funds, K-factor, liquidity, concentration, internal capital adequacy and risk assessment (ICARA), remuneration and disclosure requirements. It is the UK counterpart to the EU's Investment Firms Regulation and Directive (IFR/IFD).

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of work, a participant who uses specialised hardware and electricity to compete for the right to add the next block and earn the reward.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of work, a participant who uses specialised hardware and electricity to compete for the right to add the next block and earn the reward.

concepts.term: Minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities
concepts.shortDefinition: The amount of capital and debt that a bank must hold that can absorb losses or be converted to equity in resolution, so that it can be recapitalised without public money.
concepts.bodyHtml: The amount of capital and debt that a bank must hold that can absorb losses or be converted to equity in resolution, so that it can be recapitalised without public money.
concepts.sortKey: minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of work, the process of competing to add blocks by solving computational puzzles, in return for newly issued coins and fees.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of work, the process of competing to add blocks by solving computational puzzles, in return for newly issued coins and fees. In proof of stake, validators perform the equivalent role by locking up a stake (32 ETH per validator on Ethereum). Mining or validating on one's own account is generally not a regulated service.

concepts.shortDefinition: Miners combining computing power and sharing rewards; the pool operator chooses the transactions and builds the block.
concepts.bodyHtml: Miners combining computing power and sharing rewards; the pool operator chooses the transactions and builds the block. Bitcoin mining is concentrated in a small number of large pools.

concepts.shortDefinition: To create new tokens.
concepts.bodyHtml: To create new tokens.

concepts.shortDefinition: Creating new tokens and removing them from supply.
concepts.bodyHtml: Creating new tokens and removing them from supply. For a stablecoin, tokens are minted against money received and burned on redemption, so every mint should match money in and every burn a payment out, reconciled daily.

concepts.shortDefinition: Selling a product to an investor for whom it is unsuitable, or on the basis of misleading information.
concepts.bodyHtml: Selling a product to an investor for whom it is unsuitable, or on the basis of misleading information. Marketing and mis-selling risk arises from misleading or out-of-date offering and sales documents.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that pools and redistributes funds from many users to break the link between the source and the destination.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that pools and redistributes funds from many users to break the link between the source and the destination. Tornado Cash is a smart contract mixer.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of 12 or 24 words that encodes a wallet's master private key, from which all its keys can be regenerated.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of 12 or 24 words that encodes a wallet's master private key, from which all its keys can be regenerated. Anyone who obtains it can take the wallet's assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Deterioration in a model's performance because the data or relationships it encounters change from those it was trained on.
concepts.bodyHtml: Deterioration in a model's performance because the data or relationships it encounters change from those it was trained on.

concepts.shortDefinition: A set of asset allocations and funds designed by a manager that advisers or platforms apply to clients' accounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: A set of asset allocations and funds designed by a manager that advisers or platforms apply to clients' accounts. Responsibility for suitability depends on who makes investment decisions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss or poor decisions because a model, including an artificial intelligence (AI) model, is badly designed, wrongly used or based on poor data.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss or poor decisions because a model, including an artificial intelligence (AI) model, is badly designed, wrongly used or based on poor data. It is managed through model inventories, independent validation, monitoring and limits on use.

concepts.shortDefinition: Independent review that a model is conceptually sound, correctly implemented and performing as intended.
concepts.bodyHtml: Independent review that a model is conceptually sound, correctly implemented and performing as intended. A model inventory lists all models in use with their owners and risk ratings.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native coin of Monero, a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that hides the sender, receiver and amount of transactions by default.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native coin of Monero, a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that hides the sender, receiver and amount of transactions by default. Many exchanges have delisted it, and the EU anti-money laundering (AML) Regulation bars regulated firms from handling anonymity-enhancing coins from July 2027.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Monetary Authority of Singapore, Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Monetary Authority of Singapore, Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator. It licenses digital payment token service providers and has a regulatory framework for single-currency stablecoins.

concepts.shortDefinition: Money laundering: disguising the criminal origin of money or assets so that they appear legitimate.
concepts.bodyHtml: Money laundering: disguising the criminal origin of money or assets so that they appear legitimate. In technology contexts, ML can also mean machine learning.

concepts.shortDefinition: The officer responsible for overseeing a firm's day-to-day compliance with anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: The officer responsible for overseeing a firm's day-to-day compliance with anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules. In some jurisdictions this is a separate role from the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO), who decides whether to report suspicions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017, the main UK anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules for firms.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017, the main UK anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules for firms. They require risk assessments, customer due diligence, record keeping and policies and controls, and cover cryptoasset exchange and custodian wallet providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The person in a firm responsible for receiving internal suspicion reports and deciding whether to report to the Financial Intelligence Unit.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person in a firm responsible for receiving internal suspicion reports and deciding whether to report to the Financial Intelligence Unit. The role needs access to data, authority and a direct line to the board.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests in short-term money market instruments, deposits and reverse repos, aiming to preserve capital and provide daily liquidity with a return in line with short-term interest rates.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests in short-term money market instruments, deposits and reverse repos, aiming to preserve capital and provide daily liquidity with a return in line with short-term interest rates. MMFs, whether UCITS or alternative investment funds (AIFs), are regulated by the Money Market Funds Regulation (MMFR), which limits the weighted average maturity (WAM) and weighted average life (WAL) of a short-term MMF to 60 and 120 days and of a standard MMF to 6 and 12 months.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2017/1131), which has applied to all money market funds (MMFs), whether UCITS or alternative investment funds (AIFs), since 21 January 2019.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2017/1131), which has applied to all money market funds (MMFs), whether UCITS or alternative investment funds (AIFs), since 21 January 2019. It defines public debt constant net asset value (CNAV), low volatility net asset value (LVNAV) and variable net asset value (VNAV) MMFs and sets rules on eligible assets, diversification, credit quality, liquidity, valuation, stress testing and transparency.

concepts.shortDefinition: Short-term debt instruments normally dealt in on the money market, such as treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit, that are liquid and can be accurately valued at any time.
concepts.bodyHtml: Short-term debt instruments normally dealt in on the money market, such as treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit, that are liquid and can be accurately valued at any time.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person who moves illicit funds through their own accounts or wallets on behalf of criminals, knowingly or not.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person who moves illicit funds through their own accounts or wallets on behalf of criminals, knowingly or not.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment service in which funds are received from a payer, without any payment account being created, solely to transfer a corresponding amount to a payee or another provider acting for the payee.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment service in which funds are received from a payer, without any payment account being created, solely to transfer a corresponding amount to a payee or another provider acting for the payee. It carries higher money laundering risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Council of Europe's committee of experts that evaluates its member states' anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing systems against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Council of Europe's committee of experts that evaluates its member states' anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing systems against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards. It is an associate member of the FATF.

concepts.shortDefinition: A form of security in which legal ownership of the asset is transferred to the creditor while the debtor keeps possession and use of it, subject to the debtor’s right to redeem by repaying the debt.
concepts.bodyHtml: A form of security in which legal ownership of the asset is transferred to the creditor while the debtor keeps possession and use of it, subject to the debtor’s right to redeem by repaying the debt. In Ireland, a legal mortgage of land can now only be created by way of charge.

concepts.shortDefinition: A side-letter term giving an investor the right to receive any more favourable terms granted to other investors of the same or smaller size.
concepts.bodyHtml: A side-letter term giving an investor the right to receive any more favourable terms granted to other investors of the same or smaller size.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that uses multi-party computation to split signing power into shares held by several parties.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that uses multi-party computation to split signing power into shares held by several parties. A provider that can sign, co-sign or block transactions is exercising control and may be a virtual asset service provider; one that only licenses software generally is not.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose signing key is split between several parties using multi-party computation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose signing key is split between several parties using multi-party computation. It still uses elliptic curves, so it is not quantum-safe.

concepts.shortDefinition: An account allowing customers to hold, send and receive several currencies, typically offered by e-money institutions and banks for international payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: An account allowing customers to hold, send and receive several currencies, typically offered by e-money institutions and banks for international payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: Logging in with two or more independent types of evidence, such as a password, a code from a device or a biometric.
concepts.bodyHtml: Logging in with two or more independent types of evidence, such as a password, a code from a device or a biometric. It greatly reduces the risk of account takeover and is expected for remote and privileged access.

concepts.shortDefinition: A stablecoin issued by affiliated entities in more than one jurisdiction, so that the same token is issued under different regulatory regimes, often with separate reserves.
concepts.bodyHtml: A stablecoin issued by affiliated entities in more than one jurisdiction, so that the same token is issued under different regulatory regimes, often with separate reserves. It raises the question of whether holders in each jurisdiction have equal rights to redeem and equal access to the reserves.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund whose portfolio is divided among several portfolio managers, each with a mandate to manage a portion, selected and overseen by a principal manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund whose portfolio is divided among several portfolio managers, each with a mandate to manage a portion, selected and overseen by a principal manager. Also called a manager of managers fund. The sub-managers are delegates of the management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM).

concepts.shortDefinition: A cryptographic technique in which several parties each hold a share of a key and sign jointly, without the full key ever existing in one place.
concepts.bodyHtml: A cryptographic technique in which several parties each hold a share of a key and sign jointly, without the full key ever existing in one place. In practice the vendor's policy engine often becomes the real control point, which is invisible on-chain.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Financial Stability Board (FSB)'s term for a firm or group that combines a broad range of crypto services, typically around a trading platform.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Financial Stability Board (FSB)'s term for a firm or group that combines a broad range of crypto services, typically around a trading platform.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, a group of countries that monitors and reports on the implementation of UN sanctions on North Korea, including its theft and laundering of crypto-assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, a group of countries that monitors and reports on the implementation of UN sanctions on North Korea, including its theft and laundering of crypto-assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet that requires signatures from several keys (for example three of five) to approve a transaction.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet that requires signatures from several keys (for example three of five) to approve a transaction. Multisig and multi-party computation add little protection if every signer relies on the same compromised screen, as the Bybit hack showed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The peer assessment of a jurisdiction against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards, by FATF or a regional body, rating technical compliance and effectiveness and setting recommended actions tracked through follow-up.
concepts.bodyHtml: The peer assessment of a jurisdiction against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards, by FATF or a regional body, rating technical compliance and effectiveness and setting recommended actions tracked through follow-up.

concepts.shortDefinition: In the US, an open-ended investment company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
concepts.bodyHtml: In the US, an open-ended investment company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940. Elsewhere the term is often used generally for retail collective investment schemes.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank that holds only safe, liquid assets against its deposits.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank that holds only safe, liquid assets against its deposits. A fiat-backed stablecoin issuer works in a similar way, with tokens as liabilities and reserves as assets, but usually keeps the interest and has no deposit insurance or lender of last resort.

concepts.shortDefinition: Belgium's central bank and prudential supervisor of banks, insurers, payment and e-money institutions.
