concepts.bodyHtml: A consensus mechanism in which miners compete to solve computational puzzles to add blocks.

concepts.shortDefinition: The authenticated instructions, defined in the depositary agreement, on which the fund depositary may act to move a fund’s assets and cash.
concepts.bodyHtml: The authenticated instructions, defined in the depositary agreement, on which the fund depositary may act to move a fund’s assets and cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK open-ended fund investing mainly in property, with a tax regime under which the fund pays no tax on property income and investors are taxed as if they held property directly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK open-ended fund investing mainly in property, with a tax regime under which the fund pays no tax on property income and investors are taxed as if they held property directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: Scaling regulatory requirements to a firm's size, clients and complexity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Scaling regulatory requirements to a firm's size, clients and complexity. Proportionality changes how much evidence or capital is required, not whether a risk must be controlled.

concepts.shortDefinition: Separating the role of building blocks from proposing them, so specialist builders compete to assemble the most valuable block and validators simply choose the highest bid.
concepts.bodyHtml: Separating the role of building blocks from proposing them, so specialist builders compete to assemble the most valuable block and validators simply choose the highest bid. On Ethereum it is currently implemented outside the protocol by relay software.

concepts.shortDefinition: A management company (ManCo) set up by a fund promoter within its own group to manage the group’s own funds, usually delegating portfolio management to a group investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: A management company (ManCo) set up by a fund promoter within its own group to manage the group’s own funds, usually delegating portfolio management to a group investment manager. Sometimes called a group ManCo. It differs from a third-party ManCo, which is independent and serves many unrelated promoters.

concepts.shortDefinition: Trading for a firm's own account rather than for clients.
concepts.bodyHtml: Trading for a firm's own account rather than for clients. On crypto platforms it can create conflicts with clients, which the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) addresses by restricting trading platform operators from dealing on own account on their own platform.

concepts.shortDefinition: The regulator-approved document setting out the details of a fund, including its objective and policies, restrictions, fees, service providers, dealing arrangements, risks and liquidity management tools (LMTs).
concepts.bodyHtml: The regulator-approved document setting out the details of a fund, including its objective and policies, restrictions, fees, service providers, dealing arrangements, risks and liquidity management tools (LMTs). It is the main document for investors deciding whether to invest and the rulebook for the fund’s operation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A document setting out the features specific to one sub-fund of an umbrella fund, read together with the core prospectus.
concepts.bodyHtml: A document setting out the features specific to one sub-fund of an umbrella fund, read together with the core prospectus.

concepts.shortDefinition: A company whose assets and liabilities are divided into legally segregated cells, so that the liabilities of one cell cannot be met from the assets of another.
concepts.bodyHtml: A company whose assets and liabilities are divided into legally segregated cells, so that the liabilities of one cell cannot be met from the assets of another. Widely used for insurance and investment fund structures.

concepts.shortDefinition: Liquidity held by a protocol's own treasury rather than rented from liquidity providers with incentives.
concepts.bodyHtml: Liquidity held by a protocol's own treasury rather than rented from liquidity providers with incentives.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that researches company meetings and recommends to investors how to vote.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that researches company meetings and recommends to investors how to vote. EU rules under the Shareholder Rights Directive II require proxy advisers to disclose their methods and conflicts of interest.

concepts.shortDefinition: Voting at a company’s general meeting by instructing another person (a proxy) to vote on the shareholder’s behalf.
concepts.bodyHtml: Voting at a company’s general meeting by instructing another person (a proxy) to vote on the shareholder’s behalf. It is how funds usually exercise their voting rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Prudential Regulation Authority, part of the Bank of England.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Prudential Regulation Authority, part of the Bank of England. It supervises the safety and soundness of UK banks, building societies, credit unions, insurers and major investment firms.

concepts.shortDefinition: The belief that people can raise concerns, admit mistakes or disagree without being punished or seen as disloyal.
concepts.bodyHtml: The belief that people can raise concerns, admit mistakes or disagree without being punished or seen as disloyal. On a board, it is a precondition for effective challenge.

concepts.shortDefinition: A public chain lets anyone run a node and transact; a permissioned ledger limits who can take part.
concepts.bodyHtml: A public chain lets anyone run a node and transact; a permissioned ledger limits who can take part. Regulated tokens on public chains usually restrict holders through a whitelist.

concepts.shortDefinition: A key derived from the private key that others use to verify signatures.
concepts.bodyHtml: A key derived from the private key that others use to verify signatures. Addresses are derived from it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Inflating a token's price through promotion or fake volume, then selling to the buyers drawn in.
concepts.bodyHtml: Inflating a token's price through promotion or fake volume, then selling to the buyers drawn in. A rug pull is a related fraud in which a project team raises money, drains the liquidity and disappears.

concepts.shortDefinition: Shorthand for the day a quantum computer can break today's public-key cryptography.
concepts.bodyHtml: Shorthand for the day a quantum computer can break today's public-key cryptography. Nobody can date it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The independent regulator of firms authorised in the Qatar Financial Centre, which has issued rules on digital assets and tokenisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The independent regulator of firms authorised in the Qatar Financial Centre, which has issued rules on digital assets and tokenisation.

concepts.shortDefinition: Paying by scanning a QR code with a phone, usually triggering an account-to-account or wallet payment.
concepts.bodyHtml: Paying by scanning a QR code with a phone, usually triggering an account-to-account or wallet payment. It is widespread in Asia and growing in Europe with instant payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK authorised fund that can only be sold to professional and sophisticated investors, with wider investment and borrowing powers than retail funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK authorised fund that can only be sold to professional and sophisticated investors, with wider investment and borrowing powers than retail funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: In the US, an individual with at least $5 million in investments or an institution with at least $25 million, which may invest in private funds relying on the section 3(c)(7) exemption from the Investment Company Act.
concepts.bodyHtml: In the US, an individual with at least $5 million in investments or an institution with at least $25 million, which may invest in private funds relying on the section 3(c)(7) exemption from the Investment Company Act.

concepts.shortDefinition: In the UK, the category of cryptoasset to which the new regulated activities under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026 apply.
concepts.bodyHtml: In the UK, the category of cryptoasset to which the new regulated activities under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026 apply. It is broadly a fungible, transferable cryptoasset that is not already a specified investment, such as a security.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ireland, an investor eligible to invest in a qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF), such as a professional investor or an informed investor, who must generally subscribe at least €100,000.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ireland, an investor eligible to invest in a qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF), such as a professional investor or an informed investor, who must generally subscribe at least €100,000.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish alternative investment fund (AIF) reserved for qualifying investors subscribing at least €100,000.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish alternative investment fund (AIF) reserved for qualifying investors subscribing at least €100,000. It is largely free of the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) investment and borrowing restrictions and can be authorised on a fast-track basis on the business day after filing.

concepts.shortDefinition: The former name of the Irish qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF), a fund reserved for professional and qualifying investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The former name of the Irish qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF), a fund reserved for professional and qualifying investors.
concepts.notes: former name of the Irish QIAIF

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA) regime's term for a cryptoasset seeking a stable value by reference to fiat, with the issuer holding backing assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA) regime's term for a cryptoasset seeking a stable value by reference to fiat, with the issuer holding backing assets. Systemic coins are also regulated by the Bank of England.

concepts.shortDefinition: A liquidity management tool (LMT) that limits or alters investors’ redemptions: a redemption gate, an extension of the notice period or redemption in kind.
concepts.bodyHtml: A liquidity management tool (LMT) that limits or alters investors’ redemptions: a redemption gate, an extension of the notice period or redemption in kind. The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) guidelines recommend that managers select at least one.

concepts.shortDefinition: Computing that uses quantum effects.
concepts.bodyHtml: Computing that uses quantum effects. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could break the signature schemes used by most blockchains today.

concepts.shortDefinition: The basic unit of a quantum computer.
concepts.bodyHtml: The basic unit of a quantum computer. Many noisy physical qubits are combined, by error correction, into each reliable logical qubit.

concepts.shortDefinition: Questions and answers published by a regulator to explain how it applies its rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: Questions and answers published by a regulator to explain how it applies its rules. The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) and the European Banking Authority (EBA) publish Q&As that national supervisors are expected to follow.

concepts.shortDefinition: Malicious software that encrypts or steals an organisation's data and demands payment, usually in crypto-assets, for its release.
concepts.bodyHtml: Malicious software that encrypts or steals an organisation's data and demands payment, usually in crypto-assets, for its release. Ransom payments may breach sanctions if the attackers are designated persons.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart-contract vulnerability in which an external contract calls back into the vulnerable contract before it has updated its records, letting the attacker withdraw funds repeatedly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart-contract vulnerability in which an external contract calls back into the vulnerable contract before it has updated its records, letting the attacker withdraw funds repeatedly.

concepts.shortDefinition: Physical assets with intrinsic worth, such as real estate, land, commodities, precious metals, equipment and natural resources.
concepts.bodyHtml: Physical assets with intrinsic worth, such as real estate, land, commodities, precious metals, equipment and natural resources. They are generally less liquid than securities. UCITS may not invest in them directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests in, or obtains exposure to, property, directly, through property companies or synthetically through derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests in, or obtains exposure to, property, directly, through property companies or synthetically through derivatives. Because property is illiquid, open-ended real estate funds face a liquidity mismatch.

concepts.shortDefinition: A listed company or fund that invests mainly in income-producing property and qualifies for special tax treatment if it meets conditions on its assets, sources of profit and distribution of income.
concepts.bodyHtml: A listed company or fund that invests mainly in income-producing property and qualifies for special tax treatment if it meets conditions on its assets, sources of profit and distribution of income.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment system in which high-value payments are settled individually and immediately in central bank money, rather than netted at the end of the day.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment system in which high-value payments are settled individually and immediately in central bank money, rather than netted at the end of the day. Examples are the Eurosystem's T2 and the Bank of England's RTGS system.

concepts.shortDefinition: A traditional asset, such as a bond, fund, property or commodity, represented by a token.
concepts.bodyHtml: A traditional asset, such as a bond, fund, property or commodity, represented by a token.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person, usually an accountant, appointed by a secured creditor to take possession of and sell secured property to repay the debt owed to that creditor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person, usually an accountant, appointed by a secured creditor to take possession of and sell secured property to repay the debt owed to that creditor. A receiver is distinct from a liquidator.

concepts.shortDefinition: A regulated service of receiving a client's order to buy or sell an instrument or crypto-asset and passing it to another firm for execution.
concepts.bodyHtml: A regulated service of receiving a client's order to buy or sell an instrument or crypto-asset and passing it to another firm for execution. It is an investment service under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID) and a crypto-asset service under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum period for which an investor is advised to hold an investment to have a reasonable prospect of achieving its objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum period for which an investor is advised to hold an investment to have a reasonable prospect of achieving its objective. For a fund it is usually several years, and it is stated in the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID).

concepts.shortDefinition: Checking that two records agree.
concepts.bodyHtml: Checking that two records agree. For a crypto firm, this means its books, its customers' balances and the assets held on-chain.

concepts.shortDefinition: A difference between the blockchain, the register and the cash or assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A difference between the blockchain, the register and the cash or assets. Each break needs to be explained and resolved; tokens without backing dilute other holders.

concepts.shortDefinition: Requirements to keep records of transactions, communications, customer due diligence and decisions for set periods, such as five years under anti-money laundering (AML) rules and the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID).
concepts.bodyHtml: Requirements to keep records of transactions, communications, customer due diligence and decisions for set periods, such as five years under anti-money laundering (AML) rules and the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID).

concepts.shortDefinition: A recovery plan sets out how a firm would restore its financial position in severe stress.
concepts.bodyHtml: A recovery plan sets out how a firm would restore its financial position in severe stress. A resolution plan, usually prepared by the authority, sets out how a failing firm would be resolved.

concepts.shortDefinition: Testing in which a team simulates a real adversary to test an organisation's prevention, detection and response, usually without the defending (blue) team knowing.
concepts.bodyHtml: Testing in which a team simulates a real adversary to test an organisation's prevention, detection and response, usually without the defending (blue) team knowing. Purple teaming has the two teams work together to improve defences.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which an investor in an open-ended fund sells units or shares back to the fund and receives their current value, usually in cash; the units or shares are then cancelled.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which an investor in an open-ended fund sells units or shares back to the fund and receives their current value, usually in cash; the units or shares are then cancelled.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Exchanging a token for the underlying asset or money from the issuer, for example a stablecoin for dollars at par.

concepts.shortDefinition: A liquidity stress testing measure comparing the amount of assets a fund can sell within a period with the redemptions it could face in the same period.
concepts.bodyHtml: A liquidity stress testing measure comparing the amount of assets a fund can sell within a period with the redemptions it could face in the same period. A ratio below one shows a potential liquidity shortfall.

concepts.shortDefinition: A pre-set fee paid into the fund by redeeming investors to cover the dealing costs their redemptions cause.
concepts.bodyHtml: A pre-set fee paid into the fund by redeeming investors to cover the dealing costs their redemptions cause. It is an anti-dilution liquidity management tool (LMT).

concepts.shortDefinition: A liquidity management tool (LMT) that temporarily limits redemptions on a dealing day to a set percentage of the fund (often 10%), scaling back all requests pro rata and carrying the balance forward.
concepts.bodyHtml: A liquidity management tool (LMT) that temporarily limits redemptions on a dealing day to a set percentage of the fund (often 10%), scaling back all requests pro rata and carrying the balance forward. Unlike a suspension, the fund continues to deal.

concepts.shortDefinition: Meeting a redemption by transferring the investor’s pro rata share of the fund’s assets instead of cash.
concepts.bodyHtml: Meeting a redemption by transferring the investor’s pro rata share of the fund’s assets instead of cash. Also called an in specie redemption, it is usually limited to professional investors; subscriptions may likewise be made in specie.

concepts.shortDefinition: Moving a fund or company from one jurisdiction to another while keeping it as the same legal entity, where the laws of both jurisdictions allow.
concepts.bodyHtml: Moving a fund or company from one jurisdiction to another while keeping it as the same legal entity, where the laws of both jurisdictions allow.

concepts.shortDefinition: Compensation paid to customers for harm caused by a firm's failings.
concepts.bodyHtml: Compensation paid to customers for harm caused by a firm's failings. A past business review identifies affected customers and calculates what they are owed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The record that decides legal ownership.
concepts.bodyHtml: The record that decides legal ownership. It may be on-chain, off-chain with an on-chain mirror, or hybrid; the documents must name it and say how it is corrected.

concepts.shortDefinition: A central register of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies, trusts or other legal entities.
concepts.bodyHtml: A central register of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies, trusts or other legal entities. EU anti-money laundering (AML) law requires member states to keep such registers and give access to authorities and obliged entities.

concepts.shortDefinition: The register that UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must keep under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) of all their contracts with information and communication technology (ICT) third-party service providers, which is submitted to the regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: The register that UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must keep under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) of all their contracts with information and communication technology (ICT) third-party service providers, which is submitted to the regulator.

concepts.shortDefinition: The register of unitholders or shareholders that records who owns a fund’s units or shares.
concepts.bodyHtml: The register of unitholders or shareholders that records who owns a fund’s units or shares. It is maintained by the transfer agent (TA) and may be kept using distributed ledger technology (DLT); the register shows the legal owner, which may be a nominee.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that provides only account information services and is registered rather than fully authorised, needing professional indemnity insurance instead of capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that provides only account information services and is registered rather than fully authorised, needing professional indemnity insurance instead of capital.

concepts.shortDefinition: The person named in the terms of a tokenised security, or in law, who keeps its register of holders and can correct it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person named in the terms of a tokenised security, or in law, who keeps its register of holders and can correct it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Recording a security interest on a public or other register to give notice of it, to complete the creditor’s title or to establish priority.
concepts.bodyHtml: Recording a security interest on a public or other register to give notice of it, to complete the creditor’s title or to establish priority. Most charges created by an Irish company must be registered with the Companies Registration Office (or, for an Irish collective asset-management vehicle (ICAV), the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)) within 21 days.

concepts.shortDefinition: Technology that helps firms meet regulatory requirements, such as monitoring, reporting and onboarding tools.
concepts.bodyHtml: Technology that helps firms meet regulatory requirements, such as monitoring, reporting and onboarding tools. SupTech is technology used by supervisors.

concepts.shortDefinition: A multilateral trading system authorised under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) and operated by a market operator, such as a stock exchange’s main market.
concepts.bodyHtml: A multilateral trading system authorised under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) and operated by a market operator, such as a stock exchange’s main market. The Shareholder Rights Directive II (SRD II) applies to asset managers investing in shares traded on an EEA regulated market.

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU legislative act that applies directly in all Member States without transposition, such as the Money Market Funds Regulation (MMFR), the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Regulation, the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) and the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU legislative act that applies directly in all Member States without transposition, such as the Money Market Funds Regulation (MMFR), the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Regulation, the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) and the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA).

concepts.shortDefinition: Locating or booking an activity wherever the rules or supervision are lightest.
concepts.bodyHtml: Locating or booking an activity wherever the rules or supervision are lightest. Uneven implementation of international standards across countries creates the opportunity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum financial resources (own funds) that a management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) must hold under regulation, partly to cover liability risks.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum financial resources (own funds) that a management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) must hold under regulation, partly to cover liability risks. An AIFM must also hold additional own funds or professional indemnity insurance.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process of identifying upcoming regulatory changes (horizon scanning), assessing their impact and implementing them on time.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process of identifying upcoming regulatory changes (horizon scanning), assessing their impact and implementing them on time.

concepts.shortDefinition: The periodic data and information firms must submit to their regulators, such as financial, prudential, transaction and conduct returns.
concepts.bodyHtml: The periodic data and information firms must submit to their regulators, such as financial, prudential, transaction and conduct returns.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of failing to identify and comply with the regulatory requirements of each market in which a fund or manager operates, or of failing to adapt to new regulation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of failing to identify and comply with the regulatory requirements of each market in which a fund or manager operates, or of failing to adapt to new regulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A framework that lets firms test innovative products with real customers under regulatory supervision and with safeguards.
concepts.bodyHtml: A framework that lets firms test innovative products with real customers under regulatory supervision and with safeguards. Innovation hubs give firms informal guidance on how rules apply.

concepts.shortDefinition: Detailed technical rules drafted by an ESA and adopted by the Commission as delegated regulations, for example on liquidity management tools (LMTs), loan origination, European long-term investment funds (ELTIFs) and the SFDR templates.
concepts.bodyHtml: Detailed technical rules drafted by an ESA and adopted by the Commission as delegated regulations, for example on liquidity management tools (LMTs), loan origination, European long-term investment funds (ELTIFs) and the SFDR templates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Re-using assets received as collateral, or held for clients, for the firm's own purposes such as lending.
concepts.bodyHtml: Re-using assets received as collateral, or held for clients, for the firm's own purposes such as lending.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person or firm connected to a firm or its owners, such as a founder's own project or token.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person or firm connected to a firm or its owners, such as a founder's own project or token. Dealings with related parties need independent approval and disclosure.

concepts.shortDefinition: The customer money that a payment or e-money institution must safeguard: sums received from or for customers for payment transactions, and funds received in exchange for e-money.
concepts.bodyHtml: The customer money that a payment or e-money institution must safeguard: sums received from or for customers for payment transactions, and funds received in exchange for e-money.

concepts.shortDefinition: Fixing control weaknesses or compliance failures and, where customers have been harmed, putting them back in the position they should have been in.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fixing control weaknesses or compliance failures and, where customers have been harmed, putting them back in the position they should have been in. Issue management tracks findings to closure.

concepts.shortDefinition: A remote procedure call: a request from one computer to run a function on another.
concepts.bodyHtml: A remote procedure call: a request from one computer to run a function on another. Wallets and apps use RPC providers to read blockchain data and send transactions, which makes those providers a point of dependency.

concepts.shortDefinition: The policy that UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must have for the pay of their key staff, consistent with sound risk management and not encouraging excessive risk-taking.
concepts.bodyHtml: The policy that UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must have for the pay of their key staff, consistent with sound risk management and not encouraging excessive risk-taking.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK tax status for offshore funds that report their income to investors each year, allowing UK investors to pay capital gains tax rather than income tax on disposals.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK tax status for offshore funds that report their income to investors each year, allowing UK investors to pay capital gains tax rather than income tax on disposals.

concepts.shortDefinition: A merchant's challenge to a chargeback, submitting evidence through its acquirer that the transaction was valid.
concepts.bodyHtml: A merchant's challenge to a chargeback, submitting evidence through its acquirer that the transaction was valid. The card scheme's rules decide the outcome.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transaction in which a fund sells securities and agrees to buy them back at a set price on a future date, in effect borrowing cash against the securities.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transaction in which a fund sells securities and agrees to buy them back at a set price on a future date, in effect borrowing cash against the securities.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that investors lose confidence in a fund or its manager and redeem their holdings, for example after errors, breaches or misconduct.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that investors lose confidence in a fund or its manager and redeem their holdings, for example after errors, breaches or misconduct.

concepts.shortDefinition: A request for quote: a trading method in which a buyer asks one or more dealers for a price before trading.
concepts.bodyHtml: A request for quote: a trading method in which a buyer asks one or more dealers for a price before trading. Common in over the counter (OTC) crypto trading and bond markets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A messaging service that lets a payee send a payment request, which the payer can approve, decline or reschedule, triggering a payment such as an instant credit transfer.
concepts.bodyHtml: A messaging service that lets a payee send a payment request, which the payer can approve, decline or reschedule, triggering a payment such as an instant credit transfer.

concepts.shortDefinition: Separating payment for investment research from payment for trade execution.
concepts.bodyHtml: Separating payment for investment research from payment for trade execution. Since 2018 EU and UK rules have required portfolio managers to pay for research from their own resources or a research payment account funded by clients; both have since reintroduced options to pay jointly under conditions.

concepts.shortDefinition: India's central bank and banking regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: India's central bank and banking regulator. It also regulates non-bank financial companies and payment systems, including the oversight of UPI, and runs the digital rupee pilots.

concepts.shortDefinition: The pool of assets that backs an asset-referenced token or e-money token and from which holders are repaid.
concepts.bodyHtml: The pool of assets that backs an asset-referenced token or e-money token and from which holders are repaid. Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), the reserve must be segregated from the issuer's own assets, held with approved custodians, invested only in highly liquid, low-risk instruments and independently audited.

concepts.shortDefinition: A stablecoin issuer's board-approved policy setting eligible reserve assets, liquidity tiers, maturities, concentration limits, encumbrance, segregation, reconciliation and governance.
concepts.bodyHtml: A stablecoin issuer's board-approved policy setting eligible reserve assets, liquidity tiers, maturities, concentration limits, encumbrance, segregation, reconciliation and governance.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg AIF reserved for well-informed investors that does not require the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval but must be managed by an authorised EEA alternative investment fund manager (AIFM).
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg AIF reserved for well-informed investors that does not require the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval but must be managed by an authorised EEA alternative investment fund manager (AIFM). Its offering document must state that it is not supervised in Luxembourg.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that remains after controls are applied.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that remains after controls are applied. Credit for controls depends on evidence that they work.

concepts.shortDefinition: A set of documents that payment and e-money firms in the UK must keep, enabling an insolvency practitioner to identify and return customers' funds quickly if the firm fails.
concepts.bodyHtml: A set of documents that payment and e-money firms in the UK must keep, enabling an insolvency practitioner to identify and return customers' funds quickly if the firm fails.

concepts.shortDefinition: Re-using staked assets, or liquid staking tokens, to secure additional services, in return for extra rewards and extra slashing risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: Re-using staked assets, or liquid staking tokens, to secure additional services, in return for extra rewards and extra slashing risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU legislative package, politically agreed on 18 December 2025 but not yet applicable, that would strengthen value for money (VfM) requirements, revise the inducement rules and amend the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID).
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU legislative package, politically agreed on 18 December 2025 but not yet applicable, that would strengthen value for money (VfM) requirements, revise the inducement rules and amend the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID).

concepts.shortDefinition: A member of the general public investing on their own account.
concepts.bodyHtml: A member of the general public investing on their own account. Retail investors receive the highest level of regulatory protection and may usually subscribe freely only to more tightly regulated funds, such as UCITS.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish AIF that may be sold to retail investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish AIF that may be sold to retail investors. It is subject to the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) investment and borrowing restrictions that are less onerous than those for UCITS, and must be managed by an authorised alternative investment fund manager (AIFM). Luxembourg’s equivalent is the Part II UCI.

concepts.shortDefinition: The use, for one's own account, of assets received as collateral or held in custody.
concepts.bodyHtml: The use, for one's own account, of assets received as collateral or held in custody. EU rules restrict depositaries and their delegates from reusing fund assets and require clients' express consent for reuse of collateral.

concepts.shortDefinition: The use by a recipient, for its own account, of assets it has received as collateral or holds for a client, such as a prime broker reusing a hedge fund’s assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The use by a recipient, for its own account, of assets it has received as collateral or holds for a client, such as a prime broker reusing a hedge fund’s assets. Under the Securities Financing Transactions Regulation (SFTR) it requires the provider’s prior consent, and a fund must disclose any such right.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transaction in which a fund buys securities and agrees to sell them back at a set price on a future date, in effect lending cash against collateral.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transaction in which a fund buys securities and agrees to sell them back at a set price on a future date, in effect lending cash against collateral.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment made at the investor’s own exclusive initiative, without marketing by the manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment made at the investor’s own exclusive initiative, without marketing by the manager. It is not marketing, so no notification is needed, but regulators interpret it narrowly.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Serving a client at the client's own exclusive initiative. Under MiCA Article 61 and ESMA's guidelines (December 2024), any solicitation by the firm defeats it, and the firm must be able to evidence that the client approached it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The withdrawal of a fund’s regulatory authorisation by its regulator, usually on application once all its assets have been returned to investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The withdrawal of a fund’s regulatory authorisation by its regulator, usually on application once all its assets have been returned to investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: Returns paid to holders of a stablecoin, usually by platforms out of the income earned on the reserves.
concepts.bodyHtml: Returns paid to holders of a stablecoin, usually by platforms out of the income earned on the reserves. Many regimes prohibit stablecoin issuers from paying interest to holders, while rewards offered by third parties such as exchanges are more contested. Paying yield on a payment stablecoin can change its regulatory character.

concepts.shortDefinition: An offer by a company to its existing shareholders of the right to buy new shares in proportion to their holdings, usually at a discount.
concepts.bodyHtml: An offer by a company to its existing shareholders of the right to buy new shares in proportion to their holdings, usually at a discount. It is a voluntary corporate action.

concepts.shortDefinition: Keeping a fund’s assets identifiable and separate from the assets of the entity holding them, such as the fund depositary, so that they are protected if that entity becomes insolvent.
concepts.bodyHtml: Keeping a fund’s assets identifiable and separate from the assets of the entity holding them, such as the fund depositary, so that they are protected if that entity becomes insolvent.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US dollar stablecoin issued by Ripple, backed by cash and short-dated US government securities.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US dollar stablecoin issued by Ripple, backed by cash and short-dated US government securities.

concepts.shortDefinition: A process in which business areas identify their risks, assess how well controls work and plan improvements, usually challenged by the risk function.
concepts.bodyHtml: A process in which business areas identify their risks, assess how well controls work and plan improvements, usually challenged by the risk function.

concepts.shortDefinition: The combination of the return a fund targets and the level of investment risk it takes to achieve it, which drives its asset selection and target market.
concepts.bodyHtml: The combination of the return a fund targets and the level of investment risk it takes to achieve it, which drives its asset selection and target market.

concepts.shortDefinition: A board's statement of how much risk the firm is willing to take, with limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: A board's statement of how much risk the firm is willing to take, with limits. Limits that are routinely breached and waived without escalation suggest the appetite is not being applied.

concepts.shortDefinition: The written statement, approved by the board, of the types and amounts of risk the firm is willing to take to achieve its objectives, combining qualitative statements with measurable limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The written statement, approved by the board, of the types and amounts of risk the firm is willing to take to achieve its objectives, combining qualitative statements with measurable limits.

concepts.shortDefinition: The maximum level of risk a firm can take before breaching its capital or liquidity requirements, regulatory constraints or obligations to customers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The maximum level of risk a firm can take before breaching its capital or liquidity requirements, regulatory constraints or obligations to customers. Risk appetite should sit within it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investment in entities to support their launch, development or listing, such as private equity and venture capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investment in entities to support their launch, development or listing, such as private equity and venture capital. A SICAR invests exclusively in risk capital, and a reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF) that does so is not subject to risk-spreading.

concepts.shortDefinition: A quantitative limit on a specific risk, business line or activity, derived from the risk appetite, with escalation when it is approached or breached.
concepts.bodyHtml: A quantitative limit on a specific risk, business line or activity, derived from the risk appetite, with escalation when it is approached or breached.

concepts.shortDefinition: The function that identifies, measures, monitors and manages the risks to which a fund is exposed, such as market, liquidity, credit and counterparty risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: The function that identifies, measures, monitors and manages the risks to which a fund is exposed, such as market, liquidity, credit and counterparty risk. It must be independent of portfolio management, in some cases functionally and hierarchically.

concepts.shortDefinition: A record of a firm's identified risks, their assessment, controls, owners and actions.
concepts.bodyHtml: A record of a firm's identified risks, their assessment, controls, owners and actions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The AIFMD II requirement that an alternative investment fund (AIF) retain 5% of the notional value of each loan it originates and then transfers, generally until maturity for loans of up to eight years and for at least eight years otherwise.
concepts.bodyHtml: The AIFMD II requirement that an alternative investment fund (AIF) retain 5% of the notional value of each loan it originates and then transfers, generally until maturity for loans of up to eight years and for at least eight years otherwise.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assigning a risk score to an address or transaction based on its direct and indirect exposure to illicit or high-risk sources, using blockchain analytics.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assigning a risk score to an address or transaction based on its direct and indirect exposure to illicit or high-risk sources, using blockchain analytics.

concepts.shortDefinition: A prescribed statement in financial promotions warning of the risks of an investment, such as the UK warning for crypto-assets that investors should be prepared to lose all their money.
concepts.bodyHtml: A prescribed statement in financial promotions warning of the risks of an investment, such as the UK warning for crypto-assets that investors should be prepared to lose all their money.

concepts.shortDefinition: Applying anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) measures in proportion to the risks identified: more resources and enhanced measures where risks are higher, and simplified measures where they are lower.
concepts.bodyHtml: Applying anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) measures in proportion to the risks identified: more resources and enhanced measures where risks are higher, and simplified measures where they are lower. It is the foundation of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards (Recommendation 1).

concepts.shortDefinition: An overnight interest rate benchmark based on actual transactions, such as euro short-term rate (€STR) (euro), Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) (sterling) and Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) (US dollar), which has replaced interbank offered rates such as London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) in derivatives and loans.
concepts.bodyHtml: An overnight interest rate benchmark based on actual transactions, such as euro short-term rate (€STR) (euro), Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) (sterling) and Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) (US dollar), which has replaced interbank offered rates such as London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) in derivatives and loans.

concepts.shortDefinition: The principle, applied to Luxembourg Part II funds, specialised investment funds (SIFs) and reserved alternative investment funds (RAIFs), that a fund must diversify its investments, under rules less stringent than the UCITS diversification limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The principle, applied to Luxembourg Part II funds, specialised investment funds (SIFs) and reserved alternative investment funds (RAIFs), that a fund must diversify its investments, under rules less stringent than the UCITS diversification limits.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that provides investment advice or portfolio management through algorithms with little human involvement.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that provides investment advice or portfolio management through algorithms with little human involvement. It is subject to the same suitability and disclosure rules as human advice.

concepts.shortDefinition: A layer 2 that executes transactions off the main chain and posts compressed data and proofs back to it.
concepts.bodyHtml: A layer 2 that executes transactions off the main chain and posts compressed data and proofs back to it. Optimistic rollups rely on a challenge window; zero-knowledge rollups post validity proofs.

concepts.shortDefinition: Rollup-as-a-service: providers that let projects launch their own rollup networks using ready-made software and infrastructure.
concepts.bodyHtml: Rollup-as-a-service: providers that let projects launch their own rollup networks using ready-made software and infrastructure.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investigating why a problem happened, rather than just its symptoms, so that remediation prevents it recurring.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investigating why a problem happened, rather than just its symptoms, so that remediation prevents it recurring.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that runs blockchain nodes and lets wallets, exchanges and applications read data and send transactions through an interface, instead of running their own nodes.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that runs blockchain nodes and lets wallets, exchanges and applications read data and send transactions through an interface, instead of running their own nodes. Reliance on a few providers is a concentration risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fraud in which the developers of a token or protocol take the investors' funds and disappear.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fraud in which the developers of a token or protocol take the investors' funds and disappear.

concepts.shortDefinition: The requirement for payment and e-money institutions to protect customers' money so that it can be returned if the firm fails.
concepts.bodyHtml: The requirement for payment and e-money institutions to protect customers' money so that it can be returned if the firm fails. Funds must either be held in a segregated account with a bank or in secure, liquid assets, or be covered by an insurance policy or guarantee.

concepts.shortDefinition: A separate account at a bank or central bank, named to show it holds customers' funds safeguarded by a payment or e-money institution, so that the funds are protected from the firm's other creditors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A separate account at a bank or central bank, named to show it holds customers' funds safeguarded by a payment or e-money institution, so that the funds are protected from the firm's other creditors.

concepts.shortDefinition: An annual audit of a payment or e-money institution's compliance with safeguarding rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: An annual audit of a payment or e-money institution's compliance with safeguarding rules. In the UK, it is required for firms subject to an audit of their accounts under the Companies Act and is part of the Client Assets Sourcebook (CASS) 15 regime from May 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ways payment and e-money institutions may protect customer funds: segregation in a separate account at a credit institution or investment in secure liquid assets, or cover by an insurance policy or guarantee for the amount of the funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ways payment and e-money institutions may protect customer funds: segregation in a separate account at a credit institution or investment in secure liquid assets, or cover by an insurance policy or guarantee for the amount of the funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund depositary’s duty to hold in custody all financial instruments that can be held in custody and, for other assets, to verify the fund’s ownership and keep a record.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund depositary’s duty to hold in custody all financial instruments that can be held in custody and, for other assets, to verify the fund’s ownership and keep a record. The fund depositary may delegate custody to a sub-custodian but remains liable for the assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Good-practice custody rule: customer assets identifiable and recorded in the customer's name, with no use or lending without explicit, prior, written consent (and collateral for lending).
concepts.bodyHtml: Good-practice custody rule: customer assets identifiable and recorded in the customer's name, with no use or lending without explicit, prior, written consent (and collateral for lending).

concepts.term: Same activity, same risk, same regulation
concepts.shortDefinition: Equivalent activities face equivalent requirements, whatever the label or technology.
concepts.bodyHtml: Equivalent activities face equivalent requirements, whatever the label or technology. The language of the Financial Stability Board (FSB) and the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO); it stops a race to the bottom between centres.
concepts.sortKey: same activity, same risk, same regulation

concepts.shortDefinition: Restrictive measures imposed by the EU, the UN or other authorities against countries, entities or persons.
concepts.bodyHtml: Restrictive measures imposed by the EU, the UN or other authorities against countries, entities or persons. A fund must not make assets available to, or deal with, sanctioned persons, so investors, counterparties and investments are screened and holdings may have to be frozen.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK law that gives the government power to make sanctions regulations and to amend money laundering rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK law that gives the government power to make sanctions regulations and to amend money laundering rules. UK sanctions regimes are made under it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Attempts to avoid sanctions, for example through intermediaries, front companies, falsified documents or crypto-assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Attempts to avoid sanctions, for example through intermediaries, front companies, falsified documents or crypto-assets. Knowingly participating in circumvention is itself an offence.

concepts.shortDefinition: An authorisation from a sanctions authority allowing an otherwise prohibited activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: An authorisation from a sanctions authority allowing an otherwise prohibited activity. General licences cover anyone meeting their conditions; specific licences are granted on application for a particular case.

concepts.shortDefinition: Checking customers, counterparties, payments and, for crypto, wallet addresses against sanctions lists, both at onboarding and on an ongoing basis.
concepts.bodyHtml: Checking customers, counterparties, payments and, for crypto, wallet addresses against sanctions lists, both at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Screening must pick up new designations quickly and handle name variations and transliterations.

concepts.shortDefinition: A form of maximal extractable value in which an attacker places a transaction just before and just after a victim's trade on a decentralised exchange, profiting from the price movement the victim's trade causes.
concepts.bodyHtml: A form of maximal extractable value in which an attacker places a transaction just before and just after a victim's trade on a decentralised exchange, profiting from the price movement the victim's trade causes.

concepts.shortDefinition: Saudi Arabia's central bank, still known by its former acronym SAMA.
concepts.bodyHtml: Saudi Arabia's central bank, still known by its former acronym SAMA. It regulates banks, insurers, finance companies and payment service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU's strategy, launched in 2025 to succeed the Capital Markets Union, to channel more of Europeans' savings into productive investment and to integrate EU capital markets and their supervision.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU's strategy, launched in 2025 to succeed the Capital Markets Union, to channel more of Europeans' savings into productive investment and to integrate EU capital markets and their supervision.

concepts.shortDefinition: A type of zero-knowledge proof that needs no trusted setup and is considered resistant to quantum attacks, at the cost of larger proofs.
concepts.bodyHtml: A type of zero-knowledge proof that needs no trusted setup and is considered resistant to quantum attacks, at the cost of larger proofs. Used by some rollups to prove transactions were processed correctly.

concepts.shortDefinition: Testing whether a firm could stay within impact tolerances or survive severe but plausible disruptions, such as loss of a key supplier or a cyber attack.
concepts.bodyHtml: Testing whether a firm could stay within impact tolerances or survive severe but plausible disruptions, such as loss of a key supplier or a cyber attack.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fee charged by a card scheme to issuers and acquirers for using its network.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fee charged by a card scheme to issuers and acquirers for using its network. Unlike interchange, scheme fees are not capped in the EU or UK.

concepts.shortDefinition: A compromise between a company and its creditors, approved by the court, that binds all creditors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A compromise between a company and its creditors, approved by the court, that binds all creditors. In Irish examinership the examiner prepares one for the company’s survival.

concepts.shortDefinition: Categories of greenhouse gas emissions: scope 1 from a company's own operations, scope 2 from the energy it buys, and scope 3 from its value chain.
concepts.bodyHtml: Categories of greenhouse gas emissions: scope 1 from a company's own operations, scope 2 from the energy it buys, and scope 3 from its value chain. For financial firms, financed emissions from investments and loans fall in scope 3.

concepts.term: SCS (société en commandite simple) and SCSp (société en commandite spéciale)
concepts.shortDefinition: The Luxembourg limited partnership vehicles used for AIFs.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Luxembourg limited partnership vehicles used for AIFs. The SCS has legal personality; the société en commandite spéciale (SCSp) does not. The SCSp is widely used for private equity, real estate and infrastructure funds, either unregulated or as a reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF), specialised investment fund (SIF), Part II UCI or SICAR.
concepts.sortKey: scs (société en commandite simple) and scsp (société en commandite spéciale)

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2015/2366), the EU's main law on payment services.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2015/2366), the EU's main law on payment services. It sets the rules for authorising payment institutions, the information and rights of payment users, liability for unauthorised payments, strong customer authentication and access to payment accounts for account information and payment initiation services (open banking). It is being replaced by the Third Payment Services Directive (PSD3) and the Payment Services Regulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: The purchase and sale of existing interests in private funds or portfolio companies, giving investors liquidity before a fund ends.
concepts.bodyHtml: The purchase and sale of existing interests in private funds or portfolio companies, giving investors liquidity before a fund ends. LP-led secondaries are sales by investors; GP-led secondaries are transactions organised by the manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: A private equity fund that buys existing interests in other private equity funds from investors wishing to sell them.
concepts.bodyHtml: A private equity fund that buys existing interests in other private equity funds from investors wishing to sell them.

concepts.shortDefinition: The market in which securities are traded between investors after they have been issued, providing liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: The market in which securities are traded between investors after they have been issued, providing liquidity. Exchange traded fund (ETF) shares are traded on the secondary market on exchanges or over the counter (OTC).

concepts.shortDefinition: Sanctions that target non-US persons for dealing with sanctioned parties, even with no US connection, used mainly by the US.
concepts.bodyHtml: Sanctions that target non-US persons for dealing with sanctioned parties, even with no US connection, used mainly by the US.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK requirement since February 2024 that authorised firms must have the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) permission before approving financial promotions for unauthorised persons.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK requirement since February 2024 that authorised firms must have the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) permission before approving financial promotions for unauthorised persons.

concepts.shortDefinition: Sanctions restricting specific activities with certain sectors of a country's economy, such as financing for energy or defence firms, rather than freezing all assets of named persons.
concepts.bodyHtml: Sanctions restricting specific activities with certain sectors of a country's economy, such as financing for energy or defence firms, rather than freezing all assets of named persons.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Secured Overnight Financing Rate, the US dollar risk-free reference rate based on overnight repo transactions backed by US Treasuries.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Secured Overnight Financing Rate, the US dollar risk-free reference rate based on overnight repo transactions backed by US Treasuries. It replaced US dollar London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).

concepts.term: Securities and Exchange Board of India
concepts.shortDefinition: India's securities markets regulator, which oversees exchanges, intermediaries, mutual funds, alternative investment funds and foreign portfolio investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: India's securities markets regulator, which oversees exchanges, intermediaries, mutual funds, alternative investment funds and foreign portfolio investors.
concepts.sortKey: securities and exchange board of india

concepts.shortDefinition: The US Securities and Exchange Commission, the federal regulator of securities markets, investment advisers and investment companies.
concepts.bodyHtml: The US Securities and Exchange Commission, the federal regulator of securities markets, investment advisers and investment companies. It regulates crypto-assets that are securities and approved spot bitcoin and ether exchange-traded products.

concepts.shortDefinition: Hong Kong's securities and futures regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Hong Kong's securities and futures regulator. It licenses intermediaries, authorises funds offered to the public, and licenses virtual asset trading platforms.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transaction in which securities are used to borrow cash or other securities, such as securities lending, repo and reverse repo transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transaction in which securities are used to borrow cash or other securities, such as securities lending, repo and reverse repo transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2015/2365), which requires securities lending, repo and similar transactions to be reported to a trade repository (for funds, by the management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM)), their use to be disclosed in the prospectus and periodic reports, and collateral to be re-used only with prior consent.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2015/2365), which requires securities lending, repo and similar transactions to be reported to a trade repository (for funds, by the management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM)), their use to be disclosed in the prospectus and periodic reports, and collateral to be re-used only with prior consent.

concepts.shortDefinition: Lending securities from a fund’s portfolio to a borrower, such as a bank or broker, for a fee, against collateral worth more than the securities lent.
concepts.bodyHtml: Lending securities from a fund’s portfolio to a borrower, such as a bank or broker, for a fee, against collateral worth more than the securities lent.

concepts.shortDefinition: A financial instrument, such as a share or bond, issued by a company, financial institution or government to raise capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: A financial instrument, such as a share or bond, issued by a company, financial institution or government to raise capital.

concepts.shortDefinition: A right given to a creditor over a debtor’s asset to secure payment of a debt, allowing the creditor to look to the asset if the debt is not paid.
concepts.bodyHtml: A right given to a creditor over a debtor’s asset to secure payment of a debt, allowing the creditor to look to the asset if the debt is not paid. Common forms are the mortgage, charge, pledge and lien.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token carrying share, debt or derivative rights.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token carrying share, debt or derivative rights. It is a security under securities law, whatever it is called; in the EU, the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) excludes financial instruments.

concepts.shortDefinition: Money committed by seed investors, often the promoter itself, to a new fund at launch so that it can begin investing and grow to a viable size.
concepts.bodyHtml: Money committed by seed investors, often the promoter itself, to a new fund at launch so that it can begin investing and grow to a viable size. Seed investors may receive a seed or founder share class on favourable terms.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of 12 or 24 words from which a wallet's private keys can be regenerated.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of 12 or 24 words from which a wallet's private keys can be regenerated. Whoever has it controls the wallet.

concepts.shortDefinition: The statutory principle, in Ireland and Luxembourg, that the liabilities of one sub-fund of an umbrella can be met only out of that sub-fund’s assets and not those of other sub-funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: The statutory principle, in Ireland and Luxembourg, that the liabilities of one sub-fund of an umbrella can be met only out of that sub-fund’s assets and not those of other sub-funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Keeping client assets separate from a firm's own assets, both in the records and, ideally, in separate wallets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Keeping client assets separate from a firm's own assets, both in the records and, ideally, in separate wallets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Holding reserves apart from the issuer's own assets, on trust for holders, so that they go to holders if the issuer fails.
concepts.bodyHtml: Holding reserves apart from the issuer's own assets, on trust for holders, so that they go to holders if the issuer fails. The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) requires a statutory trust.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are held by the user, not by a service provider.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are held by the user, not by a service provider. Transfers to and from self-hosted wallets are subject to risk-based anti-money-laundering controls under the Travel Rule.

concepts.shortDefinition: Steps a crypto service provider takes to confirm a client owns or controls a self-hosted wallet, as required in the EU for transfers above €1,000.
concepts.bodyHtml: Steps a crypto service provider takes to confirm a client owns or controls a self-hosted wallet, as required in the EU for transfers above €1,000. Methods include a small test transfer (a 'Satoshi test') or signing a message with the wallet's key.

concepts.shortDefinition: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate management company (ManCo) and is itself authorised as, and subject to the rules for, a ManCo.
concepts.bodyHtml: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate management company (ManCo) and is itself authorised as, and subject to the rules for, a ManCo. Also called an internally managed fund; a corporate fund of this type is known as a self-managed investment company (SMIC). Self-management is now uncommon.

concepts.shortDefinition: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate management company (ManCo) and is itself authorised and regulated as a ManCo.
concepts.bodyHtml: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate management company (ManCo) and is itself authorised and regulated as a ManCo. Such funds are now uncommon.

concepts.shortDefinition: A category used in some EU fund regimes for investors who are not professional clients but invest a large minimum amount, such as €100,000 or more, and confirm they understand the risks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A category used in some EU fund regimes for investors who are not professional clients but invest a large minimum amount, such as €100,000 or more, and confirm they understand the risks. Luxembourg's well-informed investor is an example.

concepts.shortDefinition: The element of the Irish the Individual Accountability Framework (IAF) that requires firms to map responsibilities to senior individuals.
concepts.bodyHtml: The element of the Irish the Individual Accountability Framework (IAF) that requires firms to map responsibilities to senior individuals. It has applied since 1 July 2024 only to credit institutions, insurers and certain investment firms, not to fund management companies (FMCs).

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent non-executive director appointed to act as a sounding board for the chair, lead the chair's appraisal and serve as an intermediary for other directors and shareholders when needed.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent non-executive director appointed to act as a sounding board for the chair, lead the chair's appraisal and serve as an intermediary for other directors and shareholders when needed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The individuals who effectively conduct a management company (ManCo)’s business.
concepts.bodyHtml: The individuals who effectively conduct a management company (ManCo)’s business. They must be of good repute and sufficiently experienced, and since 16 April 2026 at least two must be employed or engaged full-time and resident in the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the UK Senior Managers and Certification Regime, a role designated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) or the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), such as chief executive or chair, that requires regulatory approval before appointment and carries a statement of responsibilities.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the UK Senior Managers and Certification Regime, a role designated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) or the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), such as chief executive or chair, that requires regulatory approval before appointment and carries a statement of responsibilities.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK regime that makes senior individuals at financial firms personally accountable.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK regime that makes senior individuals at financial firms personally accountable. Senior managers are approved by the regulator and have defined responsibilities, certified staff are assessed as fit and proper by their firm, and conduct rules apply to most staff.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standard euro credit transfer scheme across the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), settling within one business day.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standard euro credit transfer scheme across the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), settling within one business day.

concepts.shortDefinition: The euro direct debit schemes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The euro direct debit schemes. Under SEPA Core, consumers have an unconditional right to a refund within eight weeks; the business-to-business scheme has no refund right.

concepts.shortDefinition: The European scheme for euro credit transfers that reach the payee within ten seconds, at any time of day, every day.
concepts.bodyHtml: The European scheme for euro credit transfers that reach the payee within ten seconds, at any time of day, every day. The Instant Payments Regulation requires payment providers that offer euro transfers to offer instant transfers too.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bespoke arrangement, usually for an institutional investor, under which a manager manages assets for that investor alone rather than pooling them in a fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bespoke arrangement, usually for an institutional investor, under which a manager manages assets for that investor alone rather than pooling them in a fund. Also called a segregated mandate.

concepts.shortDefinition: The operator that orders transactions on a layer 2.
concepts.bodyHtml: The operator that orders transactions on a layer 2. A single sequencer is a central point of control and failure.

concepts.shortDefinition: A third party appointed by a fund or its management company (ManCo) to perform tasks supporting its management, administration or marketing, such as the administrator, transfer agent (TA), distributor, external valuer or auditor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A third party appointed by a fund or its management company (ManCo) to perform tasks supporting its management, administration or marketing, such as the administrator, transfer agent (TA), distributor, external valuer or auditor.

concepts.shortDefinition: The counterbalancing of mutual debts between two parties so that only the net amount is payable.
concepts.bodyHtml: The counterbalancing of mutual debts between two parties so that only the net amount is payable. It may arise by contract or by implication and can operate like a form of security. In derivatives it is often called netting, and the Irish Netting of Financial Contracts Act 1995 preserves contractual netting in an insolvency.

concepts.shortDefinition: The completion of a transaction by the exchange of cash for securities or for units or shares.
concepts.bodyHtml: The completion of a transaction by the exchange of cash for securities or for units or shares. EU securities trades on trading venues settle two business days after the trade (T+2) until 11 October 2027, when the cycle shortens to one (T+1).

concepts.shortDefinition: The point at which a transfer cannot be reversed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The point at which a transfer cannot be reversed. On public blockchains it is probabilistic or protocol-defined, not legal.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive 98/26/EC), which protects transfer orders and collateral in designated payment and securities settlement systems from being unwound if a participant becomes insolvent.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive 98/26/EC), which protects transfer orders and collateral in designated payment and securities settlement systems from being unwound if a participant becomes insolvent. Amendments made in 2024 allow payment and e-money institutions to participate in designated systems.

concepts.shortDefinition: The European Commission’s proposal of 20 November 2025, not yet law, to revise the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) by replacing Articles 8 and 9 with three product categories – “transition”, “environmental, social and governance (ESG) basics” and “sustainable” – each requiring at least 70% of investments to meet the category’s objective).
concepts.bodyHtml: The European Commission’s proposal of 20 November 2025, not yet law, to revise the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) by replacing Articles 8 and 9 with three product categories – “transition”, “environmental, social and governance (ESG) basics” and “sustainable” – each requiring at least 70% of investments to meet the category’s objective).

concepts.shortDefinition: The standard disclosure templates in the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) Delegated Regulation: pre-contractual templates annexed to the prospectus of Article 8 and 9 funds (Annexes II and III) and periodic templates included in their annual reports (Annexes IV and V), applying since 1 January 2023.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standard disclosure templates in the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) Delegated Regulation: pre-contractual templates annexed to the prospectus of Article 8 and 9 funds (Annexes II and III) and periodic templates included in their annual reports (Annexes IV and V), applying since 1 January 2023.

concepts.shortDefinition: Splitting a blockchain's workload across parts of the network so it can process more in parallel.
concepts.bodyHtml: Splitting a blockchain's workload across parts of the network so it can process more in parallel. Ethereum's roadmap focuses on providing cheap data space for rollups, through designs known as danksharding.

concepts.shortDefinition: A category of units or shares in the same fund or sub-fund, sharing the same portfolio but differing in features such as currency, fees, minimum investment, investor type or distribution policy.
concepts.bodyHtml: A category of units or shares in the same fund or sub-fund, sharing the same portfolio but differing in features such as currency, fees, minimum investment, investor type or distribution policy. Assets are not segregated between share classes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The four principles in the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)’s opinion on UCITS share classes: a common investment objective reflected by a common pool of assets; non-contagion between classes; pre-determination of all features before a class is set up; and transparency of differences between classes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The four principles in the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)’s opinion on UCITS share classes: a common investment objective reflected by a common pool of assets; non-contagion between classes; pre-determination of all features before a class is set up; and transparency of differences between classes. Share classes may hedge only currency risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive that requires asset managers investing in shares traded on EEA regulated markets to publish an engagement policy on a comply-or-explain basis and report annually on how they have applied it, including how they voted.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive that requires asset managers investing in shares traded on EEA regulated markets to publish an engagement policy on a comply-or-explain basis and report annually on how they have applied it, including how they voted.

concepts.shortDefinition: A company with no significant operations or assets, which can be used legitimately or to hide ownership and launder money.
concepts.bodyHtml: A company with no significant operations or assets, which can be used legitimately or to hide ownership and launder money. A front company has some real business that is used to mix illicit funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A quantum algorithm that would break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography, letting an attacker derive a private key from a public key.
concepts.bodyHtml: A quantum algorithm that would break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography, letting an attacker derive a private key from a public key.

concepts.shortDefinition: Selling an asset the seller does not own, usually by borrowing it, in the expectation of buying it back later at a lower price.
concepts.bodyHtml: Selling an asset the seller does not own, usually by borrowing it, in the expectation of buying it back later at a lower price. In the EU it is governed by the Short Selling Regulation. A UCITS may not short sell physically and can obtain short exposure only through derivatives.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation governing short selling of shares and sovereign debt, which requires significant net short positions to be reported to regulators and, for shares, larger ones to be disclosed publicly.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation governing short selling of shares and sovereign debt, which requires significant net short positions to be reported to regulators and, for shares, larger ones to be disclosed publicly.

concepts.shortDefinition: A money market fund (MMF) whose portfolio must have a weighted average maturity (WAM) of no more than 60 days and a weighted average life (WAL) of no more than 120 days.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money market fund (MMF) whose portfolio must have a weighted average maturity (WAM) of no more than 60 days and a weighted average life (WAL) of no more than 120 days. It may be a public debt constant net asset value (CNAV), low volatility net asset value (LVNAV) or VNAV MMF.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg corporate fund with fixed capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg corporate fund with fixed capital. It cannot be a UCITS.

concepts.term: SICAR (société d’investissement en capital à risque)
aliases: société d’investissement en capital à risque
concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg vehicle for investment in risk capital, such as private equity and venture capital, reserved for well-informed investors and requiring the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg vehicle for investment in risk capital, such as private equity and venture capital, reserved for well-informed investors and requiring the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval. It is not subject to risk-spreading.
concepts.sortKey: sicar (société d’investissement en capital à risque)

concepts.shortDefinition: The main Luxembourg corporate fund, whose capital always equals its net assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The main Luxembourg corporate fund, whose capital always equals its net assets. It can be a UCITS, a Part II fund, a specialised investment fund (SIF) or a reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF), may be self-managed or appoint a management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM), and may be an umbrella with segregated compartments.
