concepts.shortDefinition: An agreement between a fund or its manager and a particular investor giving that investor terms different from those of other investors, for example on fees or reporting.
concepts.bodyHtml: An agreement between a fund or its manager and a particular investor giving that investor terms different from those of other investors, for example on fees or reporting. The revised AIF Rulebook requires side letters to be disclosed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The separation, in exceptional circumstances, of assets that have become illiquid or hard to value, or whose legal or economic features have changed significantly, from the rest of a fund’s assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The separation, in exceptional circumstances, of assets that have become illiquid or hard to value, or whose legal or economic features have changed significantly, from the rest of a fund’s assets. It is a liquidity management tool (LMT) available to alternative investment funds (AIFs), including Irish retail investor AIFs (RIAIFs), but not to UCITS.

concepts.shortDefinition: Fund tools that separate illiquid assets or limit redemptions in stress.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fund tools that separate illiquid assets or limit redemptions in stress. Without them, early redeemers leave others holding the illiquid assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A separate chain with its own validators, linked to a main chain by a bridge (e.g.
concepts.bodyHtml: A separate chain with its own validators, linked to a main chain by a bridge (e.g. Polygon proof of stake (PoS), Liquid). Not a true layer 2.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), an asset-referenced token or e-money token classified as significant by the European Banking Authority (EBA) because of its size, number of holders, transaction volumes or links with the financial system.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), an asset-referenced token or e-money token classified as significant by the European Banking Authority (EBA) because of its size, number of holders, transaction volumes or links with the financial system. Issuers face higher requirements and EBA supervision.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), a crypto-asset service provider with at least 15 million active users in the EU on average over a year.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), a crypto-asset service provider with at least 15 million active users in the EU on average over a year. It must notify its regulator, and supervision involves greater cooperation with the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA).

concepts.shortDefinition: Fraud in which criminals persuade a mobile operator to move a victim's phone number to a SIM they control, so they can receive one-time passcodes and take over accounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fraud in which criminals persuade a mobile operator to move a victim's phone number to a SIM they control, so they can receive one-time passcodes and take over accounts.

concepts.shortDefinition: Reduced customer due diligence measures permitted where the money laundering and terrorist financing risk is demonstrably low.
concepts.bodyHtml: Reduced customer due diligence measures permitted where the money laundering and terrorist financing risk is demonstrably low. Ongoing monitoring must still be carried out.

concepts.shortDefinition: The area in which euro payments, including credit transfers, direct debits and instant transfers, can be made across borders as easily as domestic payments, using common standards.
concepts.bodyHtml: The area in which euro payments, including credit transfers, direct debits and instant transfers, can be made across borders as easily as domestic payments, using common standards. It covers the EU and EEA and several other European countries.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dealing at one price for both subscriptions and redemptions, usually based on mid-market asset values.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dealing at one price for both subscriptions and redemptions, usually based on mid-market asset values.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU agency that plans and carries out the resolution of significant banks in the banking union when they fail or are likely to fail, so that they can be wound down without taxpayer bail-outs.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU agency that plans and carries out the resolution of significant banks in the banking union when they fail or are likely to fail, so that they can be wound down without taxpayer bail-outs. It manages the Single Resolution Fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU's system of banking supervision for the euro area and other participating countries, made up of the European Central Bank (ECB) and the national supervisors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU's system of banking supervision for the euro area and other participating countries, made up of the European Central Bank (ECB) and the national supervisors. The ECB directly supervises significant banks and grants all banking licences; national supervisors supervise less significant banks day to day.

concepts.shortDefinition: A review by an independent expert, required by a regulator, to examine an issue at a firm, make recommendations and oversee their implementation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A review by an independent expert, required by a regulator, to examine an issue at a firm, make recommendations and oversee their implementation. In the UK, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) can require one under section 166 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA).

concepts.shortDefinition: A table showing the skills and experience the board needs, such as sector knowledge, finance, risk, legal and regulatory, technology and anti-money laundering (AML), against what each director brings.
concepts.bodyHtml: A table showing the skills and experience the board needs, such as sector knowledge, finance, risk, legal and regulatory, technology and anti-money laundering (AML), against what each director brings. It makes gaps visible and guides appointments and training.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dollar stablecoins issued by the Sky protocol (formerly MakerDAO).
concepts.bodyHtml: Dollar stablecoins issued by the Sky protocol (formerly MakerDAO). DAI and its successor USDS are crypto-collateralised: users mint them by locking up collateral worth more than the coins issued.

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of stake, the destruction of part of a validator's stake as a penalty for provably dishonest behaviour, such as double signing.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of stake, the destruction of part of a validator's stake as a penalty for provably dishonest behaviour, such as double signing.

concepts.shortDefinition: The difference between the expected price of a trade and the price at which it is executed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The difference between the expected price of a trade and the price at which it is executed. On automated market makers, it grows with the size of the trade relative to the pool.

concepts.shortDefinition: An e-money institution below set thresholds for outstanding e-money, which may operate under a lighter national regime without an EU passport.
concepts.bodyHtml: An e-money institution below set thresholds for outstanding e-money, which may operate under a lighter national regime without an EU passport.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment institution whose monthly payment transactions are below a threshold set by its home member state, which may be registered rather than fully authorised, with lighter requirements but no EU passport.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment institution whose monthly payment transactions are below a threshold set by its home member state, which may be registered rather than fully authorised, with lighter requirements but no EU passport.

concepts.shortDefinition: Code deployed on a blockchain that runs automatically when called and that can hold and move assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Code deployed on a blockchain that runs automatically when called and that can hold and move assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Phishing by text message (smishing) or by phone call (vishing), used to trick victims into revealing credentials or making payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: Phishing by text message (smishing) or by phone call (vishing), used to trick victims into revealing credentials or making payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: Independent assurance reports on a service provider's controls.
concepts.bodyHtml: Independent assurance reports on a service provider's controls. SOC 1 covers controls relevant to financial reporting; the System and Organization Controls 2 (SOC 2) covers security and availability. A Type I report covers the design of controls at a date; a Type II report tests how they operated over a period.

concepts.shortDefinition: Manipulating people — fake recruiters, support calls, phishing, bribes — to gain access.
concepts.bodyHtml: Manipulating people — fake recruiters, support calls, phishing, bribes — to gain access. The usual first step in large thefts.

concepts.term: Sociedad gestora de instituciones de inversión colectiva
concepts.shortDefinition: A Spanish management company authorised to manage collective investment schemes, supervised by the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV).
concepts.bodyHtml: A Spanish management company authorised to manage collective investment schemes, supervised by the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV).
concepts.sortKey: sociedad gestora de instituciones de inversión colectiva

concepts.shortDefinition: An Italian asset management company authorised to manage collective investment schemes, including UCITS and alternative investment funds (AIFs).
concepts.bodyHtml: An Italian asset management company authorised to manage collective investment schemes, including UCITS and alternative investment funds (AIFs).

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg special limited partnership.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg special limited partnership. It has no legal personality and is widely used for private equity, real estate and other alternative investment funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Closing a fund to new investors while continuing to accept further investment from existing ones, usually to protect performance in a capacity-constrained strategy.
concepts.bodyHtml: Closing a fund to new investors while continuing to accept further investment from existing ones, usually to protect performance in a capacity-constrained strategy. A hard closure stops all new subscriptions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet app on a phone or computer that holds the key, often with an encrypted cloud backup.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet app on a phone or computer that holds the key, often with an encrypted cloud backup. Because the device is online, it is normally a hot wallet.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native token of Solana, a high-throughput proof-of-stake blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native token of Solana, a high-throughput proof-of-stake blockchain. SOL pays transaction fees and is staked to secure the network.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive 2009/138/EC), the EU's prudential regime for insurers, setting risk-based capital, governance and disclosure requirements.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive 2009/138/EC), the EU's prudential regime for insurers, setting risk-based capital, governance and disclosure requirements. It shapes how insurers invest, including in funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fully taxable Luxembourg holding company often used by private funds to hold investments, which can benefit from tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fully taxable Luxembourg holding company often used by private funds to hold investments, which can benefit from tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.

concepts.shortDefinition: A six-digit UK code identifying the bank and branch holding an account, used with the account number for domestic payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A six-digit UK code identifying the bank and branch holding an account, used with the account number for domestic payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A non-transferable token tied to a wallet, used as a badge or credential.
concepts.bodyHtml: A non-transferable token tied to a wallet, used as a badge or credential. Public, permanent and hard to revoke.

concepts.shortDefinition: The origin of the particular money or assets used in a business relationship or transaction, such as a salary, a property sale or an inheritance.
concepts.bodyHtml: The origin of the particular money or assets used in a business relationship or transaction, such as a salary, a property sale or an inheritance. Establishing it is part of enhanced due diligence.

concepts.shortDefinition: The origin of a customer's total wealth, such as business ownership, employment or inheritance.
concepts.bodyHtml: The origin of a customer's total wealth, such as business ownership, employment or inheritance. Establishing it is part of enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and other high-risk customers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A culture and arrangements in which staff feel safe to raise concerns, challenge decisions and report wrongdoing, including through whistleblowing channels.
concepts.bodyHtml: A culture and arrangements in which staff feel safe to raise concerns, challenge decisions and report wrongdoing, including through whistleblowing channels.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal entity set up for a specific, limited purpose, such as holding an investment or originating loans, often used by alternative investment funds (AIFs) to structure investments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal entity set up for a specific, limited purpose, such as holding an investment or originating loans, often used by alternative investment funds (AIFs) to structure investments.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A company set up to hold an asset; tokens are often shares in, or claims on, the SPV rather than the asset itself.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg alternative investment fund (AIF) reserved for well-informed investors, with no restriction on eligible assets but subject to risk-spreading, which requires prior the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg alternative investment fund (AIF) reserved for well-informed investors, with no restriction on eligible assets but subject to risk-spreading, which requires prior the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval.

concepts.shortDefinition: A court order requiring a party to carry out its obligations under a contract as agreed.
concepts.bodyHtml: A court order requiring a party to carry out its obligations under a contract as agreed.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank that gives payment firms indirect access to payment systems, card schemes or accounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank that gives payment firms indirect access to payment systems, card schemes or accounts. Losing a sponsor bank is one of the biggest operational risks for payment firms.

concepts.shortDefinition: Placing orders with no intention of executing them to create a false impression of supply or demand, then cancelling them once the price moves.
concepts.bodyHtml: Placing orders with no intention of executing them to create a false impression of supply or demand, then cancelling them once the price moves. It is market manipulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: An exchange-traded fund that holds a crypto-asset directly rather than through futures.
concepts.bodyHtml: An exchange-traded fund that holds a crypto-asset directly rather than through futures. US regulators approved spot bitcoin exchange traded funds (ETFs) in January 2024 and spot ether ETFs later that year; UCITS cannot hold crypto-assets directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: The gap between the price charged and a reference mid-price.
concepts.bodyHtml: The gap between the price charged and a reference mid-price. "Zero commission" usually means the money is in the spread.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto-asset designed to keep a stable value against a reference asset, usually a currency.
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto-asset designed to keep a stable value against a reference asset, usually a currency. It may be backed by reserves, by crypto collateral or by an algorithm.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Financial Stability Board (FSB)'s term for the whole set of firms around a coin — issuer, reserve manager, custodian banks, distributors, market makers, wallet providers and blockchains.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Financial Stability Board (FSB)'s term for the whole set of firms around a coin — issuer, reserve manager, custodian banks, distributors, market makers, wallet providers and blockchains. A failure at any of them can break the coin.

concepts.shortDefinition: Doubt about reserves leads holders to sell or redeem at once, forcing reserve sales and a fall below par.
concepts.bodyHtml: Doubt about reserves leads holders to sell or redeem at once, forcing reserve sales and a fall below par. Usually without deposit insurance or a lender of last resort; transparency speeds it up.

concepts.shortDefinition: The owner of tokens who puts them behind a validator and shares the rewards and penalties.
concepts.bodyHtml: The owner of tokens who puts them behind a validator and shares the rewards and penalties. Clients of a staking service bear slashing and lock-up risk unless the contract says otherwise.

concepts.shortDefinition: Locking up coins to help secure a proof of stake network, in return for rewards.
concepts.bodyHtml: Locking up coins to help secure a proof of stake network, in return for rewards.

sectorNotes.defi: In DeFi, staking also describes locking tokens in a protocol's smart contracts to earn a share of fees or incentives, often through liquid staking or restaking protocols. This adds smart-contract risk to the network's own penalties.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that runs validators using other people's tokens, for a fee.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that runs validators using other people's tokens, for a fee. Custodians and exchanges often provide staking, which brings outsourcing and concentration risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: A provider pools customers' tokens, stakes them with validators and passes on rewards less a commission.
concepts.bodyHtml: A provider pools customers' tokens, stakes them with validators and passes on rewards less a commission. It may need a virtual asset service provider (VASP) licence depending on the facts and for whom it is done.

concepts.shortDefinition: A price that no longer reflects an asset’s current value because the asset has not traded recently, for example because it has been suspended, delisted or become illiquid.
concepts.bodyHtml: A price that no longer reflects an asset’s current value because the asset has not traded recently, for example because it has been suspended, delisted or become illiquid. Valuation procedures must deal with it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The simplest fund structure: a single fund with no structural connection to any other fund, with its own prospectus, service contracts and authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The simplest fund structure: a single fund with no structural connection to any other fund, with its own prospectus, service contracts and authorisation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A money market fund (MMF) that may hold assets with longer maturities than a short-term MMF, subject to a weighted average maturity (WAM) of no more than six months and a weighted average life (WAL) of no more than 12 months.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money market fund (MMF) that may hold assets with longer maturities than a short-term MMF, subject to a weighted average maturity (WAM) of no more than six months and a weighted average life (WAL) of no more than 12 months. It must be a VNAV MMF.

concepts.shortDefinition: An instruction from a payer to their bank to make regular payments of a fixed amount to a payee.
concepts.bodyHtml: An instruction from a payer to their bank to make regular payments of a fixed amount to a payee.

concepts.shortDefinition: An off-chain arrangement in which parties lock funds on-chain, transact privately between themselves and settle only the final balance on the blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: An off-chain arrangement in which parties lock funds on-chain, transact privately between themselves and settle only the final balance on the blockchain. The Lightning Network uses payment channels for Bitcoin.

concepts.shortDefinition: A document setting out the responsibilities of a senior manager, submitted to the regulator under the UK Senior Managers Regime and Ireland's Senior Executive Accountability Regime.
concepts.bodyHtml: A document setting out the responsibilities of a senior manager, submitted to the regulator under the UK Senior Managers Regime and Ireland's Senior Executive Accountability Regime.

concepts.shortDefinition: The annual audit of financial statements required by law, carried out by a registered auditor.
concepts.bodyHtml: The annual audit of financial statements required by law, carried out by a registered auditor. For funds, the auditor also reports certain breaches to the regulator.

concepts.shortDefinition: A statutory instrument: UK secondary legislation made by ministers under powers in an Act of Parliament.
concepts.bodyHtml: A statutory instrument: UK secondary legislation made by ministers under powers in an Act of Parliament. Much of UK financial regulation, including the Cryptoassets Regulations 2026, is made by statutory instrument.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Sterling Overnight Index Average, the risk-free reference rate for sterling, based on overnight unsecured lending.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Sterling Overnight Index Average, the risk-free reference rate for sterling, based on overnight unsecured lending. It is published by the Bank of England and replaced sterling London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).

concepts.shortDefinition: The responsible oversight of the companies in which a fund invests, including monitoring, engagement and voting, to protect and enhance long-term value for investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The responsible oversight of the companies in which a fund invests, including monitoring, engagement and voting, to protect and enhance long-term value for investors. Under the Shareholder Rights Directive II (SRD II) asset managers must publish an engagement policy on a comply-or-explain basis, and UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must have a strategy for exercising voting rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: Codes setting standards for how investors monitor, engage with and vote at the companies they invest in.
concepts.bodyHtml: Codes setting standards for how investors monitor, engage with and vote at the companies they invest in. The UK Stewardship Code is voluntary and applied by asset managers and owners on an apply-and-explain basis; other countries have similar codes.

concepts.shortDefinition: A regulated exchange on which shares, bonds, exchange traded funds (ETFs) and other securities are listed and traded.
concepts.bodyHtml: A regulated exchange on which shares, bonds, exchange traded funds (ETFs) and other securities are listed and traded. Listed funds must comply with its rules and filing obligations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The automated passing of orders, prices and settlement instructions between systems without manual re-keying, which reduces errors and costs.
concepts.bodyHtml: The automated passing of orders, prices and settlement instructions between systems without manual re-keying, which reduces errors and costs.

concepts.shortDefinition: Testing how a firm, fund or portfolio would cope with severe but plausible adverse scenarios, such as a market crash, a spike in redemptions or the failure of a counterparty.
concepts.bodyHtml: Testing how a firm, fund or portfolio would cope with severe but plausible adverse scenarios, such as a market crash, a spike in redemptions or the failure of a counterparty. Results are used to set limits, plan responses and inform the board.

concepts.shortDefinition: The obligation of a UCITS depositary, and an Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) depositary, to return an identical asset or the corresponding amount without undue delay if a financial instrument held in custody is lost, unless the loss resulted from an external event beyond its reasonable control.
concepts.bodyHtml: The obligation of a UCITS depositary, and an Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) depositary, to return an identical asset or the corresponding amount without undue delay if a financial instrument held in custody is lost, unless the loss resulted from an external event beyond its reasonable control.

concepts.shortDefinition: The requirement under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) (and in future the PSR) that payment service providers verify a customer's identity using at least two independent elements: something they know (such as a password), something they have (such as a phone) and something they are (such as a fingerprint).
concepts.bodyHtml: The requirement under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) (and in future the PSR) that payment service providers verify a customer's identity using at least two independent elements: something they know (such as a password), something they have (such as a phone) and something they are (such as a fingerprint).

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund, such as a structured UCITS, whose return is determined by a pre-set formula linked to the performance of assets or indices, often with capital protection provided through derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund, such as a structured UCITS, whose return is determined by a pre-set formula linked to the performance of assets or indices, often with capital protection provided through derivatives. Structured UCITS are complex products under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II).

concepts.shortDefinition: Splitting transfers into smaller amounts to stay below an alert, enhanced due diligence or Travel Rule threshold.
concepts.bodyHtml: Splitting transfers into smaller amounts to stay below an alert, enhanced due diligence or Travel Rule threshold. A classic the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) red-flag indicator.

concepts.shortDefinition: When a fund's actual investments move away from its stated investment objective, strategy or style, for example a value fund buying growth stocks or a liquid fund building up illiquid holdings.
concepts.bodyHtml: When a fund's actual investments move away from its stated investment objective, strategy or style, for example a value fund buying growth stocks or a liquid fund building up illiquid holdings. It can mislead investors about the risks they are taking.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity to which a fund depositary delegates the custody of some of a fund’s assets, often in a particular market.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity to which a fund depositary delegates the custody of some of a fund’s assets, often in a particular market. The fund depositary remains liable for the assets; a prime broker holding a hedge fund’s assets acts as sub-custodian.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A firm appointed by the custodian that holds keys or wallets. A technology vendor that can sign, block or recover transactions is acting as a sub-custodian in substance.

concepts.shortDefinition: The further delegation of a delegated function or task by a delegate, such as an investment manager appointing a sub-investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: The further delegation of a delegated function or task by a delegate, such as an investment manager appointing a sub-investment manager. It is subject to the same conditions as delegation and to the management company (ManCo)’s consent and oversight.

concepts.shortDefinition: A separate compartment of an umbrella fund with its own portfolio, investment policy and assets and liabilities, described in its own prospectus supplement.
concepts.bodyHtml: A separate compartment of an umbrella fund with its own portfolio, investment policy and assets and liabilities, described in its own prospectus supplement. Also called a compartment.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIFM whose assets under management do not exceed the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) thresholds of €100 million, or €500 million for unleveraged AIFs with no redemption rights for five years.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIFM whose assets under management do not exceed the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) thresholds of €100 million, or €500 million for unleveraged AIFs with no redemption rights for five years. It must register and report to its regulator but is not subject to the full AIFMD unless it opts in. Also called an exempt AIFM.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which an investor puts money (or, exceptionally, assets) into a fund and receives newly issued units or shares in return.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which an investor puts money (or, exceptionally, assets) into a fund and receives newly issued units or shares in return.

concepts.shortDefinition: Paying for fund units by transferring securities or other assets rather than cash.
concepts.bodyHtml: Paying for fund units by transferring securities or other assets rather than cash. The assets must fit the fund's investment policy and be valued fairly so that existing investors are not disadvantaged.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short-term loan to a private fund secured on investors' uncalled commitments, used to make investments before capital is called.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short-term loan to a private fund secured on investors' uncalled commitments, used to make investments before capital is called. It can flatter reported returns by shortening the time investors' money is invested.

concepts.shortDefinition: The annual tax (taxe d’abonnement) paid by Luxembourg funds on their NAV, generally 0.05%, reduced to 0.01% for money market funds (MMFs), specialised investment funds (SIFs) and institutional share classes, with exemptions for some fund types.
concepts.bodyHtml: The annual tax (taxe d’abonnement) paid by Luxembourg funds on their NAV, generally 0.05%, reduced to 0.01% for money market funds (MMFs), specialised investment funds (SIFs) and institutional share classes, with exemptions for some fund types. It is a cost borne by investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The human and technical resources a management company (ManCo) must have in its home state to control the funds it manages and oversee its delegates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The human and technical resources a management company (ManCo) must have in its home state to control the funds it manages and oversee its delegates. Since 16 April 2026, at least two persons conducting its business must be employed or engaged full-time and resident in the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: Planning for the replacement of the chair, directors and key executives, both in an orderly way over time and in an emergency.
concepts.bodyHtml: Planning for the replacement of the chair, directors and key executives, both in an orderly way over time and in an emergency. Good succession plans set out the skills needed, possible candidates and a timetable.

concepts.shortDefinition: A venue that takes over the clients and liquidity of a sanctioned or closed exchange, as Grinex did for Garantex.
concepts.bodyHtml: A venue that takes over the clients and liquidity of a sanctioned or closed exchange, as Grinex did for Garantex. Sanctions screening needs to follow successor venues and their tokens.

concepts.shortDefinition: A type of zero-knowledge proof that is short and quick to verify.
concepts.bodyHtml: A type of zero-knowledge proof that is short and quick to verify. Many SNARKs need a trusted setup ceremony; they are widely used in zero-knowledge rollups and privacy protocols.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) assessment that a firm giving investment advice or managing a portfolio must carry out of a client’s knowledge and experience, financial situation, objectives and sustainability preferences, so that only suitable funds are recommended.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) assessment that a firm giving investment advice or managing a portfolio must carry out of a client’s knowledge and experience, financial situation, objectives and sustainability preferences, so that only suitable funds are recommended.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk measure in the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID) that ranks a product on a scale from 1 (lower risk) to 7 (higher risk), combining market risk and credit risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk measure in the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID) that ranks a product on a scale from 1 (lower risk) to 7 (higher risk), combining market risk and credit risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Travel Rule takes effect at different times in different countries, so a counterparty may be unable to send or receive the required information.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Travel Rule takes effect at different times in different countries, so a counterparty may be unable to send or receive the required information. Firms must decide, and record, how they handle such transfers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A management company (ManCo) authorised both as a UCITS ManCo and as an alternative investment fund manager (AIFM), allowing a single fund management group to manage both its UCITS and its AIFs; also called a universal ManCo.
concepts.bodyHtml: A management company (ManCo) authorised both as a UCITS ManCo and as an alternative investment fund manager (AIFM), allowing a single fund management group to manage both its UCITS and its AIFs; also called a universal ManCo. Each fund or umbrella is still either a UCITS or an AIF. Super ManCos are common in Ireland and Luxembourg. It can be either a proprietary ManCo or a third-party ManCo.

concepts.shortDefinition: A standing arrangement for the supervisors of a cross-border group to share information and coordinate, backed by MoUs.
concepts.bodyHtml: A standing arrangement for the supervisors of a cross-border group to share information and coordinate, backed by MoUs. Essential when the keys, reserves or operations sit abroad.

concepts.shortDefinition: The regular reporting of information by managers to their NCA, such as AIFMD reporting on each alternative investment fund (AIF)’s exposures, leverage and liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: The regular reporting of information by managers to their NCA, such as AIFMD reporting on each alternative investment fund (AIF)’s exposures, leverage and liquidity. From 16 April 2027, enhanced reporting under AIFMD II includes delegation arrangements.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which EU supervisors assess a firm's business model, governance, risks and capital and liquidity adequacy, and may set additional requirements.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which EU supervisors assess a firm's business model, governance, risks and capital and liquidity adequacy, and may set additional requirements.

concepts.shortDefinition: The compromise of a supplier - a device, firmware, software library, reseller or vendor - that reaches every one of its customers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The compromise of a supplier - a device, firmware, software library, reseller or vendor - that reaches every one of its customers. Examples include the Ledger Connect Kit attack (2023) and the Bybit hack through Safe{Wallet} (2025).

concepts.shortDefinition: Charging a customer extra for using a particular payment method.
concepts.bodyHtml: Charging a customer extra for using a particular payment method. In the EU, surcharging on consumer cards and on Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) transfers and direct debits is banned.

concepts.shortDefinition: The temporary halting of subscriptions and redemptions, permitted only in exceptional circumstances where justified in investors’ interests.
concepts.bodyHtml: The temporary halting of subscriptions and redemptions, permitted only in exceptional circumstances where justified in investors’ interests. It is a tool of last resort, and the regulator must be notified without delay.

concepts.shortDefinition: A report to the Financial Intelligence Unit where a firm knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing (the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 20).
concepts.bodyHtml: A report to the Financial Intelligence Unit where a firm knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing (the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 20). The threshold is low. A useful crypto report names the typology and attaches addresses, transaction hashes and the trace.

concepts.shortDefinition: A report that firms arranging or executing transactions must submit to their regulator when they reasonably suspect an order or transaction may constitute market abuse.
concepts.bodyHtml: A report that firms arranging or executing transactions must submit to their regulator when they reasonably suspect an order or transaction may constitute market abuse.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK regime for sustainability-related claims and product labels for investment funds and other products.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK regime for sustainability-related claims and product labels for investment funds and other products. It includes an anti-greenwashing rule for all FCA-authorised firms, four voluntary labels and disclosure and naming and marketing rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: Environmental, social and employee matters, respect for human rights, and anti-corruption and anti-bribery matters.
concepts.bodyHtml: Environmental, social and employee matters, respect for human rights, and anti-corruption and anti-bribery matters.

concepts.shortDefinition: A client’s choice, which the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) advisers and portfolio managers must ask about in the suitability assessment, for a minimum proportion of Taxonomy-aligned investments, a minimum proportion of sustainable investments, or consideration of principal adverse impactses (PAIs)).
concepts.bodyHtml: A client’s choice, which the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II) advisers and portfolio managers must ask about in the suitability assessment, for a minimum proportion of Taxonomy-aligned investments, a minimum proportion of sustainable investments, or consideration of principal adverse impactses (PAIs)).

concepts.shortDefinition: An environmental, social or governance event or condition that, if it occurs, could cause an actual or a potential material negative impact on the value of an investment.
concepts.bodyHtml: An environmental, social or governance event or condition that, if it occurs, could cause an actual or a potential material negative impact on the value of an investment. It looks inwards, at the effect of environmental, social and governance (ESG) events on the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The requirement, since 1 August 2022 under the amended UCITS and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) delegated rules, for UCITS management companies (ManCos) and AIFMs to integrate sustainability risks into their organisation, risk management, due diligence and conflicts of interest processes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The requirement, since 1 August 2022 under the amended UCITS and the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) delegated rules, for UCITS management companies (ManCos) and AIFMs to integrate sustainability risks into their organisation, risk management, due diligence and conflicts of interest processes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2019/2088), applying since 10 March 2021, which requires financial market participants, including UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs), to disclose how they integrate sustainability risks and consider principal adverse impactses (PAIs), at entity and product level.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2019/2088), applying since 10 March 2021, which requires financial market participants, including UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs), to disclose how they integrate sustainability risks and consider principal adverse impactses (PAIs), at entity and product level. Funds are commonly classified under it as Article 6, 8 or 9 funds).

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), an investment in an economic activity that contributes to an environmental or social objective, does not significantly harm any such objective, and whose investee companies follow good governance practices.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), an investment in an economic activity that contributes to an environmental or social objective, does not significantly harm any such objective, and whose investee companies follow good governance practices.

concepts.shortDefinition: A derivative in which two parties exchange payment streams, such as fixed for floating interest or the return on an index for a fixed or floating rate.
concepts.bodyHtml: A derivative in which two parties exchange payment streams, such as fixed for floating interest or the return on an index for a fixed or floating rate. Synthetic exchange traded funds (ETFs) use swaps to obtain an index’s return.

aliases: Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication
concepts.shortDefinition: The cooperative that runs the main global messaging network that banks use to send payment and securities instructions to each other.
concepts.bodyHtml: The cooperative that runs the main global messaging network that banks use to send payment and securities instructions to each other. Its messages carry payer and payee information required under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) travel rule for wire transfers.

concepts.shortDefinition: Adjusting a fund’s NAV by a swing factor, upwards on net subscriptions and downwards on net redemptions, so that dealing costs fall on the investors who trade.
concepts.bodyHtml: Adjusting a fund’s NAV by a swing factor, upwards on net subscriptions and downwards on net redemptions, so that dealing costs fall on the investors who trade. Under partial swing pricing the adjustment applies only when net flows exceed a set threshold. It is an anti-dilution liquidity management tool (LMT).

concepts.shortDefinition: Switzerland's integrated financial regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Switzerland's integrated financial regulator. It supervises banks, insurers, securities firms, asset managers, fund management companies, collective investment schemes and financial market infrastructures, including distributed ledger technology (DLT) trading facilities.

concepts.shortDefinition: Redeeming units or shares in one sub-fund or share class and using the proceeds to buy units or shares in another of the same umbrella, usually without initial charges.
concepts.bodyHtml: Redeeming units or shares in one sub-fund or share class and using the proceeds to buy units or shares in another of the same umbrella, usually without initial charges. Also called exchanging or converting.

concepts.shortDefinition: An attack in which one actor creates many fake identities to gain disproportionate influence, for example over a peer-to-peer network, a vote or an airdrop.
concepts.bodyHtml: An attack in which one actor creates many fake identities to gain disproportionate influence, for example over a peer-to-peer network, a vote or an airdrop.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token that tracks the price of another asset, such as a share or commodity, without holding it, usually through collateral and oracles.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token that tracks the price of another asset, such as a share or commodity, without holding it, usually through collateral and oracles. It may be a regulated derivative.

concepts.shortDefinition: An index-tracking exchange traded fund (ETF) that obtains the return of the index through derivatives, such as swaps, rather than holding the securities, and so is exposed to counterparty risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: An index-tracking exchange traded fund (ETF) that obtains the return of the index through derivatives, such as swaps, rather than holding the securities, and so is exposed to counterparty risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: Fraud using an identity built from a mix of real and invented details, which can pass identity checks and build credit history before being used for fraud.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fraud using an identity built from a mix of real and invented details, which can pass identity checks and build credit history before being used for fraud.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token that aims for a stable value by holding crypto-assets and an offsetting short position in perpetual futures, so that price moves cancel out ("delta-neutral"), rather than by holding cash (for example Ethena's USDe).
concepts.bodyHtml: A token that aims for a stable value by holding crypto-assets and an offsetting short position in perpetual futures, so that price moves cancel out ("delta-neutral"), rather than by holding cash (for example Ethena's USDe). Its yield comes from funding rates, which can turn negative.

concepts.shortDefinition: System and Organization Controls 2: an independent assurance report on a service provider's controls over security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy.
concepts.bodyHtml: System and Organization Controls 2: an independent assurance report on a service provider's controls over security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. Firms ask for SOC 2 Type II reports from custodians and technology vendors.

concepts.shortDefinition: A sterling stablecoin that is, or is likely to become, so widely used for payments in the UK that its failure could threaten financial stability.
concepts.bodyHtml: A sterling stablecoin that is, or is likely to become, so widely used for payments in the UK that its failure could threaten financial stability. Systemic stablecoins are recognised by HM Treasury and regulated by the Bank of England; other stablecoins are regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

concepts.shortDefinition: The Eurosystem's service for settling instant payments in euro, 24 hours a day, in central bank money.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Eurosystem's service for settling instant payments in euro, 24 hours a day, in central bank money.

concepts.shortDefinition: The type of end investor whose needs, characteristics, objectives and sustainability-related objectives a fund is designed to meet.
concepts.bodyHtml: The type of end investor whose needs, characteristics, objectives and sustainability-related objectives a fund is designed to meet.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Eurosystem's platform for settling securities transactions in central bank money across European markets, used by central securities depositories.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Eurosystem's platform for settling securities transactions in central bank money across European markets, used by central securities depositories.

concepts.shortDefinition: Freezing designated persons' funds and making nothing available to them, without delay and with no risk-based discretion (the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) R.6 and R.7).
concepts.bodyHtml: Freezing designated persons' funds and making nothing available to them, without delay and with no risk-based discretion (the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) R.6 and R.7). Reports go to the sanctions authority by the route the national law sets.

concepts.term: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
concepts.shortDefinition: An industry task force set up by the Financial Stability Board that in 2017 published recommendations for climate disclosures covering governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.
concepts.bodyHtml: An industry task force set up by the Financial Stability Board that in 2017 published recommendations for climate disclosures covering governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets. The International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards have since taken them over.
concepts.sortKey: task force on climate-related financial disclosures

concepts.shortDefinition: The principle that a fund itself should not create additional tax for investors, so that their tax liability depends on where they are resident.
concepts.bodyHtml: The principle that a fund itself should not create additional tax for investors, so that their tax liability depends on where they are resident. Irish and Luxembourg funds are generally exempt from tax on their income and gains.

concepts.shortDefinition: Treatment of a fund under which its income and gains are taxed as if they accrued directly to its investors rather than to the fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: Treatment of a fund under which its income and gains are taxed as if they accrued directly to its investors rather than to the fund. Contractual funds and limited partnerships are generally tax-transparent.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that is not itself taxed, with investors taxed as if they held the underlying assets directly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that is not itself taxed, with investors taxed as if they held the underlying assets directly. Examples include partnerships and some contractual funds; it can help investors access treaty benefits.

concepts.shortDefinition: An agreement between two countries that allocates taxing rights and reduces taxes on income flowing between them, to mitigate double taxation.
concepts.bodyHtml: An agreement between two countries that allocates taxing rights and reduces taxes on income flowing between them, to mitigate double taxation. Fund domiciles develop networks of them.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment in an economic activity that qualifies as environmentally sustainable under the EU Taxonomy.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment in an economic activity that qualifies as environmentally sustainable under the EU Taxonomy. Article 8 and 9 funds disclose their minimum and actual proportion of such investments).

concepts.shortDefinition: Whether a country's laws and rules meet each the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation.
concepts.bodyHtml: Whether a country's laws and rules meet each the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation. It is necessary but not sufficient; countries with strong technical ratings can still be grey-listed for weak effectiveness.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK regime that has allowed EEA funds already marketed in the UK before Brexit to continue to be marketed while they move to recognition under the Overseas Funds Regime.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK regime that has allowed EEA funds already marketed in the UK before Brexit to continue to be marketed while they move to recognition under the Overseas Funds Regime. It closes at the end of 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: A regime that lets firms already carrying on an activity continue for a limited time while they apply for authorisation under a new regime.
concepts.bodyHtml: A regime that lets firms already carrying on an activity continue for a limited time while they apply for authorisation under a new regime. The UK has used one for EEA firms after Brexit and for buy now pay later lenders from July 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short document summarising the key terms of a fund being offered to professional investors, such as its strategy, minimum commitment, investment period, drawdowns, fees and management team.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short document summarising the key terms of a fund being offered to professional investors, such as its strategy, minimum commitment, investment period, drawdowns, fees and management team.

concepts.shortDefinition: Providing or collecting funds, by any means, with the intention or knowledge that they will be used for terrorist acts or by terrorists.
concepts.bodyHtml: Providing or collecting funds, by any means, with the intention or knowledge that they will be used for terrorist acts or by terrorists. The funds can come from legitimate sources and amounts are often small.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US dollar stablecoin issued by Tether, the largest stablecoin by market value.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US dollar stablecoin issued by Tether, the largest stablecoin by market value. It is backed by reserves including US Treasury bills and is widely used for trading and cross-border transfers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The trade body for UK investment managers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The trade body for UK investment managers. It publishes industry data and runs the sector classification system used to group UK funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: One topic examined across many firms, such as critical wallet providers, to find shared weaknesses and set sector expectations.
concepts.bodyHtml: One topic examined across many firms, such as critical wallet providers, to find shared weaknesses and set sector expectations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The directive that will replace the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the E-Money Directive.
concepts.bodyHtml: The directive that will replace the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the E-Money Directive. It covers the authorisation and supervision of payment institutions, which will in future include e-money institutions, and safeguarding. Conduct rules move into the directly applicable Payment Services Regulation. Political agreement was reached in November 2025.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) mechanism under which non-EEA AIFMs and AIFs could be marketed across the EEA under a passport.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) mechanism under which non-EEA AIFMs and AIFs could be marketed across the EEA under a passport. It requires activation by the European Commission and has not been switched on, so non-EEA AIFs rely on national private placement regimes (NPPRs).

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules under which firms from outside a jurisdiction may provide services into it, often depending on an equivalence decision that the home regime is comparable.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules under which firms from outside a jurisdiction may provide services into it, often depending on an equivalence decision that the home regime is comparable.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent management company (ManCo), not part of the promoter’s group, that acts as ManCo for the funds of many unrelated promoters and typically delegates portfolio management back to the promoter as investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent management company (ManCo), not part of the promoter’s group, that acts as ManCo for the funds of many unrelated promoters and typically delegates portfolio management back to the promoter as investment manager. It differs from a proprietary ManCo, which belongs to the promoter's own group. It is sometimes called a host ManCo.

concepts.shortDefinition: In open banking, an account information or payment initiation service provider that accesses a customer's payment account held by another provider.
concepts.bodyHtml: In open banking, an account information or payment initiation service provider that accesses a customer's payment account held by another provider.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that a firm suffers losses or disruption because of a failure at a supplier, outsourcing provider or other third party, including their own subcontractors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that a firm suffers losses or disruption because of a failure at a supplier, outsourcing provider or other third party, including their own subcontractors. Firms remain responsible for functions they outsource.

concepts.shortDefinition: Advanced security testing that imitates the tactics of real attackers against a firm's live production systems, based on threat intelligence.
concepts.bodyHtml: Advanced security testing that imitates the tactics of real attackers against a firm's live production systems, based on threat intelligence. Under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), firms identified by their supervisor must carry out TLPT at least every three years.

concepts.shortDefinition: A governance model in which business functions own and manage risk (first line), the risk management and compliance functions oversee it (second line) and internal audit provides independent assurance (third line).
concepts.bodyHtml: A governance model in which business functions own and manage risk (first line), the risk management and compliance functions oversee it (second line) and internal audit provides independent assurance (third line).

concepts.shortDefinition: A daily comparison of on-chain balances (ideally from the firm's own node), the internal ledger and client statements, with every difference logged and resolved.
concepts.bodyHtml: A daily comparison of on-chain balances (ideally from the firm's own node), the internal ledger and client statements, with every difference logged and resolved.

concepts.shortDefinition: A cryptographic method in which a private key is split into shares held by different parties and a set number of them must cooperate to sign a transaction, without the full key ever being assembled.
concepts.bodyHtml: A cryptographic method in which a private key is split into shares held by different parties and a set number of them must cooperate to sign a transaction, without the full key ever being assembled. It is a form of multi-party computation used in custody.

concepts.shortDefinition: The European framework for intelligence-led red-team testing of financial firms' cyber resilience, now aligned with the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)'s threat-led penetration testing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The European framework for intelligence-led red-team testing of financial firms' cyber resilience, now aligned with the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)'s threat-led penetration testing. CBEST is the UK equivalent.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person who promotes a single investment firm's services, receives and transmits orders or gives advice under that firm's full responsibility, without its own authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person who promotes a single investment firm's services, receives and transmits orders or gives advice under that firm's full responsibility, without its own authorisation. Tied agents must be registered.

concepts.shortDefinition: A built-in delay before an approved smart contract change takes effect, giving users notice so that changes are visible before they apply.
concepts.bodyHtml: A built-in delay before an approved smart contract change takes effect, giving users notice so that changes are visible before they apply.

concepts.shortDefinition: Telling a customer or anyone else that a suspicious activity report has been made or that an investigation is under way.
concepts.bodyHtml: Telling a customer or anyone else that a suspicious activity report has been made or that an investigation is under way. It is a criminal offence in most countries.

concepts.shortDefinition: A way of providing collateral in which full ownership passes to the receiver, who must return equivalent assets when the obligation is discharged, as under an English law Credit Support Annex.
concepts.bodyHtml: A way of providing collateral in which full ownership passes to the receiver, who must return equivalent assets when the obligation is discharged, as under an English law Credit Support Annex.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The client hands over ownership and holds only a claim, so it queues as a creditor on insolvency (Celsius Earn, January 2023).

concepts.shortDefinition: A unit recorded on a blockchain - either a native coin built into the protocol (such as bitcoin or ether) or a token issued by a smart contract.
concepts.bodyHtml: A unit recorded on a blockchain - either a native coin built into the protocol (such as bitcoin or ether) or a token issued by a smart contract. Its legal rights, not its technology, decide which regulatory regime applies.

concepts.term: Token and Trusted Technology Service Provider Act
concepts.shortDefinition: Liechtenstein's law on tokens and service providers using trusted technologies such as blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: Liechtenstein's law on tokens and service providers using trusted technologies such as blockchain. It introduced a 'token container' model for representing rights on a blockchain and a registration regime for service providers, alongside the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
concepts.sortKey: token and trusted technology service provider act

concepts.shortDefinition: A project or protocol using its revenue to buy its own tokens on the market, sometimes destroying them, to support the price.
concepts.bodyHtml: A project or protocol using its revenue to buy its own tokens on the market, sometimes destroying them, to support the price.

concepts.shortDefinition: Selling crypto-assets to investors to raise funds, including initial coin offerings.
concepts.bodyHtml: Selling crypto-assets to investors to raise funds, including initial coin offerings. Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), an offer to the public in the EU requires a published white paper and, for some tokens, authorisation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A common interface that token smart contracts follow so that wallets, exchanges and applications can handle them.
concepts.bodyHtml: A common interface that token smart contracts follow so that wallets, exchanges and applications can handle them. On Ethereum, ERC-20 is the standard for fungible tokens, ERC-721 for non-fungible tokens and ERC-1155 for contracts that issue both.

concepts.shortDefinition: Arrangements that release tokens allocated to founders, staff and early investors gradually over time.
concepts.bodyHtml: Arrangements that release tokens allocated to founders, staff and early investors gradually over time. Large unlocks can push prices down, so investors watch unlock schedules closely.

concepts.shortDefinition: Representing an asset, or a right in an asset, as a token on a distributed ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: Representing an asset, or a right in an asset, as a token on a distributed ledger.

sectorNotes.funds-asset-managers: Representing fund units or shares, or the assets a fund holds, as digital tokens recorded using DLT, such as a blockchain. The legal rights of investors are unchanged.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank's deposit liability recorded on a ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank's deposit liability recorded on a ledger. Banking law applies; digital fiat is excluded from the virtual-asset definition.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund whose shares or units are represented as tokens on a distributed ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund whose shares or units are represented as tokens on a distributed ledger. The register can be native, with the ledger as the legal record, or mirrored, with tokens reflecting a traditional register.

concepts.shortDefinition: A money-market fund whose units are issued as tokens and used as on-chain cash or collateral, for example BlackRock's BUIDL, launched in March 2024.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money-market fund whose units are issued as tokens and used as on-chain cash or collateral, for example BlackRock's BUIDL, launched in March 2024.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund investing in short-term government debt whose units are issued as tokens on a blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund investing in short-term government debt whose units are issued as tokens on a blockchain. It is increasingly used as on-chain collateral and as a yield-bearing cash alternative.

concepts.shortDefinition: The economic design of a crypto-asset: supply, issuance and burning, allocation, vesting, utility, incentives and governance rights.
concepts.bodyHtml: The economic design of a crypto-asset: supply, issuance and burning, allocation, vesting, utility, incentives and governance rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ethical example set by the board and senior management through their words, decisions and behaviour, which strongly shapes culture.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ethical example set by the board and senior management through their words, decisions and behaviour, which strongly shapes culture.

concepts.shortDefinition: A measure of a fund’s annual operating costs as a percentage of its average NAV, commonly quoted for exchange traded funds (ETFs).
concepts.bodyHtml: A measure of a fund’s annual operating costs as a percentage of its average NAV, commonly quoted for exchange traded funds (ETFs). It is broadly equivalent to the ongoing charges figure (OCF).

concepts.shortDefinition: A derivative in which one party pays the total economic return of an asset, including income and price changes, in exchange for a fixed or floating payment.
concepts.bodyHtml: A derivative in which one party pays the total economic return of an asset, including income and price changes, in exchange for a fixed or floating payment. Funds that use them must disclose them under the Securities Financing Transactions Regulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: The value of assets deposited in a decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol or network.
concepts.bodyHtml: The value of assets deposited in a decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol or network.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Polish investment fund company that creates and manages investment funds, supervised by the Komisja Nadzoru Finansowego (KNF).
concepts.bodyHtml: A Polish investment fund company that creates and manages investment funds, supervised by the Komisja Nadzoru Finansowego (KNF).

concepts.shortDefinition: The difference between the return of an index fund, such as an index exchange traded fund (ETF), and the return of the index it tracks, over a period.
concepts.bodyHtml: The difference between the return of an index fund, such as an index exchange traded fund (ETF), and the return of the index it tracks, over a period. Tracking error is the volatility of this difference.

concepts.shortDefinition: The volatility of the tracking difference, which is the gap between an index fund’s return and the return of its index.
concepts.bodyHtml: The volatility of the tracking difference, which is the gap between an index fund’s return and the return of its index. Managers of passive funds seek to keep both low.

concepts.shortDefinition: How a manager divides a block trade among the funds and accounts it was placed for.
concepts.bodyHtml: How a manager divides a block trade among the funds and accounts it was placed for. It must follow a fair, documented policy decided before execution, especially for partial fills.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity that centrally collects and maintains records of derivatives or securities financing transactions reported under the European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) or the Securities Financing Transactions Regulation (SFTR), for use by regulators.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity that centrally collects and maintains records of derivatives or securities financing transactions reported under the European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) or the Securities Financing Transactions Regulation (SFTR), for use by regulators.

concepts.shortDefinition: Disguising criminal proceeds through trade transactions, for example by over- or under-invoicing goods or invoicing for goods never shipped.
concepts.bodyHtml: Disguising criminal proceeds through trade transactions, for example by over- or under-invoicing goods or invoicing for goods never shipped.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), a regulated market, multilateral trading facility or organised trading facility on which financial instruments are traded.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II), a regulated market, multilateral trading facility or organised trading facility on which financial instruments are traded.

concepts.shortDefinition: Requirements that staff have the knowledge and skills for their roles, are assessed as competent and keep them up to date through continuing professional development.
concepts.bodyHtml: Requirements that staff have the knowledge and skills for their roles, are assessed as competent and keep them up to date through continuing professional development.

concepts.shortDefinition: An instruction to move value from one address to another.
concepts.bodyHtml: An instruction to move value from one address to another. Once confirmed, a blockchain transaction is usually final, with no recall and no chargeback.

concepts.shortDefinition: The costs of buying and selling a fund’s portfolio assets, such as brokerage, spreads and taxes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The costs of buying and selling a fund’s portfolio assets, such as brokerage, spreads and taxes. They reduce returns but are not part of the management fee and are excluded from the ongoing charges figure (OCF), though included in the Key Information Document (KID).

concepts.shortDefinition: Processing payments for an undisclosed business through the merchant account of an approved one, often to hide illegal sales.
concepts.bodyHtml: Processing payments for an undisclosed business through the merchant account of an approved one, often to hide illegal sales. Acquirers detect it through website monitoring and transaction analysis.

concepts.shortDefinition: Reviewing customers' transactions, manually or automatically, to detect unusual or suspicious activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Reviewing customers' transactions, manually or automatically, to detect unusual or suspicious activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract appointing a transfer agent (TA), describing its services, such as processing application forms, subscriptions and redemptions, confirming deals and maintaining the register and paying dividends.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract appointing a transfer agent (TA), describing its services, such as processing application forms, subscriptions and redemptions, confirming deals and maintaining the register and paying dividends.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entity, often the fund administrator, that maintains the register of investors and processes subscriptions, redemptions, transfers and switches, including the anti-money laundering (AML) and customer due diligence checks on investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entity, often the fund administrator, that maintains the register of investors and processes subscriptions, redemptions, transfers and switches, including the anti-money laundering (AML) and customer due diligence checks on investors.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The firm that keeps the register of a fund's or issuer's holders and processes transfers; in BUIDL, Securitize. Franklin Templeton runs its own for BENJI.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) service of transferring crypto-assets from one address or account to another on behalf of a client.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) service of transferring crypto-assets from one address or account to another on behalf of a client.

concepts.shortDefinition: Negotiable securities such as shares, bonds and other debt securities.
concepts.bodyHtml: Negotiable securities such as shares, bonds and other debt securities. They are the core eligible asset of a UCITS.

concepts.shortDefinition: A plan setting out how a company or financial institution will align its business with a path to a low-carbon economy, with targets, actions and governance.
concepts.bodyHtml: A plan setting out how a company or financial institution will align its business with a path to a low-carbon economy, with targets, actions and governance. EU and UK rules increasingly require or encourage them.

concepts.shortDefinition: The period during which crypto firms operating under national rules before 30 December 2024 could continue while applying for the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The period during which crypto firms operating under national rules before 30 December 2024 could continue while applying for the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) authorisation. Member states could allow up to 18 months, ending no later than 1 July 2026; some chose shorter periods.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which EU member states incorporate a directive into national law by a set deadline.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which EU member states incorporate a directive into national law by a set deadline. Differences in how countries transpose can lead to inconsistent rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 16 as applied to virtual assets: originator and beneficiary information must travel with a transfer between virtual asset service providers (VASPs).
concepts.bodyHtml: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 16 as applied to virtual assets: originator and beneficiary information must travel with a transfer between virtual asset service providers (VASPs).

concepts.shortDefinition: A short-term debt instrument issued by a government, sold at a discount to its face value and paying no interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short-term debt instrument issued by a government, sold at a discount to its face value and paying no interest. It is a money market instrument.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)'s earlier principle-based approach to fair treatment of customers, largely superseded by the Consumer Duty.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)'s earlier principle-based approach to fair treatment of customers, largely superseded by the Consumer Duty.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assets stay at a custodian, pledged to an exchange that mirrors the balance for trading.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assets stay at a custodian, pledged to an exchange that mirrors the balance for trading. Exposure shrinks to the unsettled amount; the legal terms decide who can release the collateral.

concepts.shortDefinition: Informal negotiations between the European Parliament, the Council of the EU and the Commission to agree the final text of an EU law.
concepts.bodyHtml: Informal negotiations between the European Parliament, the Council of the EU and the Commission to agree the final text of an EU law. A provisional agreement reached in trilogue still needs formal adoption by both co-legislators.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native token of the Tron blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native token of the Tron blockchain. Tron is widely used for low-cost tether US dollar stablecoin (USDT) transfers, including, according to law enforcement reports, by criminal networks.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standard against which an external auditor gives its opinion on financial statements.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standard against which an external auditor gives its opinion on financial statements. It is not defined, but is generally understood to mean that the accounting policies are appropriate and comply with accounting standards (“true”) and that the accounts do not distort or mislead (“fair”).

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal arrangement under which a trustee holds property as legal owner for the benefit of beneficiaries, who are the beneficial owners.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal arrangement under which a trustee holds property as legal owner for the benefit of beneficiaries, who are the beneficial owners. It is recognised by common law systems. Luxembourg recognises foreign trusts and has its own fiduciary contract, the fiducie.

concepts.shortDefinition: The document constituting a unit trust or other trust, which sets out the terms on which the assets are held and managed and the rights and obligations of the trustee, the manager and the beneficiaries.
concepts.bodyHtml: The document constituting a unit trust or other trust, which sets out the terms on which the assets are held and managed and the rights and obligations of the trustee, the manager and the beneficiaries.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal owner of property who holds it on behalf of, and carries out active duties for, beneficial owners.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal owner of property who holds it on behalf of, and carries out active duties for, beneficial owners. In a unit trust, the fund depositary acts as trustee and is the legal owner of the fund’s assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Another name for a mixer: a service that pools and redistributes crypto-assets to break the traceable link between sender and recipient.
concepts.bodyHtml: Another name for a mixer: a service that pools and redistributes crypto-assets to break the traceable link between sender and recipient.

concepts.shortDefinition: Two-factor authentication: logging in with two different types of evidence, such as a password and a code from a phone or hardware key.
concepts.bodyHtml: Two-factor authentication: logging in with two different types of evidence, such as a password and a code from a phone or hardware key. Strong customer authentication rules for payments build on the same idea.

concepts.shortDefinition: A recognised pattern of criminal use, such as scams, ransomware, hacks, sanctions evasion, darknet markets or terrorist financing.
concepts.bodyHtml: A recognised pattern of criminal use, such as scams, ransomware, hacks, sanctions evasion, darknet markets or terrorist financing.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive 2009/65/EC; the UCITS IV recast, as amended), the EU framework for UCITS.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive 2009/65/EC; the UCITS IV recast, as amended), the EU framework for UCITS. It sets product rules, management company rules, depositary rules and disclosure rules, and gives UCITS a product passport and UCITS ManCos a management passport.

concepts.shortDefinition: The 2009 recast of the UCITS Directive, which facilitated cross-border marketing, introduced the management company passport, fund mergers and master-feeder structures, and replaced the simplified prospectus with the Key Investor Information Document (KIID).
concepts.bodyHtml: The 2009 recast of the UCITS Directive, which facilitated cross-border marketing, introduced the management company passport, fund mergers and master-feeder structures, and replaced the simplified prospectus with the Key Investor Information Document (KIID).

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive (Directive 2014/91/EU), applying from 18 March 2016, which harmonised depositary eligibility, duties and liability, introduced remuneration policies for UCITS management companies (ManCos) and harmonised administrative sanctions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive (Directive 2014/91/EU), applying from 18 March 2016, which harmonised depositary eligibility, duties and liability, introduced remuneration policies for UCITS management companies (ManCos) and harmonised administrative sanctions.
