concepts.shortDefinition: The name commonly given to the amendments made to the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) by AIFMD II from 16 April 2026, covering liquidity management tools (LMTs), delegation reporting, substance and additional services.
concepts.bodyHtml: The name commonly given to the amendments made to the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) by AIFMD II from 16 April 2026, covering liquidity management tools (LMTs), delegation reporting, substance and additional services.

concepts.shortDefinition: An account in the name of an Irish umbrella fund through which subscription and redemption monies pass before shares are issued or redemption proceeds are paid.
concepts.bodyHtml: An account in the name of an Irish umbrella fund through which subscription and redemption monies pass before shares are issued or redemption proceeds are paid. Investors whose money is in it may rank as unsecured creditors of the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A single fund vehicle containing several sub-funds, each with its own investment policy and portfolio, governed by one constitutional document.
concepts.bodyHtml: A single fund vehicle containing several sub-funds, each with its own investment policy and portfolio, governed by one constitutional document. An umbrella is authorised under one regime, so it cannot mix UCITS and alternative investment fund (AIF) sub-funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Customer money that a firm has received but cannot match to a specific customer, which must still be safeguarded and promptly resolved.
concepts.bodyHtml: Customer money that a firm has received but cannot match to a specific customer, which must still be safeguarded and promptly resolved.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment the payer did not consent to, such as one made with a stolen card.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment the payer did not consent to, such as one made with a stolen card. Payment law requires the provider to refund it promptly, subject to limited liability for the payer and exceptions for fraud or gross negligence.

concepts.shortDefinition: A payment the payer did not consent to.
concepts.bodyHtml: A payment the payer did not consent to. Under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) the payer's provider must refund it by the end of the next business day, unless it suspects fraud by the payer, with limited liability for the payer unless they acted fraudulently or with gross negligence.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto-asset, such as bitcoin, that is not backed by any asset or issuer and whose value depends only on supply and demand.
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto-asset, such as bitcoin, that is not backed by any asset or issuer and whose value depends only on supply and demand.

concepts.shortDefinition: A collective investment undertaking: a vehicle that pools investors' money and invests it collectively.
concepts.bodyHtml: A collective investment undertaking: a vehicle that pools investors' money and invests it collectively. In Luxembourg, 'UCI' is the general term for regulated funds, covering UCITS and other funds.

concepts.term: Undertaking for collective investment in transferable securities
concepts.shortDefinition: An open-ended fund authorised under the UCITS Directive that raises capital from the public, invests in transferable securities and other eligible liquid assets subject to diversification rules, and entrusts its assets to an independent fund depositary.
concepts.bodyHtml: An open-ended fund authorised under the UCITS Directive that raises capital from the public, invests in transferable securities and other eligible liquid assets subject to diversification rules, and entrusts its assets to an independent fund depositary. A UCITS can be marketed to retail investors throughout the EEA under a passport.
concepts.sortKey: undertaking for collective investment in transferable securities

concepts.shortDefinition: Costs charged to a fund or its investors that are not justified by, or are disproportionate to, the service provided.
concepts.bodyHtml: Costs charged to a fund or its investors that are not justified by, or are disproportionate to, the service provided. UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) must prevent them.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US fund that buys a fixed portfolio and holds it until a set termination date, without active management.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US fund that buys a fixed portfolio and holds it until a set termination date, without active management.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund constituted under a trust deed between a management company (ManCo) and a trustee (the fund depositary), which is the legal owner of the assets on behalf of the investors (unitholders).
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund constituted under a trust deed between a management company (ManCo) and a trustee (the fund depositary), which is the legal owner of the assets on behalf of the investors (unitholders). A unit trust has no legal personality. Irish unit trusts are established under the Unit Trusts Act 1990 or, for UCITS, the UCITS Regulations.

concepts.shortDefinition: An insurance-based investment product whose value is linked to units of underlying funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: An insurance-based investment product whose value is linked to units of underlying funds. It is a packaged retail and insurance-based investment product (PRIIP) and an indirect route through which investors gain exposure to funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
concepts.bodyHtml: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Since leaving the EU, the UK has its own financial services rules, overseen by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Bank of England.

concepts.shortDefinition: The United Nations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The United Nations. UN Security Council sanctions, such as asset freezes, must be implemented by all member states and are central to targeted financial sanctions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The United States of America.
concepts.bodyHtml: The United States of America. US financial regulation is split between federal agencies such as the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and Federal Reserve, and state regulators.

concepts.shortDefinition: The instruments evidencing an investor’s interest in a fund: units in a unit trust or contractual fund, shares in a corporate fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The instruments evidencing an investor’s interest in a fund: units in a unit trust or contractual fund, shares in a corporate fund. The terms are often used interchangeably; interests in a limited partnership are partnership interests.

concepts.shortDefinition: Italy's financial intelligence unit, established within the Banca d'Italia, which receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports.
concepts.bodyHtml: Italy's financial intelligence unit, established within the Banca d'Italia, which receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIF that is not itself authorised or supervised by a regulator, such as a Luxembourg société en commandite spéciale (SCSp) not established as a specialised investment fund (SIF) or reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF).
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIF that is not itself authorised or supervised by a regulator, such as a Luxembourg société en commandite spéciale (SCSp) not established as a specialised investment fund (SIF) or reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF). Its manager may still be regulated under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD).

concepts.shortDefinition: A creditor with no security over the debtor’s assets, who ranks behind secured and preferential creditors in a liquidation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A creditor with no security over the debtor’s assets, who ranks behind secured and preferential creditors in a liquidation. A fund with cash at a failed bank, and investors whose money is in umbrella cash collection accounts, may rank as unsecured creditors.

concepts.shortDefinition: Unspent transaction output: the accounting model used by Bitcoin, in which each transaction consumes earlier outputs and creates new ones.
concepts.bodyHtml: Unspent transaction output: the accounting model used by Bitcoin, in which each transaction consumes earlier outputs and creates new ones. A wallet's balance is the total of the unspent outputs it controls.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract whose logic can be replaced while its address and balances stay the same, usually through a proxy contract.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract whose logic can be replaced while its address and balances stay the same, usually through a proxy contract. Whoever controls the upgrade key can change every rule, which is why multi-party approval and time locks matter.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract pattern in which users interact with a proxy that forwards calls to a separate logic contract, which administrators can replace to upgrade the system.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract pattern in which users interact with a proxy that forwards calls to a separate logic contract, which administrators can replace to upgrade the system. It allows bug fixes but means whoever controls the upgrade can change the rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto-asset that gives access to a good or service provided by its issuer.
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto-asset that gives access to a good or service provided by its issuer. Under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), offers of utility tokens for goods or services that already exist benefit from some exemptions.

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of stake, a participant who stakes coins and runs software to propose and attest to blocks.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of stake, a participant who stakes coins and runs software to propose and attest to blocks.

concepts.shortDefinition: A committee, usually of a management company, alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) or fund board, that oversees the valuation of fund assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A committee, usually of a management company, alternative investment fund manager (AIFM) or fund board, that oversees the valuation of fund assets. It approves valuation methods, reviews hard-to-value and stale prices and decides on price challenges and overrides, independently of portfolio management.

concepts.shortDefinition: The time at which a fund’s assets are valued to calculate the NAV for a dealing day.
concepts.bodyHtml: The time at which a fund’s assets are valued to calculate the NAV for a dealing day.

concepts.shortDefinition: The document setting out how a fund's assets are valued, including methodologies, data sources, frequency, review and escalation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The document setting out how a fund's assets are valued, including methodologies, data sources, frequency, review and escalation. Alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) and UCITS management companies must have one and apply it consistently.

concepts.shortDefinition: A tax on goods and services charged at each stage of supply.
concepts.bodyHtml: A tax on goods and services charged at each stage of supply. Fund management services are often exempt from VAT in the EU, which affects how fund fees are structured.

concepts.shortDefinition: A statistical estimate of the maximum loss a portfolio is likely to suffer over a given period at a given confidence level.
concepts.bodyHtml: A statistical estimate of the maximum loss a portfolio is likely to suffer over a given period at a given confidence level. A UCITS using VaR is normally limited to an absolute VaR of 20% of NAV or a relative VaR of twice that of a reference portfolio.

concepts.shortDefinition: The stages through which a fund is created, invested, distributed and operated, each of which is regulated – the fund as a product, the investment of its portfolio, its distribution to investors and its ongoing operation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The stages through which a fund is created, invested, distributed and operated, each of which is regulated – the fund as a product, the investment of its portfolio, its distribution to investors and its ongoing operation.

concepts.shortDefinition: The principle that a product’s costs are justified and proportionate to the benefits it delivers to investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The principle that a product’s costs are justified and proportionate to the benefits it delivers to investors. The EU Retail Investment Strategy, not yet applicable, would require manufacturers of retail investment products to assess it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A feature of many corporate funds whose share capital rises and falls automatically as shares are issued to new investors and cancelled when investors redeem, without the formalities of a normal company's capital changes.
concepts.bodyHtml: A feature of many corporate funds whose share capital rises and falls automatically as shares are issued to new investors and cancelled when investors redeem, without the formalities of a normal company's capital changes.

concepts.shortDefinition: A corporate fund whose share capital always equals its NAV, rising when investors subscribe and falling when they redeem.
concepts.bodyHtml: A corporate fund whose share capital always equals its NAV, rising when investors subscribe and falling when they redeem. Examples include the Irish collective asset-management vehicle (ICAV), the Irish investment company, the Luxembourg SICAV and the UK open-ended investment company (OEIC).

concepts.shortDefinition: A money market fund whose share price moves with the market value of its assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money market fund whose share price moves with the market value of its assets. Under the EU Money Market Funds Regulation, VNAV funds have fewer restrictions on eligible assets than constant net asset value (CNAV) and low volatility net asset value (LVNAV) funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A money market fund (MMF) that values its assets at market prices (mark-to-market or mark-to-model), so that its share price varies.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money market fund (MMF) that values its assets at market prices (mark-to-market or mark-to-model), so that its share price varies. Standard MMFs must be variable net asset value (VNAV).

concepts.shortDefinition: Open banking payments that let a customer authorise a provider to make a series of payments within agreed limits, without approving each one.
concepts.bodyHtml: Open banking payments that let a customer authorise a provider to make a series of payments within agreed limits, without approving each one. First used for moving money between a customer's own accounts, they are being extended to commercial uses.

concepts.shortDefinition: Pay that depends on performance or other conditions, such as bonuses, incentive awards and carried interest, as opposed to fixed salary.
concepts.bodyHtml: Pay that depends on performance or other conditions, such as bonuses, incentive awards and carried interest, as opposed to fixed salary. Remuneration rules require an appropriate balance with fixed pay and, for material risk takers, deferral and adjustment for risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: A change to a firm's regulatory permissions, either on its application or imposed by the regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: A change to a firm's regulatory permissions, either on its application or imposed by the regulator. A voluntary requirement is a restriction a firm agrees with the regulator, often to avoid formal action.

concepts.shortDefinition: Working out whether a crypto transfer's counterparty address belongs to another service provider, and which one, so Travel Rule information can be sent to the right recipient.
concepts.bodyHtml: Working out whether a crypto transfer's counterparty address belongs to another service provider, and which one, so Travel Rule information can be sent to the right recipient.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract that pools users' deposits and applies an automated strategy, such as lending, providing liquidity or staking, to earn a return.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract that pools users' deposits and applies an automated strategy, such as lending, providing liquidity or staking, to earn a return. Vault tokens represent each user's share.

concepts.shortDefinition: Equity finance for young, unlisted, high-growth companies.
concepts.bodyHtml: Equity finance for young, unlisted, high-growth companies. European venture capital funds (EuVECAs) and SICARs are vehicles for it).

concepts.shortDefinition: A digitally signed attestation (e.g.
concepts.bodyHtml: A digitally signed attestation (e.g. 'know your customer (KYC) passed') held by the user and checked by the firm; W3C standard v2.0 (May 2025). It proves who signed, not how well they checked.

concepts.shortDefinition: A check, before a credit transfer is sent, that the name of the payee given by the payer matches the name on the account.
concepts.bodyHtml: A check, before a credit transfer is sent, that the name of the payee given by the payer matches the name on the account. It helps prevent fraud and misdirected payments. In the UK the equivalent service is called Confirmation of Payee.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) definition, a digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and used for payment or investment.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) definition, a digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and used for payment or investment. It excludes digital representations of fiat currencies, securities and other financial assets covered elsewhere in the FATF Recommendations.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) definition, a person who, as a business, carries out one or more of five activities for or on behalf of another person - exchange between virtual assets and fiat, exchange between virtual assets, transfer, safekeeping or administration, and services related to an issuer's offer or sale.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) definition, a person who, as a business, carries out one or more of five activities for or on behalf of another person - exchange between virtual assets and fiat, exchange between virtual assets, transfer, safekeeping or administration, and services related to an issuer's offer or sale. Defined by what it does, not what it calls itself.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, which licenses and supervises virtual asset service providers in Dubai, outside the Dubai International Financial Centre.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, which licenses and supervises virtual asset service providers in Dubai, outside the Dubai International Financial Centre.

concepts.shortDefinition: An account number that routes payments into a master account, often used to collect funds for individual customers or to give a payment firm's customers their own the International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs).
concepts.bodyHtml: An account number that routes payments into a master account, often used to collect funds for individual customers or to give a payment firm's customers their own the International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs). Regulators have raised anti-money laundering (AML) concerns where the account holder is unclear.

concepts.shortDefinition: A virtual private network: an encrypted connection that hides a user's location and traffic.
concepts.bodyHtml: A virtual private network: an encrypted connection that hides a user's location and traffic. VPN use can let customers get around geographic restrictions, which is a sanctions and compliance risk for crypto platforms.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)’s approval stamp on the offering document of a Luxembourg UCITS, Part II fund or specialised investment fund (SIF).
concepts.bodyHtml: The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)’s approval stamp on the offering document of a Luxembourg UCITS, Part II fund or specialised investment fund (SIF).

concepts.shortDefinition: A token design in which holders lock tokens for a period to receive voting power and rewards that increase with the lock length, aligning governance with long-term holders.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token design in which holders lock tokens for a period to receive voting power and rewards that increase with the lock length, aligning governance with long-term holders.

concepts.shortDefinition: Identifying, prioritising and fixing weaknesses in software and systems, including applying security patches promptly.
concepts.bodyHtml: Identifying, prioritising and fixing weaknesses in software and systems, including applying security patches promptly.

concepts.shortDefinition: A customer who, because of personal circumstances such as health, life events, low resilience or low capability, is especially susceptible to harm.
concepts.bodyHtml: A customer who, because of personal circumstances such as health, life events, low resilience or low capability, is especially susceptible to harm. Regulators expect firms to identify and respond to vulnerability.

concepts.shortDefinition: Software or hardware that stores keys and lets a user see balances and sign transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Software or hardware that stores keys and lets a user see balances and sign transactions. The assets themselves stay on the blockchain.

concepts.shortDefinition: Malicious software or a scam website that tricks users into signing transactions or token approvals that let attackers empty their wallets, often sold to criminals as a service.
concepts.bodyHtml: Malicious software or a scam website that tricks users into signing transactions or token approvals that let attackers empty their wallets, often sold to criminals as a service.

concepts.shortDefinition: Online, but every movement needs human approvals and policy checks.
concepts.bodyHtml: Online, but every movement needs human approvals and policy checks. Usually refills the hot wallet within hours.

concepts.shortDefinition: A security giving the holder the right to buy a company’s shares at a specified price within a set period.
concepts.bodyHtml: A security giving the holder the right to buy a company’s shares at a specified price within a set period.

concepts.shortDefinition: Trading with oneself, or with colluding parties, to create the false appearance of volume or price movement.
concepts.bodyHtml: Trading with oneself, or with colluding parties, to create the false appearance of volume or price movement.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investment management and related services for individuals and families, usually combining discretionary or advisory portfolio management with financial planning.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investment management and related services for individuals and families, usually combining discretionary or advisory portfolio management with financial planning.

concepts.shortDefinition: The average length of time to legal maturity of all the assets of a money market fund (MMF), weighted by their relative holdings.
concepts.bodyHtml: The average length of time to legal maturity of all the assets of a money market fund (MMF), weighted by their relative holdings.

concepts.shortDefinition: The average length of time to legal maturity or, if shorter, to the next interest rate reset, of all the assets of a money market fund (MMF), weighted by their relative holdings.
concepts.bodyHtml: The average length of time to legal maturity or, if shorter, to the next interest rate reset, of all the assets of a money market fund (MMF), weighted by their relative holdings.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Luxembourg, an investor eligible to invest in a specialised investment fund (SIF) or reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF): an institutional or professional investor, or another investor who confirms in writing that they are well informed and either invests at least €100,000 (since the Law of 21 July 2023) or has their expertise certified by a regulated entity.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Luxembourg, an investor eligible to invest in a specialised investment fund (SIF) or reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF): an institutional or professional investor, or another investor who confirms in writing that they are well informed and either invests at least €100,000 (since the Law of 21 July 2023) or has their expertise certified by a regulated entity.

concepts.shortDefinition: Raising concerns about wrongdoing within an organisation, internally or to a regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Raising concerns about wrongdoing within an organisation, internally or to a regulator. Financial services rules require firms to have whistleblowing arrangements and protect whistleblowers from detriment.

concepts.shortDefinition: An exchange or wallet system operated by a technology provider under another firm's brand.
concepts.bodyHtml: An exchange or wallet system operated by a technology provider under another firm's brand. The regulated firm remains responsible, so it needs visibility of, and control over, the platform and a way to exit it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of approved addresses or users.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of approved addresses or users. Withdrawal whitelists restrict where funds can be sent; token whitelists restrict who can hold a token, which is common in tokenised funds. A whitelist is only as strong as the approvals needed to add an address.

concepts.shortDefinition: Central bank money on a ledger for use between financial institutions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Central bank money on a ledger for use between financial institutions. The safest settlement asset, but so far experimental (EIB 2021, Project Venus).

concepts.shortDefinition: A plan setting out how a firm would close its business in an orderly way, returning client money and assets and transferring or ending services, without causing harm to clients or the market.
concepts.bodyHtml: A plan setting out how a firm would close its business in an orderly way, returning client money and assets and transferring or ending services, without causing harm to clients or the market. Regulators increasingly expect payment, e-money and crypto firms to keep one up to date.

concepts.shortDefinition: Tax deducted at source from payments such as dividends or interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: Tax deducted at source from payments such as dividends or interest. In Ireland, investors who are not tax resident may receive fund distributions without it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US dollar stablecoin issued by World Liberty Financial and backed by US government securities and cash equivalents.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US dollar stablecoin issued by World Liberty Financial and backed by US government securities and cash equivalents.

concepts.shortDefinition: Wrapped bitcoin: a token on Ethereum backed one-for-one by bitcoin held by a custodian, letting bitcoin be used in Ethereum-based decentralised finance (DeFi).
concepts.bodyHtml: Wrapped bitcoin: a token on Ethereum backed one-for-one by bitcoin held by a custodian, letting bitcoin be used in Ethereum-based decentralised finance (DeFi).

concepts.shortDefinition: Wrapped ether: ether converted into an ERC-20 token so that it can be used in smart contracts that expect the ERC-20 standard.
concepts.bodyHtml: Wrapped ether: ether converted into an ERC-20 token so that it can be used in smart contracts that expect the ERC-20 standard.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token on one blockchain that represents an asset held on another, such as wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum, backed by a custodian or a bridge.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token on one blockchain that represents an asset held on another, such as wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum, backed by a custodian or a bridge. It is a different claim from the original and may not carry the original's controls or regulatory status.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a blockchain designed for fast, low-cost payments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a blockchain designed for fast, low-cost payments. XRP is used to pay transaction fees and as a bridge currency.

concepts.shortDefinition: The return on an asset, such as interest, staking rewards or trading fees, usually expressed as an annual percentage.
concepts.bodyHtml: The return on an asset, such as interest, staking rewards or trading fees, usually expressed as an annual percentage.

concepts.shortDefinition: A protocol that pools users' deposits and moves them automatically between strategies to seek the best yield, adding a layer of smart contract and strategy risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: A protocol that pools users' deposits and moves them automatically between strategies to seek the best yield, adding a layer of smart contract and strategy risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: Moving crypto-assets between decentralised finance (DeFi) protocols to earn the highest returns, often from trading fees, interest and extra token rewards.
concepts.bodyHtml: Moving crypto-assets between decentralised finance (DeFi) protocols to earn the highest returns, often from trading fees, interest and extra token rewards. It can combine several layers of risk, including smart-contract, liquidity and leverage risks.

concepts.shortDefinition: A stablecoin-like token that passes interest or other yield to holders.
concepts.bodyHtml: A stablecoin-like token that passes interest or other yield to holders. Paying interest is prohibited for e-money tokens and asset-referenced tokens under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) and for payment stablecoins under the US the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act 2025 (GENIUS Act), so such products may be regulated as investments.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native coin of Zcash, a cryptocurrency that offers optional shielded transactions using zero-knowledge proofs to hide sender, receiver and amount.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native coin of Zcash, a cryptocurrency that offers optional shielded transactions using zero-knowledge proofs to hide sender, receiver and amount.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond that pays no interest but is issued at a discount to its face value, the investor’s return being the difference between the issue price and the amount repaid.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond that pays no interest but is issued at a discount to its face value, the investor’s return being the difference between the issue price and the amount repaid.

concepts.shortDefinition: Zero-knowledge: describes cryptographic methods that prove a statement is true without revealing the information behind it, as in zero-knowledge proofs and zero-knowledge rollups.
concepts.bodyHtml: Zero-knowledge: describes cryptographic methods that prove a statement is true without revealing the information behind it, as in zero-knowledge proofs and zero-knowledge rollups.

concepts.shortDefinition: A cryptographic proof that a statement is true without revealing the underlying information.
concepts.bodyHtml: A cryptographic proof that a statement is true without revealing the underlying information.

concepts.shortDefinition: A layer 2 that posts a zero-knowledge validity proof to layer 1, so each batch is verified before it is accepted.
concepts.bodyHtml: A layer 2 that posts a zero-knowledge validity proof to layer 1, so each batch is verified before it is accepted.

acronyms.shortDefinition: A protocol used by card schemes to authenticate online card payments, often by a code or approval in the cardholder's banking app.

A firm that, with the customer's consent, collects and consolidates information from the customer's payment accounts at one or more banks or other providers, for example to show all balances in one app or to assess creditworthiness.
The bank or other provider that holds a customer's payment account.
Fraud in which a criminal gains control of a customer's account, for example by stealing credentials through phishing or a SIM swap, and uses it to make payments.
A payment that moves money directly from the payer's bank account to the payee's, without using a card network, often initiated through open banking payment initiation.
A service, such as an oracle network or a bridge, that is secured by restaked assets from a restaking protocol.
A widely used symmetric encryption algorithm, adopted as a US federal standard in 2001.
The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2024/927), which amended the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) and the UCITS Directive (UCITSD) from 16 April 2026.
A collective investment undertaking that raises capital from several investors to invest it under a defined investment policy for their benefit, and which is not a UCITS.

Bermuda's integrated financial regulator and monetary authority.
The first blockchain, launched in 2009, and its native coin (BTC).

The part of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Handbook that sets the rules for how firms protect client money and assets, including segregation, reconciliation and record keeping.

The short UCITS disclosure document introduced by UCITS IV.
A measurable value that shows how well an organisation or process is achieving a key objective.
A metric that signals a change in risk and can trigger an alert when it crosses a threshold, such as hot-wallet balances, failed withdrawals or reconciliation breaks.

Know your customer: the process of identifying and verifying customers and understanding their activities, as part of customer due diligence under anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules.
Poland's integrated financial supervisor, covering banks, insurers, capital markets, pension funds and payment institutions.
An artificial intelligence (AI) model trained on very large amounts of text to understand and generate language.
A layer 2 is a network that processes transactions off a base blockchain and settles them back to it; a layer 3 is built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.
A layer 2 is a network that processes transactions off a base blockchain and settles them back to it; a layer 3 is built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.
Lido staked ether: a liquid staking token issued by the Lido protocol in exchange for ether deposited for staking.
An exclusion from payment and e-money regulation for instruments usable only within a limited network of service providers or for a very limited range of goods or services, such as store cards.
A partnership with at least one general partner, which manages it and has unlimited liability, and limited partners, whose liability is limited to their capital contribution.
The contract governing a limited partnership fund, setting out its strategy, investment period, fees, carried interest, distributions, investor rights and the general partner's duties.
A liquid restaking token: a tradable token representing assets restaked through a restaking protocol to secure additional services.
A tradable receipt for staked tokens, such as lido staked ether (stETH) or cbETH, representing the staked asset and its rewards.

A tool used to manage redemptions in an open-ended fund, such as suspension, redemption gates, extended notice periods, redemption in kind, redemption fees, swing pricing, dual pricing, anti-dilution levies and side pockets.

The process by which a manager keeps a fund’s liquidity consistent with its redemption terms, including setting dealing terms, holding liquid assets, monitoring the investor base and liquidity stress testing.
The native coin of Litecoin, a proof-of-work cryptocurrency launched in 2011 as a faster, lighter variant of Bitcoin.
A former category of Irish qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF) permitted to originate loans.
acronyms.notes: Ireland; replaced by the AIFMD II loan origination rules

acronyms.shortDefinition: The ratio of a loan to the value of the collateral securing it.
A benchmark interest rate for interbank lending in several currencies.
The London Stock Exchange Group, which operates the London Stock Exchange and provides market data, indices and clearing services.

A UK authorised open-ended fund designed to invest in long-term, illiquid assets such as private equity, private credit, infrastructure and property, with dealing no more often than monthly and a notice period of at least 90 days.
A type of money market fund under the EU Money Market Funds Regulation whose share price can stay constant as long as the value of its assets stays within 0.2% of that price.
A committee of representatives of a private fund's largest investors that reviews conflicts of interest, valuation questions and other matters reserved to it by the partnership agreement.
The Luxembourg Stock Exchange, a major listing venue for bonds and investment funds and home to the Luxembourg Green Exchange for sustainable securities.
A branch of artificial intelligence in which systems learn patterns from data rather than following explicit rules.
Malta's single financial services regulator.
The acquisition of a company by an external management team, which replaces the incumbent management, often financed by a private equity fund.
The acquisition of a company by its existing management team, often financed by a private equity fund and debt.
The entity responsible for the management of an externally managed fund, including investment management, administration and marketing.
The reports and data management provides to the board and senior managers to monitor the business, its risks and its controls.

The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 596/2014), which bans insider dealing, unlawful disclosure of inside information and market manipulation in financial instruments, and requires issuers to disclose inside information promptly.
European Commission proposals of 4 December 2025, not yet law, to integrate EU capital markets.
The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114), which has applied in full since 30 December 2024 and regulates issuers of, and service providers in, crypto-assets that are not financial instruments.

The EU framework for investment services and activities, made up of Directive 2014/65/EU and the directly applicable the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation (MiFIR), which has applied since 3 January 2018.

The EU framework for investment services and activities, made up of Directive 2014/65/EU and the directly applicable the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation (MiFIR), which has applied since 3 January 2018.
The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) No 600/2014), which sits alongside the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (MiFID II).
Staff whose activities have a material impact on a firm's risk profile, to whom stricter remuneration rules apply.
The profit that can be made by including, excluding or reordering transactions in a block, for example by front-running a trade.
A four-digit code assigned to merchants to classify their business.
The entity that sells to the customer and is legally responsible for the transaction, including refunds, chargebacks and often tax.
The total fee an acquirer charges a merchant for accepting card payments, made up of interchange, scheme fees and the acquirer's margin.

acronyms.term: Minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities
acronyms.shortDefinition: The amount of capital and debt that a bank must hold that can absorb losses or be converted to equity in resolution, so that it can be recapitalised without public money.
The native coin of Monero, a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that hides the sender, receiver and amount of transactions by default.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore, Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator.
Money laundering: disguising the criminal origin of money or assets so that they appear legitimate.
The officer responsible for overseeing a firm's day-to-day compliance with anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules.

The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017, the main UK anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) rules for firms.
The person in a firm responsible for receiving internal suspicion reports and deciding whether to report to the Financial Intelligence Unit.
A fund that invests in short-term money market instruments, deposits and reverse repos, aiming to preserve capital and provide daily liquidity with a return in line with short-term interest rates.
The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2017/1131), which has applied to all money market funds (MMFs), whether UCITS or alternative investment funds (AIFs), since 21 January 2019.
The Council of Europe's committee of experts that evaluates its member states' anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing systems against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards.
A side-letter term giving an investor the right to receive any more favourable terms granted to other investors of the same or smaller size.
Logging in with two or more independent types of evidence, such as a password, a code from a device or a biometric.
A cryptographic technique in which several parties each hold a share of a key and sign jointly, without the full key ever existing in one place.
The Financial Stability Board (FSB)'s term for a firm or group that combines a broad range of crypto services, typically around a trading platform.
The Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, a group of countries that monitors and reports on the implementation of UN sanctions on North Korea, including its theft and laundering of crypto-assets.
Belgium's central bank and prudential supervisor of banks, insurers, payment and e-money institutions.

The national regulator in each EEA Member State that authorises and supervises funds and their managers, such as the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI) in Ireland and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) in Luxembourg.
The National Crime Agency, the UK's law enforcement agency against serious and organised crime.

acronyms.term: National Institute of Standards and Technology
acronyms.shortDefinition: The National Institute of Standards and Technology, a US federal agency that sets technical standards, including cryptographic standards such as its post-quantum cryptography standards.
A Member State’s rules allowing AIFs not entitled to the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD) passport, such as non-EEA AIFs, to be marketed to professional investors in that state.
A country's assessment of its money laundering and terrorist financing risks, required by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 1.
The cryptocurrency built into a blockchain's protocol, used to pay transaction fees and, in proof-of-stake networks, staked to secure the network.
The value of a fund’s assets less its liabilities.

acronyms.term: Network for Greening the Financial System
acronyms.shortDefinition: A network of central banks and supervisors that develops climate scenarios and supervisory practice for managing climate-related and environmental risks in the financial system.

acronyms.term: New York State Department of Financial Services
acronyms.shortDefinition: The New York State Department of Financial Services, the state regulator of banks, insurers and financial services in New York.
The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2555), which sets cybersecurity and incident-reporting requirements for essential and important entities across many sectors.
A board member who is not part of the firm's executive management.
Non-fungible token: a unique token recording ownership of a specific item or right.
A UK authorised fund that can be sold to retail investors but has wider investment powers than a UK UCITS, for example to invest more in property or other funds.
The part of HM Treasury that implements and enforces UK financial sanctions.
The Office of Foreign Assets Control, part of the US Treasury.

acronyms.term: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
acronyms.shortDefinition: The US federal agency, part of the Treasury, that charters and supervises national banks and federal savings associations, and licenses federal qualified payment stablecoin issuers under the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act 2025 (GENIUS Act).
A fund’s annual operating costs, such as the management fee and service providers’ fees, expressed as a percentage of its average NAV, excluding transaction costs and performance fees.
A UK investment fund set up as a company with variable capital, so that shares are created and cancelled as investors come and go.
The governance token of Optimism, a layer 2 network that settles to Ethereum.

acronyms.term: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
acronyms.shortDefinition: An international organisation of 38 mostly high-income countries that develops economic and tax policy standards.
Traded bilaterally between two parties rather than on an exchange or other trading venue.
The UK regime, created by the Financial Services Act 2021, that lets overseas funds be recognised for marketing to UK retail investors if their home country is found equivalent.

acronyms.term: Packaged retail and insurance-based investment product
acronyms.shortDefinition: An investment whose return depends on the performance of underlying assets and that is packaged for retail investors, including UCITS and alternative investment funds (AIFs), structured products and unit-linked insurance.

acronyms.term: Packaged retail and insurance-based investment products
acronyms.shortDefinition: Investment products whose return depends on market values or reference assets, such as funds, structured products and unit-linked insurance.
A voluntary, portable personal pension product created by Regulation (EU) 2019/1238, which can be offered across the EU by authorised providers under a single set of rules.
A US tax classification for most non-US funds.
Gold-backed tokens: Paxos Gold (PAXG) and Tether Gold (XAUT) each represent ownership of a set amount of physical gold held in custody.
Gold-backed tokens: Paxos Gold (PAXG) and Tether Gold (XAUT) each represent ownership of a set amount of physical gold held in custody.
A firm that onboards smaller merchants under its own acquiring relationship and processes card payments for them, simplifying acceptance.

A firm that, with the customer's consent, initiates a payment directly from the customer's payment account held at another provider, for example to let a customer pay an online merchant straight from their bank account.
A firm authorised to provide payment services, such as money remittance, payment accounts, card acquiring, payment initiation or account information services, without being a bank.
Any firm that provides payment services, including banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and post office giro institutions.
A person making use of a payment service, as payer, payee or both.
The EU regulation that will sit alongside the Third Payment Services Directive (PSD3) and apply directly in all member states.
The UK legislation that implemented the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and still governs UK payment institutions and payment services, supervised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
The UK economic regulator of payment systems, such as Faster Payments and Bacs.
A US dollar stablecoin issued by Paxos for PayPal, backed by cash and short-dated US government securities and redeemable at par.
Directly between users, without an intermediary.
The minimum level of own funds a regulated firm must hold at all times, set by the activities it carries on.
A derivative with no expiry date, kept close to the spot price by periodic funding payments between longs and shorts.
Under the Market Abuse Regulation, a director or senior executive of an issuer who has regular access to inside information and power to take managerial decisions.
Trading in financial instruments or crypto-assets by staff for their own account.
A politically exposed person: someone who holds or has held a prominent public function, such as a minister, senior judge or head of a state-owned company.
Cryptographic algorithms designed to resist attack by quantum computers.

In Ireland, a senior role, such as director of a fund or fund management company (FMC) or designated person, that may be filled only with the Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)’s prior approval under the fitness and probity regime.

acronyms.term: Prestataire de services sur actifs numériques
acronyms.shortDefinition: The French national registration and optional licensing regime for digital asset service providers that applied before the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

The three-page pre-contractual document that manufacturers of packaged retail and insurance-based investment products must give EU retail investors under the PRIIPs Regulation, showing the product's objectives, risk indicator, performance scenarios and costs.
The most significant negative effects of investment decisions on sustainability factors, such as greenhouse gas emissions.

The international standards for payment systems, central securities depositories, securities settlement systems, central counterparties and trade repositories, issued by the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI) and the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) in 2012.

The Central Bank of Ireland (CBI)’s risk-based supervisory framework, which assigns firms an impact rating that determines the intensity of supervision and, for fund management companies (FMCs), stricter director location rules for higher-impact firms.
The UK Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, which sets out the main UK money laundering offences, the duty to report suspicious activity and the offence of tipping off.
Proliferation financing: providing funds or financial services for the development of nuclear, chemical or biological weapons and their delivery systems.
A consensus mechanism in which validators lock up (stake) coins for the right to propose and attest to blocks, and can lose them for misbehaving.
A consensus mechanism in which miners compete to solve computational puzzles to add blocks.
A UK open-ended fund investing mainly in property, with a tax regime under which the fund pays no tax on property income and investors are taxed as if they held property directly.
Separating the role of building blocks from proposing them, so specialist builders compete to assemble the most valuable block and validators simply choose the highest bid.
A company whose assets and liabilities are divided into legally segregated cells, so that the liabilities of one cell cannot be met from the assets of another.
Liquidity held by a protocol's own treasury rather than rented from liquidity providers with incentives.
The Prudential Regulation Authority, part of the Bank of England.
The independent regulator of firms authorised in the Qatar Financial Centre, which has issued rules on digital assets and tokenisation.
A UK authorised fund that can only be sold to professional and sophisticated investors, with wider investment and borrowing powers than retail funds.
An Irish alternative investment fund (AIF) reserved for qualifying investors subscribing at least €100,000.
The former name of the Irish qualifying investor AIF (QIAIF), a fund reserved for professional and qualifying investors.
acronyms.notes: former name of the Irish QIAIF

acronyms.shortDefinition: Questions and answers published by a regulator to explain how it applies its rules.
A listed company or fund that invests mainly in income-producing property and qualifies for special tax treatment if it meets conditions on its assets, sources of profit and distribution of income.
A payment system in which high-value payments are settled individually and immediately in central bank money, rather than netted at the end of the day.
A traditional asset, such as a bond, fund, property or commodity, represented by a token.
A regulated service of receiving a client's order to buy or sell an instrument or crypto-asset and passing it to another firm for execution.
The minimum period for which an investor is advised to hold an investment to have a reasonable prospect of achieving its objective.
A liquidity stress testing measure comparing the amount of assets a fund can sell within a period with the redemptions it could face in the same period.
A central register of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies, trusts or other legal entities.
A firm that provides only account information services and is registered rather than fully authorised, needing professional indemnity insurance instead of capital.

Detailed technical rules drafted by an ESA and adopted by the Commission as delegated regulations, for example on liquidity management tools (LMTs), loan origination, European long-term investment funds (ELTIFs) and the SFDR templates.
A remote procedure call: a request from one computer to run a function on another.
A transaction in which a fund sells securities and agrees to buy them back at a set price on a future date, in effect borrowing cash against the securities.
A request for quote: a trading method in which a buyer asks one or more dealers for a price before trading.
A messaging service that lets a payee send a payment request, which the payer can approve, decline or reschedule, triggering a payment such as an instant credit transfer.
India's central bank and banking regulator.

A Luxembourg AIF reserved for well-informed investors that does not require the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval but must be managed by an authorised EEA alternative investment fund manager (AIFM).

An EU legislative package, politically agreed on 18 December 2025 but not yet applicable, that would strengthen value for money (VfM) requirements, revise the inducement rules and amend the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID).
An Irish AIF that may be sold to retail investors.
A US dollar stablecoin issued by Ripple, backed by cash and short-dated US government securities.
A process in which business areas identify their risks, assess how well controls work and plan improvements, usually challenged by the risk function.
The written statement, approved by the board, of the types and amounts of risk the firm is willing to take to achieve its objectives, combining qualitative statements with measurable limits.

Applying anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) measures in proportion to the risks identified: more resources and enhanced measures where risks are higher, and simplified measures where they are lower.
Rollup-as-a-service: providers that let projects launch their own rollup networks using ready-made software and infrastructure.
The UK law that gives the government power to make sanctions regulations and to amend money laundering rules.
Saudi Arabia's central bank, still known by its former acronym SAMA.
The EU's strategy, launched in 2025 to succeed the Capital Markets Union, to channel more of Europeans' savings into productive investment and to integrate EU capital markets and their supervision.
A type of zero-knowledge proof that needs no trusted setup and is considered resistant to quantum attacks, at the cost of larger proofs.

acronyms.term: SCS (société en commandite simple) and SCSp (société en commandite spéciale)
acronyms.shortDefinition: The Luxembourg limited partnership vehicles used for AIFs.
The EU directive (Directive (EU) 2015/2366), the EU's main law on payment services.
The Secured Overnight Financing Rate, the US dollar risk-free reference rate based on overnight repo transactions backed by US Treasuries.

acronyms.term: Securities and Exchange Board of India
acronyms.shortDefinition: India's securities markets regulator, which oversees exchanges, intermediaries, mutual funds, alternative investment funds and foreign portfolio investors.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission, the federal regulator of securities markets, investment advisers and investment companies.
Hong Kong's securities and futures regulator.
A transaction in which securities are used to borrow cash or other securities, such as securities lending, repo and reverse repo transactions.

The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2015/2365), which requires securities lending, repo and similar transactions to be reported to a trade repository (for funds, by the management company (ManCo) or alternative investment fund manager (AIFM)), their use to be disclosed in the prospectus and periodic reports, and collateral to be re-used only with prior consent.
A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate management company (ManCo) and is itself authorised and regulated as a ManCo.
The element of the Irish the Individual Accountability Framework (IAF) that requires firms to map responsibilities to senior individuals.
An independent non-executive director appointed to act as a sounding board for the chair, lead the chair's appraisal and serve as an intermediary for other directors and shareholders when needed.

Under the UK Senior Managers and Certification Regime, a role designated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) or the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), such as chief executive or chair, that requires regulatory approval before appointment and carries a statement of responsibilities.
The UK regime that makes senior individuals at financial firms personally accountable.
The UK regime that makes senior individuals at financial firms personally accountable.
The standard euro credit transfer scheme across the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), settling within one business day.
The European scheme for euro credit transfers that reach the payee within ten seconds, at any time of day, every day.
A bespoke arrangement, usually for an institutional investor, under which a manager manages assets for that investor alone rather than pooling them in a fund.
The EU directive (Directive 98/26/EC), which protects transfer orders and collateral in designated payment and securities settlement systems from being unwound if a participant becomes insolvent.

The EU directive that requires asset managers investing in shares traded on EEA regulated markets to publish an engagement policy on a comply-or-explain basis and report annually on how they have applied it, including how they voted.
A Luxembourg corporate fund with fixed capital.

acronyms.term: SICAR (société d’investissement en capital à risque)
acronyms.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg vehicle for investment in risk capital, such as private equity and venture capital, reserved for well-informed investors and requiring the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval.
The main Luxembourg corporate fund, whose capital always equals its net assets.
Reduced customer due diligence measures permitted where the money laundering and terrorist financing risk is demonstrably low.
The area in which euro payments, including credit transfers, direct debits and instant transfers, can be made across borders as easily as domestic payments, using common standards.
The EU agency that plans and carries out the resolution of significant banks in the banking union when they fail or are likely to fail, so that they can be wound down without taxpayer bail-outs.
The EU's system of banking supervision for the euro area and other participating countries, made up of the European Central Bank (ECB) and the national supervisors.
Dollar stablecoins issued by the Sky protocol (formerly MakerDAO).
Dollar stablecoins issued by the Sky protocol (formerly MakerDAO).
An e-money institution below set thresholds for outstanding e-money, which may operate under a lighter national regime without an EU passport.

A payment institution whose monthly payment transactions are below a threshold set by its home member state, which may be registered rather than fully authorised, with lighter requirements but no EU passport.

acronyms.term: Sociedad gestora de instituciones de inversión colectiva
acronyms.shortDefinition: A Spanish management company authorised to manage collective investment schemes, supervised by the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV).
An Italian asset management company authorised to manage collective investment schemes, including UCITS and alternative investment funds (AIFs).
A Luxembourg special limited partnership.
The native token of Solana, a high-throughput proof-of-stake blockchain.
The origin of the particular money or assets used in a business relationship or transaction, such as a salary, a property sale or an inheritance.
The origin of a customer's total wealth, such as business ownership, employment or inheritance.
A legal entity set up for a specific, limited purpose, such as holding an investment or originating loans, often used by alternative investment funds (AIFs) to structure investments.

A Luxembourg alternative investment fund (AIF) reserved for well-informed investors, with no restriction on eligible assets but subject to risk-spreading, which requires prior the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) approval.
A document setting out the responsibilities of a senior manager, submitted to the regulator under the UK Senior Managers Regime and Ireland's Senior Executive Accountability Regime.
A statutory instrument: UK secondary legislation made by ministers under powers in an Act of Parliament.
The Sterling Overnight Index Average, the risk-free reference rate for sterling, based on overnight unsecured lending.
The automated passing of orders, prices and settlement instructions between systems without manual re-keying, which reduces errors and costs.

The requirement under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) (and in future the PSR) that payment service providers verify a customer's identity using at least two independent elements: something they know (such as a password), something they have (such as a phone) and something they are (such as a fingerprint).
A type of zero-knowledge proof that is short and quick to verify.

The risk measure in the packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs) Key Information Document (KID) that ranks a product on a scale from 1 (lower risk) to 7 (higher risk), combining market risk and credit risk.
The process by which EU supervisors assess a firm's business model, governance, risks and capital and liquidity adequacy, and may set additional requirements.

A report to the Financial Intelligence Unit where a firm knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing (the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 20).

A report to the Financial Intelligence Unit where a firm knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing (the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 20).
A report that firms arranging or executing transactions must submit to their regulator when they reasonably suspect an order or transaction may constitute market abuse.
The UK regime for sustainability-related claims and product labels for investment funds and other products.

The EU regulation (Regulation (EU) 2019/2088), applying since 10 March 2021, which requires financial market participants, including UCITS management companies (ManCos) and alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs), to disclose how they integrate sustainability risks and consider principal adverse impactses (PAIs), at entity and product level.
The cooperative that runs the main global messaging network that banks use to send payment and securities instructions to each other.
Switzerland's integrated financial regulator.
System and Organization Controls 2: an independent assurance report on a service provider's controls over security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy.
The Eurosystem's service for settling instant payments in euro, 24 hours a day, in central bank money.
The Eurosystem's platform for settling securities transactions in central bank money across European markets, used by central securities depositories.
Freezing designated persons' funds and making nothing available to them, without delay and with no risk-based discretion (the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) R.6 and R.7).

acronyms.term: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
acronyms.shortDefinition: An industry task force set up by the Financial Stability Board that in 2017 published recommendations for climate disclosures covering governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.
A UK regime that has allowed EEA funds already marketed in the UK before Brexit to continue to be marketed while they move to recognition under the Overseas Funds Regime.
A regime that lets firms already carrying on an activity continue for a limited time while they apply for authorisation under a new regime.
A US dollar stablecoin issued by Tether, the largest stablecoin by market value.
The trade body for UK investment managers.
The directive that will replace the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the E-Money Directive.
In open banking, an account information or payment initiation service provider that accesses a customer's payment account held by another provider.
Advanced security testing that imitates the tactics of real attackers against a firm's live production systems, based on threat intelligence.
A cryptographic method in which a private key is split into shares held by different parties and a set number of them must cooperate to sign a transaction, without the full key ever being assembled.

acronyms.term: Token and Trusted Technology Service Provider Act
acronyms.shortDefinition: Liechtenstein's law on tokens and service providers using trusted technologies such as blockchain.
A measure of a fund’s annual operating costs as a percentage of its average NAV, commonly quoted for exchange traded funds (ETFs).
A derivative in which one party pays the total economic return of an asset, including income and price changes, in exchange for a fixed or floating payment.
The value of assets deposited in a decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol or network.
A Polish investment fund company that creates and manages investment funds, supervised by the Komisja Nadzoru Finansowego (KNF).
Disguising criminal proceeds through trade transactions, for example by over- or under-invoicing goods or invoicing for goods never shipped.
Requirements that staff have the knowledge and skills for their roles, are assessed as competent and keep them up to date through continuing professional development.

The entity, often the fund administrator, that maintains the register of investors and processes subscriptions, redemptions, transfers and switches, including the anti-money laundering (AML) and customer due diligence checks on investors.
The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)'s earlier principle-based approach to fair treatment of customers, largely superseded by the Consumer Duty.
The native token of the Tron blockchain.
Two-factor authentication: logging in with two different types of evidence, such as a password and a code from a phone or hardware key.
The EU directive (Directive 2009/65/EC; the UCITS IV recast, as amended), the EU framework for UCITS.
A collective investment undertaking: a vehicle that pools investors' money and invests it collectively.

acronyms.term: Undertaking for collective investment in transferable securities
acronyms.shortDefinition: An open-ended fund authorised under the UCITS Directive that raises capital from the public, invests in transferable securities and other eligible liquid assets subject to diversification rules, and entrusts its assets to an independent fund depositary.
A US fund that buys a fixed portfolio and holds it until a set termination date, without active management.
A fund constituted under a trust deed between a management company (ManCo) and a trustee (the fund depositary), which is the legal owner of the assets on behalf of the investors (unitholders).
The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
The United Nations.
The United States of America.
Italy's financial intelligence unit, established within the Banca d'Italia, which receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports.
Unspent transaction output: the accounting model used by Bitcoin, in which each transaction consumes earlier outputs and creates new ones.
A tax on goods and services charged at each stage of supply.
A statistical estimate of the maximum loss a portfolio is likely to suffer over a given period at a given confidence level.
The principle that a product’s costs are justified and proportionate to the benefits it delivers to investors.
A corporate fund whose share capital always equals its NAV, rising when investors subscribe and falling when they redeem.
A money market fund whose share price moves with the market value of its assets.
Open banking payments that let a customer authorise a provider to make a series of payments within agreed limits, without approving each one.
A check, before a credit transfer is sent, that the name of the payee given by the payer matches the name on the account.
Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) definition, a digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and used for payment or investment.

Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) definition, a person who, as a business, carries out one or more of five activities for or on behalf of another person - exchange between virtual assets and fiat, exchange between virtual assets, transfer, safekeeping or administration, and services related to an issuer's offer or sale.
Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, which licenses and supervises virtual asset service providers in Dubai, outside the Dubai International Financial Centre.

An account number that routes payments into a master account, often used to collect funds for individual customers or to give a payment firm's customers their own the International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs).
A virtual private network: an encrypted connection that hides a user's location and traffic.
The average length of time to legal maturity of all the assets of a money market fund (MMF), weighted by their relative holdings.
The average length of time to legal maturity or, if shorter, to the next interest rate reset, of all the assets of a money market fund (MMF), weighted by their relative holdings.
A US dollar stablecoin issued by World Liberty Financial and backed by US government securities and cash equivalents.
Wrapped bitcoin: a token on Ethereum backed one-for-one by bitcoin held by a custodian, letting bitcoin be used in Ethereum-based decentralised finance (DeFi).
Wrapped ether: ether converted into an ERC-20 token so that it can be used in smart contracts that expect the ERC-20 standard.
The native token of the XRP Ledger, a blockchain designed for fast, low-cost payments.
